title: Rams plan to replace K Blake Grupe in next day or two
summary: In his first, and only, game with the Rams, kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL while making a tackle during a kick return.
full_text: '' In his first, and only, game with the Rams, kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL while making a tackle during a kick return. Which leaves the Rams without a kicker. For the second straight week. On Monday, coach Sean McVay told reporters that the Rams will be adding a new kicker very soon. "We're in the process," McVay said. "[Assistant General Manager] John McKay, [special-teams coordinator] Bubba [Ventrone], [General Manager] Les Snead, those guys are working on some different options. Certainly, we'll have something here in the next day or two.” McVay was also asked about the 156-pound Grupe's decision to attempt a shoulder-to-shoulder tackle during the return that resulted in his injury. "[H]e did an instinctual thing to try to knock him out of bounds," McVay said. "You'd like us to shoulder leverage the ball up on the front line first so that it doesn't get spit out to him. But maybe you go lower and avoid the knee injury. It was kind of one of those deals that I felt terrible. He does a great job converting on his kick. Then right after that you're like, ‘You got to be shitting me.’ I feel terrible for him. The only thing I'd say is maybe go low instead of taking him on high.” It's a tough situation for any kicker, especially one who is the smallest player on the field. His choice was to try to apply a shoulder hit or basically get trampled. For the Rams, it's a matter of finding the right guy to replace the guy who replaced Harrison Mevis. They're reportedly working out Brandon McManus and Matt Prater on Tuesday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Campbell: Penei Sewell's switch to left tackle has been outstanding
summary: During the offseason, the Lions elected to move three-time first-team AP All-Pro Penei Sewell from right tackle to left tackle.
full_text: During the offseason, the Lions elected to move three-time first-team AP All-Pro Penei Sewell from right tackle to left tackle. So far, head coach Dan Campbell has liked the results. "The switch has been outstanding and yes, I have [seen growth]," Campbell said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. "I still feel an ascending player. I feel like in some regards he looks even more smooth than he did at right. And I never thought he'd looked out of place at right or didn't look smooth. It almost feels like he's found even another little gear here [with] his ability to get out of his stance, and anchor, and punch, and run off the football. "But it's a credit to him. He's banked a lot of reps and honestly, he can go anywhere. I mean, you can put him in the left, you can put him at right. That’s why we move him a little bit. But he's playing high level football right now at left tackle.” Sewell's performance at left tackle is a significant part of why the Lions are tied for the league lead at 32.8 points per game and No. 4 in yards per game at 393.8. At 3-2, the Lions will host the division rival, 4-2 Packers on Sunday afternoon.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Rams WR Davante Adams out 6-10 weeks with ruptured hamstring
summary: DTs Poona Ford and Kobie Turner also will miss significant time, with Ford going on season-ending IR.
full_text: '' Wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals, Rams coach Sean McVay announced Monday. Adams will miss 6 to 10 weeks. He pulled up with a non-contact injury while running a route in the fourth quarter. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns. Unfortunately for the Rams, Adams isn't the only player injured in Sunday's loss. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner (groin) is headed to injured reserve. He will miss 4 to 6 weeks. Kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL) is out for the season, as is defensive tackle Poona Ford (triceps).
author: Charean Williams

title: Bengals sign S Russ Yeast to their active roster
summary: The Bengals filled an open spot on their 53-man roster on Tuesday.
full_text: The Bengals filled an open spot on their 53-man roster on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed safety Russ Yeast off of their practice squad. They opened up the slot by placing tight end Tanner Hudson on injured reserve Monday. Yeast spent last season on the Bengals' practice squad and he has been elevated to play in two games this season. He has four tackles while seeing time on defense and special teams. Yeast also had 82 tackles in 36 games for the Texans, Panthers and Rams earlier in his career. The Bengals announced that they have signed tight end Josh Kattus and linebacker Emany Johnson to the practice squad. They also released safety Isaiah Nwokobia from that roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni: Sean Mannion will remain the play caller
summary: The Eagles rank 30th in total offense, including 29th in rushing.
full_text: The Eagles rank 30th in total offense, including 29th in rushing. They have not had running back Saquon Barkley since Week 4; right tackle Lane Johnson retired unexpectedly on Oct. 6; and the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars will be the final game of the season for quarterback Jalen Hurts. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion doesn't have much to work with, but head coach Nick Sirianni still faced questions about Mannion on Monday. Sirianni replied, "Yes," when asked directly whether Mannion would continue to call plays. Sirianni acknowledged the offense has to be better, and he and the coaches will spend the next few days trying to fix it. "Everything's on the table," Sirianni said, adding that the play caller and coaches aren't changing. With Tanner McKee at quarterback, the Eagles gained 222 yards in the loss to the Panthers on Sunday. McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: What's next for Dan Quinn?
summary: At the end of the first half of Monday night's game, with the Commanders down 20-3 and coach Dan Quinn going viral based on a lip-reading clip that was being widely interpreted as him not realizing it was fourth down (after a failed fourth-down play), it looked like Quinn was on track to get fired after the game.
full_text: At the end of the first half of Monday night's game, with the Commanders down 20-3 and coach Dan Quinn going viral based on a lip-reading clip that was being widely interpreted as him not realizing it was fourth down (after a failed fourth-down play), it looked like Quinn was on track to get fired after the game. Then came the second half, and an effort by the Commanders that made the final score (23-17) far more respectable. So now owner Josh Harris has a decision to make. One week removed from the humiliating clock debacle and entering the bye week, will Harris make a change? Even with the six-point margin, the Commanders remain 1-4-1. Working in Quinn's favor is the fact that the division is still there to be had, if they can turn it around. The other consideration is that the bump from making an interim hire could also give the team the kind of wakeup call that could carry them to an NFC East title. (At that point, however, it would be difficult to not reward the interim coach by giving him the permanent job.) There's a mini-bye looming, between the Week 10 Thursday night game against the Giants and the Week 11 Monday night game against the Bengals. Maybe Harris will decide to kick the can, giving the Commanders three more games (Eagles, Rams, at Giants) before making a final decision.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Quinn's fourth-down explanation exposes a different failure of attention to detail
summary: After Monday night's game, Commanders coach Dan Quinn took his time in showing up to talk to reporters.
full_text: After Monday night's game, Commanders coach Dan Quinn took his time in showing up to talk to reporters. He arrived nearly an hour after the game ended — and after quarterback Jayden Daniels met with reporters (which is very unusual, for any team). Quinn knew all about the viral moment in which he seemed to be surprised after a failed fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13 in the second quarter. It looked like he didn't know it was fourth down. At the press conference, Quinn had an explanation. " I definitely knew it was fourth down ," Quinn said, before slipping into a word salad that was largely confusing and pivoted to him explaining that they planned to go for it on fourth down throughout the game because they expected it to be a higher-scoring contest. Even though Quinn's body language suggested that he was surprised to find out it had been fourth down, we'll give him the benefit of the doubt. He knew it was fourth down. But the operation for which he's responsible didn't know, once the penatly flag landed on the field (in plain view of quarterback Jayden Daniels) that it wasn't a situation in which failure to reach the line to gain would make it fourth and seven with a chance to kick a field goal. When the play isn't shut down by a pre-snap foul, a penalty on the offense can be declined by the defense. After the play, there should have been no confusion — from anyone — as to what had happened. The 49ers would decline the penalty, and the 49ers would take possession. Because it had been fourth down. While some will believe (as I do) that Quinn (and his quarterback) didn't know it was fourth down, the explanation doesn't exonerate the lack of attention to detail. Instead, it changes the conversation from "did you know it was fourth down?" to "why didn't you realize you still had to gain at least two yards to retain possession?" It speaks to the overall culture under Quinn. The mastery, or lack thereof, of situational football. Quinn will get another chance to explain himself today, when he conducts his day-after press conference (unless he's fired before then). With the Commanders entering their annual bye, both Daniels and offensive coordinator David Blough won't be available to reporters until next week. If/when there's ever an admission that a mistake was made, we know what the drill will be : "It’s my responsibility. I take accountability. It won’t happen again." How many lessons will Quinn, Daniels, and Blough get to learn on the fly? Teams don't hire head coaches with the idea that there will be multiple years of on-the-job training when it comes to the nuances of the game. Quinn has been coaching in the NFL continuously since 2001, with the exception of a two-year stint at Florida in 2011 and 2012. He served as the Falcons' head coach for six years, and it's his third year with the Commanders. In hiring Quinn, the Commanders weren't rolling the dice on a newbie. They were hiring a fully-formed football coach who presumably knows how the game works, in all respects. The last two games have proven otherwise. And it further complicates the decision that owner Josh Harris, who is still a new, inexperienced owner, will be making as to whether to make an in-season change.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Jacobs to get full week of practice, game status to be determined
summary: The Packers won't have defensive end Micah Parsons back at practice this week, but they will have running back Josh Jacobs on the field as they prepare to face the Lions.
full_text: ' The Packers won’t have defensive end Micah Parsons back at practice this week, but they will have running back Josh Jacobs on the field as they prepare to face the Lions. Jacobs was removed from the Commissioner Exempt list on Monday and head coach Matt LaFleur said that he will get a full week of practice in his return to active duty. LaFleur said that Jacobs's status for the game against the Lions is "to be determined" by how things go in practice. That's also the case with how much he'll play if he is active. "We feel like he’s in a pretty good spot," LaFleur said at his press conference. "He’s been training, but he’s missed the exposure to football." LaFleur said Jacobs has been "engaged" with the team during his time on paid leave by attending meetings and doing conditioning work, which gives LaFleur hope that he can provide "a spark" to the league's least-productive ground attack. "I think he’s an elite-level back," LaFleur said. "He’s certainly not going to hurt it." Jacobs ran for 2,258 yards and 29 touchdowns over his first two seasons in Green Bay and the Packers would welcome that kind of jolt to their offense as soon as possible.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brock Purdy is the NFL's all-time record holder for highest career passer rating
summary: The NFL has a new all-time record holder for highest career passer rating: Brock Purdy.
full_text: The NFL has a new all-time record holder for highest career passer rating: Brock Purdy. As of Monday night, Purdy has the highest passer rating in NFL history, at 105.6. To qualify for the official career record, a player needs to have thrown at least 1,500 passes in his NFL career, and on Monday night Purdy topped the 1,500-attempt mark, giving him the passer rating record. In all, Purdy has completed 1,038 of 1,524 passes for 13,145 yards, with 98 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. The record previously belonged to Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has a career passer rating of 102.7. He's followed by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers at 101.8, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow at 101.3 and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes at 100.8. Purdy will probably keep the record for a while, as he's far enough ahead of the pack that no one would surpass him unless he has a disastrous end to the season while one of those quarterbacks behind him puts up record-setting numbers. There are also no other quarterbacks who are close to 1,500 pass attempts whose passer rating could surpass Purdy. Passer rating is determined by a complex formula that combines completion percentage, yards per pass, touchdown percentage and interception percentage. The NFL adopted it as the league's official statistic for ranking passers in 1973. It's far from a perfect method of ranking quarterbacks — it ignores first downs, sacks, fumbles, rushing and other measurements of a player's quality — but as a rough gauge of how well a quarterback is playing, it's not bad. And it ranks Purdy ahead of every quarterback, ever.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Malik Mustapha avoids another flag for hit on defenseless player, but a second fine is likely
summary: For the second straight game, 49ers safety Malik Mustapha has avoided a flag for an illegal hit on a defenseless receiver.
full_text: For the second straight game, 49ers safety Malik Mustapha has avoided a flag for an illegal hit on a defenseless receiver. For the second straight week, Mustapha likely will be fined. Against the Seahawks, Mustapha applied a helmet-to-helmet hit on Seattle receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba during the Seahawks' final drive of the game. If caught by the officials, Seattle would have had a first down on the San Francisco 35, down three points with 1:09 to play. Mustapha was fined $6,998 by the league office. On the opening Commanders drive during Monday night's game in Santa Clara, Mustapha applied an illegal helmet-to-helmet hit on Washington receiver Stefon Diggs. It was not flagged. As explained on the main ESPN broadcast, it should have been. And it likely will draw another fine. If/when fined again, Mustapha will be one more illegal hit away from an automatic suspension, under the new NFL-NFL Players Association approach to five specific safety violations. And, technically, Mustapha is already in line for a suspension. With the second violation coming so early in the Week 6 game, another one during the game against the Commanders will be No. 3.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh: We're "honing in" on who will start at QB in Week 7
summary: The Giants' HC said the team is working through who will start at QB after J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston late in Sunday's game and played well.
full_text: Who will be behind center when the Giants take on the Texans in Week 7? While Jameis Winston has started since Jaxson Dart went down with a knee injury, that could change after J.J. McCarthy's impressive fourth quarter in Sunday's loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh did not directly say who would start one way or another. That kind of answer from a coach on a Monday can often signal change is coming later in the week. “ We’re working through that now — honing in on a decision,” Harbaugh said on Monday, via SNY, when asked directly if the team would stick with Winston for the upcoming week. What’s going into those discussions? “Well I would probably say like absolutely every other personnel decision we make, what gives us the best chance to win the football game at this given time or what combination of players, schemes, and things like that, give us the best chance, in this case, to in this case move the ball, score points, protect the football, etc.,” Harbaugh said. “All the things that help us win. Whatever it is that furthers us and helps us, just to use the basic obvious point, that’s what we want to do.” Winston has appeared in five games with four starts since Dart went down during the Week 2 loss to the Rams. He’s completed 57.0 percent of his passes for 957 yards with seven touchdowns and five interceptions. He was 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two picks before McCarthy replaced him on Sunday. McCarthy completed 11-of-21 passes for 243 yards with a touchdown and a pick on Sunday, leading the Giants to three scoring drives in the fourth quarter.
author: Myles Simmons

title: The goal of team doctors shouldn't be to help players "be available"
summary: Doctors need to treat players as patients, regardless of whether that means they won't be able to play.
full_text: Given the ongoing developments in the Jalen Hurts situation, reporters covering the team understandably have questions. Given that only Eagles coach Nick Sirianni was available to talk to reporters on Monday, he understandably was the person to be asked those questions. As his comments during Monday's press conference demonstrated, Sirianni wasn't fully committed to providing the kind of transparency and details that the reporters were hoping for. But Sirianni made one comment, in passing, that highlights the deeper problem that still lingers within NFL organizations, years after the league was forced by Congress to take head trauma seriously by involving unaffiliated physicians to decide when a player should be allowed to play after suffering a concussion. Too many teams, and the doctors they employ, view the job not as treating the players as patients but as the vehicle for checking the boxes needed to allow a player to play. Here's what Sirianni said, when asked to identify the persons who were part of the conversations surrounding the medical decisions made after a blood clot was discovered in Hurts's leg: "I think I'll put it this way, the same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them." (Emphasis added.) The doctors shouldn't be there to help players "be available." They should be there to provide medical care to players who, when they have a health issue, become patients. Without an unaffiliated doctor involved in the process, the objective easily can shift from taking the best care of the patient to best enhancing the ability of the player to play. That's why the Hurts case should be the starting point for a comprehensive examination of the entire system of providing medical care to NFL players. With the player wanting to be able to play and the team wanting the player to be able to play, a doctor who is perceived as saying too often "this player shouldn't be available to play" risks being replaced by a doctor who understands the unspoken (usually) goal of ensuring that as many players as possible will "be available" to play in every game. As the Eagles continue to stumble their way through the aftermath of an incident that features a growing list of head-scratching decisions, the only way to make sense of it is to view the entire exercise as an effort not to provide Jalen Hurts with the best possible medical care but to allow the player and the team to achieve the shared objective of ensuring that he would "be available" to play. With Hurts, the immediate reaction to the discovery of the blood clot seemed to be about doing whatever needed to be done to allow him to play. Even if it meant advising him not to sleep as a precaution. That one inexplicable wrinkle has led to even more confusion, with Tom Pelissero of Netflix tweaking his report that Hurts was told not to sleep and didn’t to Hurts actually sleeping , at least a little bit, at the stadium before the game. All evidence that has been made available to the public creates the impression not that the Hurts blood clot was viewed as a medical emergency for the patient but as an availability emergency for the player and the team. "What do we need to do to make sure he'll be available?" shouldn't be the question. It should be, "What do we need to do to take care of this player?," with his availability being a secondary concern, at most. Consider the still-unanswered question of why Hurts was allowed to fly across the Atlantic Ocean despite having a diagnosed blood clot in his leg, less than three days after flying across the Atlantic Ocean with an undiagnosed blood clot in his leg. It seems that the concern wasn't ensuring that Jalen Hurts would be at no enhanced risk of further issues, but of keeping the door open to Jalen Hurts being able to play on Sunday against the Panthers, and beyond. It's an important issue that shouldn't be glossed over simply because Hurts avoided the worst possible outcome of a pulmonary embolism. The league and its teams should view the matter as a wakeup call regarding the still-lingering culture of using doctors not as resources for patient care but as tools for player availability.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after incident at team's facility
summary: The Titans announced the release of defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday.
full_text: '' The Titans announced the release of defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday. Elliott played in the first five games of the season, but was inactive last Sunday after missing practice last Friday for what the team called personal reasons. The exact nature of those reasons is not known, but the team's announcement of Elliott's release suggests they are related to the decision to part ways with him. The Titans say that there was an incident involving Elliott at their facility on October 15 and that they made the decision to release him after an internal review of what happened. The team also says they will not have any further comment on the matter. Elliott signed a two-year deal with the team as a free agent this offseason. He had 11 tackles for Tennessee and has also played for the 49ers and Browns.
author: Josh Alper

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended for one game
summary: The Bills have their bye in Week 7, but when they come back, they will not have one of their key defenders.
full_text: ' The Bills have their bye in Week 7, but when they come back, they will not have one of their key defenders. The NFL announced on Monday that safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game for spitting at an opponent during Sunday’s win over the Raiders. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the contest. The league notes Gardner-Johnson was suspended for unsportsmanlike conduct, with his actions violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” Gardner-Johnson is in his first season with the Bills. He has registered 26 total tackles with two passes defensed and one interception so far this season. Bills head coach Joe Brady called Gardner-Johnson’s actions “uncalled for” in his postgame press conference. “It can’t happen,” Brady said. “It’s going to be addressed. The team is way more important.” Buffalo will host Baltimore in Week 8. While Gardner-Johnson may appeal his suspension, he’s currently eligible to return for the Bills’ Week 9 road matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Giants release Jihad Ward
summary: Linebacker Jihad Ward's second stint with the Giants has come to a quick end.
full_text: Linebacker Jihad Ward's second stint with the Giants has come to a quick end. According to multiple reports, the Giants have released Ward on Tuesday morning. Ward was signed off of the Vikings' practice squad in late September. Ward played 41 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps in his two appearances with the team. He was credited with one tackle. Ward also played in 34 games for the Giants during the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He moved on to the Vikings in 2024 and played for the Titans in 2025 before returning to Minnesota at the start of this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Alec Pierce not ready to return to practice this week
summary: While Colts receiver Alec Pierce is eligible to return to the field this week, he still needs more time before he's ready to practice.
full_text: While Colts receiver Alec Pierce is eligible to return to the field this week, he still needs more time before he's ready to practice. Head coach Shane Steichen said in his Monday news conference that Pierce, who is on injured reserve, will not practice this week as he’s still in the rehab process. Pierce aggravated the heel injury he had surgically repaired in the offseason during Indianapolis’ Week 2 loss to Kansas City. The NFL’s leader in yards per reception in each of the past two seasons, Pierce had five catches for 72 yards before he was sidelined.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Stefon Diggs: It's still wide open for us
summary: The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after the game.
full_text: The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after the game. Diggs's third quarter touchdown catch was part of a 14-point run that pared down a 20-point 49ers lead and gave the Commanders a chance to move ahead late in the fourth quarter. A long drive ended on fourth down in the red zone and the 49ers moved to 6-0 with a 23-17 lead, but Diggs said that the effort the Commanders showed and the fact that the 49ers are an outlier when it comes to their record are reasons to hold onto hope heading into their bye week. "It’s still wide open ," Diggs said, via Marshall Kramsky of WUSA. "Where we are and where the league is, it’s kinda interesting. A weird spot right now. Nobody’s kinda made it clear — that team we just played is a helluva football team. That’s one of those guys that’s gonna be in the running. . . . We played a decent game, we could’ve played a lot better. We were still in it, just like all these games we’ve been in the past couple weeks. We’ve been in it, we just gotta find a way to pull ‘em out." Diggs isn't wrong about things being open in the NFC East. No team in the division has won a game since Week 4 and two of the other three teams in the division have lost their starting quarterbacks for the season, so the prospect of someone running away with things feels remote. That said, the Commanders have consistently fallen short in the biggest moments of games and that provides little reason to think they're going to suddenly go on a run of their own. The door is open for Diggs and company to prove otherwise, however, and that's about all you can ask for after winning once in six weeks.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dan Quinn on viral clip: "I definitely knew it was fourth down"
summary: The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13.
full_text: The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13. After the pass to the end zone landed incomplete and the Commanders were called for an illegal shift, ESPN's cameras caught Commanders coach Dan Quinn seemingly surprised to learn it was fourth down. When he met with reporters nearly an hour after the game ended, Quinn was ready for the question regarding the viral lip-reading moment. "I definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn said. "We were going for it, and I was — I think what you're referring to, I was probably saying, like, with the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it doesn't go, like, it's the turn on downs. Like, I think somebody asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?' So, now we were going for it. We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was gonna be a 17-14 game. I probably thought it was gonna need 28, 30 to score, you know, to go win it. And so it was by design that we were gonna go, but I knew what happened. I think, I probably was just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me, after an illegal shift, like it was turnover on downs, and [quarterback] Jayden [Daniels] saw the foul, too. He also came out and saw the penalty." You can watch the clip and come to your own conclusion. Again, he seemed to be surprised, not stating a fact. And he clearly had his story ready when he arrived for his press conference — along with plenty of time after the game to craft it. Obviously, after what happened last week, Quinn couldn't afford to admit he didn't know it was fourth down. Even if he didn't know it was fourth down.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan: Eddy Pineiro has got to make his extra points
summary: 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Monday night.
full_text: ' 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Monday night. Coach Kyle Shanahan was not happy about it. Pineiro has been one of the worst kickers in the NFL this season, missing three extra points and three field goals, and Shanahan said after Monday night's win over the Commanders that it can't go on this way. "Yeah, he's got to make them," Shanahan said. "He missed another one today. Fortunately it didn't get us, but I think everyone knows the answer to that, you've got to make your extra points." Pineiro has a long history of not making his extra points: Over the last five seasons, he has missed 14 extra point attempts, the most of any kicker in the NFL, and among the 30 kickers who have attempted at least 75 extra points over the last five years, Pineiro has the lowest percentage of made kicks. If Pineiro keeps missing his job may not be safe.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jed York's suspension ends today
summary: York returns after a six-game ban and $500,000 fine.
full_text: The 49ers have played their sixth game of the season. That means owner Jed York has served his full suspension. As the league explained when announcing the ban earlier this month, York may return on October 20 . York self-suspended for three games, and he got credit for those games when the league added three more. He also was fined $500,000. Whether that means he'll return to games immediately remains to be seen. The 49ers face the Falcons in Atlanta on Sunday before entering the annual bye. The quarterly ownership meeting is set for New York on Tuesday and Wednesday. He's now free to attend, if he chooses. There's still a basic and fundamental disconnect between owner and player suspensions when it comes to the financial realities of the punishment. Players, when suspended, lose all of their compensation and potentially have to repay money already received. Owners pay a fine that pales in comparison to the money they make. Case in point: York lost $500,000 for his six-game suspension. For a one-game suspension due to sucker punching Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb, Rams tackle Alaric Jackson lost $934,555. And Bears defensive end Montez Sweat loses $2.18 million for his two-game suspension under the PED policy. While the violations aren't apples-to-apples (York's suspension arose from an effort to harvest an apple from a poisonous tree at a trailer park), the numbers are the numbers. One game for Jackson equals $934,555. Two games for Sweat equals $2.18 million. Six games for York equals $500,000. It's an obvious issue that few discuss. Which means there's no chance of the approach ever changing.
author: Mike Florio

title: U2 to perform at halftime on Thanksgiving Eve
summary: U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year.
full_text: U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year. Netflix announced on Tuesday that the band will perform at halftime of the NFL's first ever Thanksgiving Eve game on November 25. The game will be at SoFi Stadium with the Rams hosting the Packers. “There's a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: they don't just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement. "We’re thrilled that they'll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. It’s going to be an unforgettable night for football fans and Netflix members worldwide.” Netflix has carried Christmas games the last two seasons and halftime shows for those contests have featured artists like Beyonce and Snoop Dogg, so they may have more to announce ahead of the two games they'll be broadcasting on the holiday this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Shane Steichen on Chris Ballard's firing: "I don't think it falls completely on Chris"
summary: In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M.
full_text: In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M. Chris Ballard on clear notice. On Monday, she fired Ballard. Steichen, who possibly remains in place only because there's no viable interim replacement on his staff (and because the Jeff Saturday experiment has already been attempted), addressed the dismissal of Ballard with reporters on Monday. “ It’s the shitty part of the business ," Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN. "I don’t think it falls completely on Chris. I’m the head football coach. It takes all of us. Coaches, scouts, everybody.” He's right, and Irsay-Gordon could be firing everybody, in time. For now, Ballard was the easiest person to replace in response to a devastating home loss to the previously winless Titans. Barring a turnaround from 2-4 to a playoff appearance, Ballard will soon have company in the category of former employees of the team. And while the absence of a clear choice to serve as interim coach may have saved Steichen for now, it's hardly a guarantee that he'll be in the job when the season ends.

author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh on RB timeshare: Someone has to "do something" to earn job
summary: Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team.
full_text: Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team. Najee Harris and Devin Singletary had four carries in the game, Tyrone Tracy had six and Cam Skattebo didn't touch the ball at all after leading the team in carries through the first five weeks of the season. Harris said, via Greg Johnson of the Trentonian , that it is " hard to get into a rhythm " while constantly going in and out of the game and those comments were brought up to head coach John Harbaugh during Monday's press conference. Harbaugh said he understands that feeling, but said that the opportunity to develop that kind of rhythm is something that has to be earned and no one has done that to this point. "I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance ," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities and you're sure to get more opportunities. Do something." The Giants made the choice to move on from Barkley before Harbaugh was in the organization, but invoking Henry is interesting because he and the Ravens were criticized in Week 16 last season for pulling Henry in favor of Keaton Mitchell at key moments in the second half against the Patriots. New England came back from 11 points down in the fourth quarter for a 28-24 win that helped keep the Ravens out of the playoffs and contributed to Harbaugh being fired at the end of the season. No one would argue that any of the Giants backs are in Henry's class, but history says that the division of labor might not be any more ideal if that was the case.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals' two wins are the two biggest upsets in the NFL this season
summary: The Cardinals are only 2-4, but their two wins have been big ones.
full_text: The Cardinals are only 2-4, but their two wins have been big ones. Specifically, they've been the two biggest upsets in the NFL this season: When the Cardinals beat the Rams on Sunday, they were 12.5-point underdogs. That was the biggest upset of the year, surpassing the Cardinals' Week 1 win over the Chargers, when they were 9.5-point underdogs. There have only been seven games this season when the point spread was more than nine points. Those two games that the Cardinals won as underdogs, and five other games in which the underdogs lost by a combined 72 points. Both of the Cardinals' wins this season have been at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, where they have two wins, the Rams have one and the Chargers have none. Don't bet against the Cardinals, at least not in Los Angeles.

title: Terry McLaurin believed to have season-ending knee injury
summary: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conjure up hopes of a quick return to the field this season.
full_text: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conjure up hopes of a quick return to the field this season. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that the team feared a "significant" injury after the game and that McLaurin would go for tests on Tuesday to determine just how significant it is. Those tests are pending, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the team is bracing to learn that McLaurin will miss the rest of the season. McLaurin missed Week 4 with a hamstring injury and has 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown on the season. McLaurin has two more years left on his contract and is set to have a $34 million cap number in 2027, but there's no guaranteed money left on the deal should the Commanders opt to move in a different direction.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Glenn: Frank Reich is doing a good job as offensive coordinator
summary: The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign.
full_text: ' The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign. Frank Reich was the choice to replace him and the Jets acquired quarterback Geno Smith while making other changes to the unit, but the results have not been much different through six games. They are 27th in points scored, dead last in red zone efficiency and in the bottom portion of the league in a number of other metrics. It hasn't helped Their Week 6 loss to the Patriots turned in part on a pair of failed fourth down conversions that saw the Jets get stopped short on a pair of runs, which is also something that contributed to their loss to the Packers in Week 2. On Monday, Glenn was asked if he's happy with what he's seen from Reich thus far. "I think he's done a good job. I really do," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, there are a number of things that we can improve on, and I think I just told you guys that from short yards to two-minute, but that also goes on me also when it comes to the defensive side, me and [defensive coordinator Brian] Duker on some things that we have to get better at, too. We have to improve on some things and that's what the season is. That's what practice is. After six games, it's hard to just say, 'Okay we're this.' We have to see how this thing plays out, but I would say I think he's done a good job. . . . As we continue to go through this season, I'll continue to see us progress and getter better on the things we have to get better at. To answer your question, I think he's done a good job." Injuries have kept running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell off the field in recent games while first-round pick Omar Cooper just got back on the field after a Week 1 ankle injury. Cooper had a strong game against the Patriots, which was a promising development for what Reich could do with a full hand but more tangible results will have to come one way or another for the Jets to improve on a 2-4 start.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Brady says Bills won't be cutting C.J. Gardner-Johnson after spitting incident
summary: The two players involved in spitting incidents during games were (and still are) star players.
full_text: '' The two players involved in spitting incidents during games were (and still are) star players. After Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was ejected before the first play from scrimmage in Week 1 (which was later treated as a suspension) and Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase was suspended after completing a game in which the spit was missed, there was zero talk about the players being cut. With safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson doing it on Sunday in Las Vegas, the question was asked on Monday whether the Bills will cut him after he missed half of a game after an ejection and all of the next game due to a suspension. "Look, C.J.'s a member of the Buffalo Bills," coach Joe Brady told reporters. "We brought him here for a reason , and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we've got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes." Brady then started to compare Gardner-Johnson's spitting to running back James Cook's fumbling problem. Brady seemed to edit himself in real time. "No different than — it's different, right? — Jimbo fumbling," Brady said. "You know, we have to continue to find ways to get better, and he knows that he has to be better, and, you know, it's just an opportunity for him. Look, it'll be an opportunity for someone else to, you know, play early the week and step up, but it is an opportunity for him to grow and be better as a better teammate and a better football player, you know, when this opportunity comes up again." Like Brady said, the Bills brought Gardner-Johnson to town "for a reason." They wanted his edge and attitude. That comes with the full package of who he is. Sometimes, Gardner-Johnson will cross the line. (And, sometimes, a teammate may get a taste of it.) It's part of the total package. Brady made it clear on Monday that the Bills are willing to tolerate the less savory aspects in the name of getting the dynamic they want on their defense.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay on Kyren Williams: "He was emotional after the game"
summary: After Sunday's loss to the previously 1-4 Cardinals, Rams running back Kyren Williams had a simple explanation for the team's inconsistency on offense.
full_text: After Sunday's loss to the previously 1-4 Cardinals, Rams running back Kyren Williams had a simple explanation for the team's inconsistency on offense. " Probably because I’m not out there ," Williams said in the locker room. On Monday, coach Sean McVay was asked whether he has spoken to Williams about his remarks. “I have," McVay told reporters. "He brought it up to me. I wasn't aware of it. He's such an energy for us. He was emotional after the game. I know this guy's heart. He wants to make sure that he's influencing and effecting positive change. I think what he said it was more of, ‘I just always want to try to be that spark.’ "He was frustrated after the game, but his teammates know what he's about. When he explained it to me, I totally understood where he was coming from. He's a great leader for us. I think the way that it was interpreted was not what his intentions were. I know his teammates and I felt that way. He actually brought that up to me on his own. I was not aware of it until he brought it up to me.” Against the Cardinals, Williams was on the field for 42 snaps, or 72 percent of the total workload. Blake Corum had 16 snaps, or 28 percent. Williams had 10 carries for 50 yards, and Corum had nine for 42. (Williams had three catches for 17 yards, and Corum had two for 18 and a touchdown.) Through six games, Williams's usage rate is at 71 percent, with 110 touches for 610 yards. Corum stands at 27 percent, with 56 touches for 314 yards. The concern, then, doesn't seem to be just playing time. Corum gets the ball more frequently when he plays — 47.45 percent of the time. Williams gets the ball 35.94 percent of the time he's on the field. Either way, Williams said what he said. And, as McVay explained it, Williams raised it with McVay and explained himself.

title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after 'incident' at team facility
summary: The veteran defensive tackle appeared in all five games this season after following head coach Robert Saleh to Tennessee from San Francisco
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans earned their first win of the 2026 season and of the Robert Saleh era this past Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , upsetting their rivals in Indy, 26-20. However, they were forced to release one of their defensive linemen this week after an "incident" at the team facility.
On Tuesday, the team announced that it had released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after reviewing an incident that happened on Thursday. The Titans issued a statement through team reporter Jim Wyatt.
"On Thursday, Oct. 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott.
Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter."
It's unclear what the incident was or if any more information will come out about it.
Elliott has played in all five games this season with one start and has recorded 11 tackles. He followed Saleh over from the San Francisco 49ers , as Elliott spent the past two seasons out in Santa Clara, making 29 starts in 31 games played.
Elliott's surprising release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn't just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach's decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation.
"We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward," Saleh told reporters on Monday.
The Titans return home this week to host the 4-2 Cleveland Browns , who currently lead the AFC North.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jalen Hurts blood clot diagnosis timeline: Where the situation started, how it developed and what now
summary: A look at everything that's happened with Hurts' health
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were found in his lungs. Speculation about the injury began shortly after the team announced he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf, which sidelined him for the Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers .
The team said his prognosis is "very good," and he is expected to make a full recovery. He's currently on blood thinners, which prevent him from participating in any contact activities until he's fully recovered. The severity of the injury has caused great concern over Hurts' future and has some calling for an investigation into how the Eagles approached the injury and treatment.
A lot has transpired in a short amount of time, and the timeline can get a bit confusing. His diagnosis also changed over the course of a week. So let's break it down to the facts:
This is the game where Hurts said the blood clot was "provoked." He was cleated in his calf during the 24-20 loss.
After practice, Hurts sought treatment on his calf, the original spot of the blood clot. Hurts was listed with a calf injury on the Week 5 injury report, but he was a full participant in Friday's practice ahead of the Eagles' trip to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars .
The team flew to London on the Friday before their international game, arriving late Friday night for the trip across the pond. The team would be in London for less than 48 hours. Hurts flew with the team, and the flight from Philly to London takes between seven and eight hours.
While in London, Hurts was seen by specialists, who reportedly found the blood clot through an MRI. According to reports, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m. local time. Initial reports said Hurts was advised by medical professionals not to sleep and had been up 36 hours before taking the field on Sunday. However, the QB's agent, Nicole Lynn, later released a statement saying that although Hurts stayed up late, he managed to get some sleep before the game. She said the team set up a room for him at the stadium.
The Eagles' medical staff and independent doctors told Hurts and the team that "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play," per a statement the team released on Oct. 15.
Hurts played the full game, throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles lost 19-17 and fell to 2-3 on the season.
The Eagles flew home from London the night of the game. Hurts was on the flight, which, again, would have taken between seven and eight hours.
Hurts was once again listed with a calf injury, this time on the Wednesday, Oct. 14 injury report, but was a full participant. Speaking with the media, before his test, he called his injury a "unique experience."
After practice, he underwent a second ultrasound, where doctors found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation.
After being a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Hurts was a non-participant in both Thursday and Friday's practices.
The team released a statement explaining that Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot when he initially sought treatment. They made the announcement that Hurts would be sidelined for their Week 6 game.
pic.twitter.com/9SeK1XzYRL
The Eagles signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad. The move felt like a premonition of Hurts going on IR, due to the number of quarterbacks they were carrying.
Shortly after reports that they would not be placing Hurts on IR, the Eagles did, in fact, put the QB on IR . Any player on IR is required to miss a minimum of four games.
Hurts was ruled out ahead of the Week 6 contest, and Tanner McKee started in his place. McKee went 26-of-45 with 215 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. The Eagles fell to 2-4 on the season.
The Eagles released a statement with an update on the situation. They said Hurts was "initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli." Pulmonary emboli means there were multiple blood clots now in his lungs, which is a serious situation.
The team said it expects him to make a full recovery and anticipates "that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners." More reports also came out at this time about Hurts' hospital stay in London and his lack of sleep before the Week 5 game.
pic.twitter.com/aBfyK55oxd
On Monday, there were multiple reports that Hurts' season was likely over, given his situation. While it seems likely, there has been no confirmation from the Eagles on an official timetable or return plan.

title: Dan Quinn denies confusion after viral fourth-down clip in Commanders loss to 49ers
summary: Broadcast cameras appeared to catch Washington's head coach surprised by a turnover on downs against the 49ers, but he insists he was just fielding a question from his staff
full_text:
To say Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was under a microscope in Week 6 is an understatement. Washington was playing the best team in the NFL, the San Francisco 49ers, on a national stage eight days after the team ran out the clock on themselves in embarrassing fashion, leading to a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants .
How Quinn managed his timeouts and the clock was going to be something everyone was watching, and it almost looked like Quinn made another embarrassing gaffe early in the second quarter.
On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Washington elected to go for it. Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball away — which is a conversation for another day — but there was a flag on the field. Officials called the Commanders for an illegal shift, and the 49ers declined the penalty, accepting the turnover on downs.
ESPN's cameras appeared to capture Quinn saying, "Oh! It was fourth down," as if he did not know the situation.
“Field goal.   Oh, that was 4th down?” certainly looks like lip readers believe Dan Quinn was completely unaware that it was 4th down and wanted to kick a field goal 💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/yJYuAUmVZX
After the game, Quinn was asked about the video that had since gone viral on social media.
"No, I definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn said. "We were going for it, and I was — I think what you're referring to, I was probably saying like, with the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it doesn't go, like — it's the turn on downs. I think somebody had asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?'  So, no, we were going for it. We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game.
"But no, I knew what happened. I think I probably was just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me, after an illegal shift, like it was a turnover on downs, and Jayden saw the foul, too. He also came out and saw the penalty."
If you go back and watch the video, that does not look like what was happening. Quinn looked surprised that the play was fourth down, not that he was correcting someone else. But you never know what kind of conversations are going on in those headsets.
There are no moral victories in the NFL , but Monday night was not a total tragedy for the Commanders. Washington put together a strong second half, storming back from down 23-3 to score 14 unanswered points. However, the Commanders could not pull off the upset, and questions remain about the man in charge.
At 1-4-1, this is Washington's worst six-game start to a season since 2020, when the "Football Team" started 1-5. That team ended up rebounding to win the NFC East.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Grading and ranking NFL first-year head coaches in new places after Week 6
summary: How the league's 10 new head coaches rank through the first third of the 2026 regular season
full_text:
With six weeks in the books, the NFL is now a third of the way through the 2026 NFL season. That means now is a fair time to check in on the 10 new head coaches hired this offseason.
Ten is tied for the most head-coaching changes in a single offseason ever, and six of the hires are first-time NFL head coaches. The head-coaching veterans in new places are Mike McCarthy, Kevin Stefanski, John Harbaugh and Robert Saleh. Here is a look at the 10 we will be grading and ranking through Week 6, listed in alphabetical order by team:
Let's dig into the 2026 new head coaches' report cards.
It's hard not to feel bad for rookie NFL head coach Jeff Hafley in his first season in charge. He's doing the best he can for a franchise that is paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million) in 2026.
As a result, the Dolphins are just the fifth team since at least 1950 to not lead in any of their first five games of a season, per CBS Sports Research. They joined Washington (1954, 1965), the Minnesota Vikings (1962) and the Houston Texans (2005) as the only teams to pull off this sad feat. Miami has the worst scoring offense (14.0 points per game) by mere decimal points.
They entered 2026 with the least experienced roster (608 career starts) by any team to open a season in recorded history since such data tracking began at the start of the 21st century, per CBS Sports Research. They also had one career Pro Bowl selection on their roster entering Week 1, running back De'Von Achane in 2025, which is tied for the fewest by any team to open a season in recorded history (2000). Oh, and Achane went down with a torn ACL in Week 3.
That really makes it almost impossible to evaluate Hafley's acumen as an NFL head coach. He's playing with an arm tied behind his back on a weekly basis in Year 1 of the Dolphins' latest rebuild.
It's been a rough start to the Robert Saleh era in Tennessee. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's group has the NFL's second-worst scoring offense (14.0 points per game), mere decimal points ahead of the Miami Dolphins, and the league's worst total offense (236.3 total yards per game). Quarterback Cam Ward , the 2025 first overall pick, has the worst expected points added (EPA) per dropback (-0.15) since he entered the league last season.
However, special teams coordinator John "Bones" Fassel's unit generated the first blocked punt return of 2026 in the Titans' 26-20 comeback win over the Indianapolis Colts . Tennessee overcame a 13-point deficit at halftime by outscoring the Colts 26-7 in the second half. Saleh has a lot of work to do, but his squad is entering Week 7 on a high note at least.
Kevin Stefanski deserves a mulligan for having to start Cooper Rush the first two weeks of the season. Once starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr . returned to the lineup in Week 3, the Falcons soared, crushing both the Green Bay Packers and the New Orleans by a combined score of 80-38. Then, the struggles returned with consecutive home losses against the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens and the Chicago Bears .
Atlanta is now 2-4 or worse for the first time since 2020, and it is 0-3 at home to start a season for just the third time in the 21st century (2003, 2020). Stefanski needs to be able to help his talented team find a more consistent existence going forward.
The Arizona Cardinals snapped their four-game losing streak in style in Week 6, upsetting the preseason Super Bowl betting favorite Los Angeles Rams on the road 18-16 with six made field goals and no touchdowns. That makes the Cardinals the owners of the largest upset win (13.5-point underdog) by any team this season, per CBS Sports Research. Week 6 also marked Arizona's first win since its season opener, also at SoFi Stadium, against the Los Angeles Chargers.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett doesn't really scare defenses deep downfield. He is averaging 6.9 air yards per pass attempt, the seventh fewest in the NFL this season. However, LaFleur made things work in Week 6. Now, LaFleur's mission needs to be maximizing the 2026 NFL Draft third-overall pick, running back Jeremiyah Love's rookie year, while hoping for a more dynamic starting quarterback in 2027.
The Las Vegas Raiders even being .500 six weeks through the season while starting a 38-year-old, post-Achilles tear Kirk Cousins is downright impressive. Las Vegas doesn't quite have the horses on the offensive line and the defense needed to truly contend, but it has been a much more fun watch than people would have thought. It is a disturbing trend that the defense, not Kubiak's side of the ball, has allowed 27-plus points for the fourth straight game, after allowing 27 points across Weeks 1 and 2 combined.
Las Vegas has a bright future ahead with Kubiak and Cousins helping develop 2026 first overall pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza .
John Harbaugh was trending to place a lot higher here as of just a couple of weeks ago, with the  Giants entering Week 5 out to a 3-1 start despite season-ending knee injuries to quarterback Jaxson Dart and three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns . However, the last two weeks have dropped him down the list. A tie with the Washington Commanders and the slump-buster that ended the New Orleans Saints ' three-game losing streak make for a brutal stretch.
Fortunately for Harbaugh, the rest of the NFC East has no desire to climb up the standings with the entire division going winless two weeks in a row.
The Steelers are starting to find their groove under new head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is averaging the fifth-most points per game (28.5) since Week 3, a major improvement after averaging the second-fewest points per game (11.5) in the league through the first two weeks.
Pittsburgh also just completed its largest fourth-quarter comeback (13 points, 16-3) since the 2002 AFC Wild Card Round against the Cleveland Browns in its 26-19 overtime road win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . McCarthy's offense has added more life this season to the Steelers' attack, and Pittsburgh is in a 4-2 bottleneck at the top of the AFC North as a result.
Inheriting two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson is a blessing for new Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, but he hasn't had him the last two weeks because of an ankle injury. In Week 5, Minter's squad went on the road in primetime and beat the Falcons on "Sunday Night Football" with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley . In Week 6, Huntley wasn't enough in a 13-10 loss against the Cleveland Browns.
Minter showed a coaching edge in Week 5 in Atlanta and the Week 3 win in Brazil against the Dallas Cowboys. The Ravens' +24-point differential is the eighth-best in the NFL this season, and they have the same record as the Browns and Steelers atop the AFC North.
New Bills head coach Joe Brady has an unfair advantage among his class of 2026 head-coaching hires because he has been his team's offensive coordinator since 2023. Quarterback Josh Allen leads the NFL in total touchdowns (17), and running back James Cook's 627 yards rushing rank as the third most in the NFL. The Bills were also able to overcome a five-turnover performance against the Los Angeles Chargers to win 24-16 in Week 3.
While Brady spends the bulk of his time on offense as the play caller, he is still responsible for overseeing his defense as his team's head coach. His Bills lead the league in points per drive (3.13) while ranking dead last in points per drive allowed (2.76). Buffalo's 28th-ranked scoring defense (28.5 points per game allowed) is holding Brady back from reaching an A-grade.
Cleveland Browns first-time NFL head coach Todd Monken is currently pulling off a miracle: His Browns are in first place in the AFC North in Week 6 or later for the first time since 2014. That's absolutely incredible. There's certainly a smoke and mirrors element to it as the Browns have the worst point differential (-16) by a team with a winning record this…
author: Garrett Podell
