title: 49ers vs. Commanders prediction: Can San Francisco remain unbeaten? Full 'Monday Night Football' breakdown
summary: San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset
full_text:
In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders .
San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night.
Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants , wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East.
Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Jayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook.
While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football.
The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL .
San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games.
It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards.
Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night.
San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league.
Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are.
Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game.
Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards.
The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't.
I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense. Pick: 49ers 27, Commanders 16
author: Jared Dubin

title: Rams special teams woes continue: Kicker Blake Grupe placed on injured reserve after knee injury
summary: Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams ' kicking conundrum continued into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect.
After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter.
However, things went downhill after that. Grupe left the game early after suffering a knee injury on a kickoff. On Monday, the Rams placed him on injured reserve, leaving them once again looking for a kicker. Head coach Sean McVay said Grupe tore his ACL.
Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly.
New Rams kicker Blake Grupe is doubtful to return after making this tackle pic.twitter.com/EgxKFTFSsq
With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation was reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans served as the kicker. He only attempted one kicker, a successful extra point after the Rams' fourth-quarter touchdown.
The punter Ethan Evans makes the PAT to give the Rams the lead! AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0HpOiZAWLp
However, otherwise, Los Angeles was hesitant to use Evans. After Matthew Stafford connected with Blake Corum for a 15-yard touchdown in the second quarter, they kept the offense on the field for a two-point attempt, which failed. Then, when they were at the Arizona 27-yard line and faced with a fourth-and-1, Los Angeles went for it, but turned the ball over on downs.
Grupe entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2023, initially signing with the Saints . He played for New Orleans until midway through the 2025 season, when he was released. After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. Coming into this game, Grupe had converted 81.9% of his career field goals (86-of-105) and 98% of his extra points (96-of-98).
The kicking game has been an issue throughout the first half of the season for the Rams, and it came to a head during Monday's overtime loss to the Bills . Mevis failed to convert on either of his field goal attempts, including what would've been a game-winner, which was blocked. That forced Los Angeles' hand to make a change in favor of Grupe, but this latest injury keeps them in a kicking nightmare.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: John Harbaugh provides update on Giants' QB situation between JJ McCarthy, Jameis Winston
summary: McCarthy made his Giants debut on Sunday after Jameis Winston was benched
full_text:
John Harbaugh's first season as the New York Giants coach is once again dominated by his quarterback situation. First, it was the season-ending injury to Jaxson Dart . Now, it's a position battle between JJ McCarthy and Jameis Winston .
The Giants initially turned to Winston after Dart suffered his injury in Week 2. As he is known to do, Winston has had good and bad moments over the past five games. He has played well enough, though, to post a 2-1-1 record as the Giants' starting quarterback.
Winston struggled on Sunday, however, and he was replaced in the second half by McCarthy, who engineered three fourth-quarter scoring drives. The comeback fell short, however, as the Saints left New Jersey with a 34-27 win.
Harbaugh, as expected, was asked on Monday if Winston would be his starting quarterback for the Giants' upcoming road game against the Houston Texans .
"We're working through that now, homing in on a decision," Harbaugh said.
John Harbaugh says the Giants are "honing in" on a QB decision when asked if Jameis Winston will be the starter for their next game pic.twitter.com/UzG817HV2U
Harbaugh's decision will be crucial for the Giants, who are currently in first place in the NFC East. Should they give Winston another shot, or is it time to see what McCarthy can do ?
Harbaugh is likely considering the opponent. The Texans, after an 0-4 start, have won two straight games after they defeated the Jaguars on Sunday in London. While this season hasn't been their best, the Texans have talented players on defense, especially pass rusher Will Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. While McCarthy's mobility may be an asset, his lack of experience running the Giants' offense could also hold the Giants back.
Expect Harbaugh to give both quarterbacks reps during practice until a decision is made.
Quarterback isn't the only position Harbaugh needs to address. He also needs to figure out who the Giants' starting running back is after Cam Skattebo — the Giants' starter on paper — inexplicably received zero carries during Sunday's loss to the Saints. Harbaugh said afterward that he is waiting for one of his running backs to earn the job.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL suspends Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson for spitting on Raiders' Brock Bowers
summary: Gardner-Johnson was ejected during Sunday's game vs. the Raiders and will forfeit money and playing time
full_text:
C.J. Gardner-Johnson will face discipline from the NFL after spitting on Brock Bowers during the Buffalo Bills ' Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .
On Monday, the NFL suspended the Buffalo safety for one game without pay for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct. Gardner-Johnson will miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens .
Gardner-Johnson was ejected after spitting on Bowers as he walked away during the second quarter. According to the NFL, his actions violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."
C.J. Gardner-Johnson spits in the direction of Brock Bowers, leading to disqualification pic.twitter.com/8zW4OYIP7o
Because the Bills are in their bye week, Gardner-Johnson's suspension won't begin until Monday, October 26. He will be eligible to return to the Bills' active roster the following Monday ahead of their Week 9 road game against the Minnesota Vikings .
Gardner-Johnson may appeal the suspension, but it's currently unknown whether he intends to do so. He issued an apology after the game through his Instagram page.
"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."
The NFL has taken a firmer stance on players spitting on one another since Broncos linebacker Bill Romanowski's infamous spit on 49ers wideout J.J. Stokes during a Monday night game in 1997. While he was fined $7,500 and received a stern letter from the league, Romanowski did not miss any games. He ultimately helped the Broncos win their first Super Bowl that season.
Last season, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was fined $57,222 (the equivalent of a game check) and was ejected after spitting on Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott prior to Philadelphia's season-opening win over Dallas. The league decided not to suspend Carter for an additional game.
An eight-year veteran, Gardner-Johnson is in the middle of his first season with the Bills. While he has played for six teams, Gardner-Johnson is best known for his two seasons with the Eagles. He had a league-high six interceptions in 2022 while helping the Eagles become NFC Champions. In 2024 (following a season in Detroit), Gardner-Johnson had six interceptions for the eventual Super Bowl champs.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Jalen Hurts expected to miss rest of 2026 season after blood clots found in lungs
summary: The Eagles quarterback is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery, but he cannot participate in contact activities
full_text:
Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season , according to multiple reports, after blood clots were found in his lungs.
The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issued a joint statement on Monday laying out his updated diagnosis after originally announcing he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf that caused him to miss Week 6. A follow-up scan over the weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, and he had "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.
The Eagles said Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery. However, he will be treated with blood thinners, which will take him away from football activities until he is off the treatment.
Here is the full statement:
"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.
"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.
"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."
It was initially diagnosed as a superficial blood clot. At that time, doctors advised Hurts not to sleep as a precaution, so he stayed awake for roughly 36 hours prior to the game against the Jaguars , according to reports. Despite not getting any sleep, Hurts started and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown.
Lynn has since clarified that Hurts was able to sleep despite being evaluated at the hospital until the early hours of Sunday morning. She said that the Eagles set up a room for him at the stadium.
No clots were found until Hurts was in London.  It was later discovered that the blood clot was "provoked," meaning that it was caused by Hurts getting cleated in his calf during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. That game took place a week before Philadelphia's game in London.
Hurts traveled to London that week, appearing on that week's injury report with a calf injury on Friday. He was a full practice participant that day and had no injury designation prior to the Eagles' game against the Jaguars. Hurts reportedly went to the hospital the evening prior to Sunday's game.
Philadelphia will move forward with Tanner McKee at quarterback. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee made his first start of the season Sunday against the Panthers . He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-15 loss that dropped the Eagles to 2-4.
Hurts, 28, is in his seventh season with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft . During his first six seasons, Hurts earned three Pro Bowl selections and helped lead the Eagles to two NFC titles and a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. He holds the single-game Super Bowl record for rushing yards by a quarterback (72 against the Chiefs ). Hurts is one of just two players (the other being Terrell Davis) to run for three touchdowns in a Super Bowl game.
Hurts was named MVP of Super Bowl LIX after amassing 293 total yards and scoring three total touchdowns in the Eagles' 40-22 win over the Chiefs. Hurts has the highest career completion percentage (73.3%) in Super Bowl history among passers with at least 40 attempts.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Rams face historic Super Bowl challenge after stunning 2-4 start, but schedule offers path back
summary: No team has ever stood in the Rams' position and proceeded to win the Super Bowl
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams put together the most impressive offseason of any team in the NFL , it would have taken an extreme amount of imagination to picture them opening the year at 2-4 and sitting in last place in the NFC West. The Rams were preseason Super Bowl favorites by a hefty margin, but just six weeks into the campaign, they find themselves forced to overcome historically long odds in order to deliver on those expectations.
No team in the Super Bowl era has won its conference after opening the season with a losing record through six weeks. Not only do the Rams have a losing record, but they are two games back from .500 at 2-4.
Winning the NFC was once a Super Bowl prerequisite that many expected the Rams to accomplish without much pushback. Now they would carve their name into the history books if they achieve it.
The volume of talent on the roster is ample enough that nobody would bat an eye if the Rams caught fire, rattled off a prolonged winning streak and peaked at the right time on their way to a championship. The coaching staff is as heralded as they come, too. Nearly all of the pieces are in place, and the ones that are not -- like Myles Garrett as he works his way back from knee surgery -- will be in due time. This has the makings of a loaded team that simply has not yet gelled, and once it does, it could be a monster that obliterates everything in its path.
At the same time, Los Angeles stands at the bottom of its division for good reason. Its special teams EPA is the lowest in the league, and its kicking woes were directly to blame for the Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Matthew Stafford regressed noticeably from his MVP form, leading to a sharp downturn in explosive plays and general offensive consistency. The pass rush clearly misses Garrett, because the defense's sack rate is the sixth-lowest in the NFL. There are real discipline questions, too, as penalties and turnovers rear their ugly heads.
The Rams cannot turn their season into a success over the next month (they can only do so by pulling off the historic run to the Super Bowl), but these next four games will determine whether it is a complete failure or if they can turn things around.
The most difficult stretch of the 17-game slate is complete. The Rams' schedule was always projected as front- and back-loaded with a soft filling in the middle. That central part is even cushier than anticipated, and the home stretch seems nowhere near as grueling as it looked on paper heading into the year. Even with three of their next four games coming away from home, they will be sizable favorites in each of them. Taking care of business would put them at 6-4 entering the bye week.
Once the Rams emerge from their week off, they face a handful of division title contenders. The Packers and Cowboys have glaring issues but remain well within striking distance of the NFC North and NFC East leads, respectively, and beating them will be critical in the Wild Card race. And, of course, the divisional rivalry games against the 49ers and Seahawks could be where the NFC West is won or lost.
If the Rams continue to play at the same level they performed in Weeks 1-6, they cannot be trusted to even beat their overmatched opponents in this favorable upcoming four-game stretch, let alone the more formidable squads that line the back half of the schedule. They deserve the benefit of the doubt because of the supreme talent on their roster and Sean McVay's track record as a superstar coach, but they had better correct course during this next month of advantageous matchups, because their goodwill is running low.
Success from here on looks like this: Stafford pulls out of his slump as he faces more manageable competition, Garrett returns before the bye week and uplifts the defense as he nears midseason form and the revitalized units mask the unfixable problems on special teams.
If those elements come together, the Rams should be in ideal shape to attack the back half of their schedule and clinch a playoff spot. Once they reach the postseason, all bets are off. It becomes a one-game season, and their talent will stack up favorably against anyone they see.
The Super Bowl is still an attainable goal, but there is a reason no team in this position has ever won it. The difference between the Rams and those who came before them, though, is that this is as stacked of a roster as the league has ever seen. If anyone is capable of pulling off the turnaround, it has to be them.

title: Cowboys' Stephen Jones addresses Brian Schottenheimer's job status after team's 2-4 start
summary: Dallas is 10-13 under Schottenheimer after a lackluster loss against the Packers on Sunday
full_text:
Brian Schottenheimer's job status has become a hot-button topic amid the Cowboys ' slow start to the 2026 season. After Sunday's uninspiring loss to historical rival Green Bay Packers, the Cowboys sit at 2-4.
Dallas is now just 10-13 since Schottenheimer succeeded Mike McCarthy as coach ahead of the 2025 season. The Cowboys, despite playing in the NFL's easiest division, find themselves behind the Giants and Eagles (who likely won't have Jalen Hurts for the rest of the 2026 season) in the NFC East standings.
On Monday, Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones was asked about his confidence level in Schottenheimer. He said that he and owner/GM Jerry Jones "absolutely" believe in Schottenheimer, the rest of the coaching staff and the players.
"There's not any question in Jerry and my mind," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan, via The Athletic . "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. Feel really good about our coaching staff. We just got to have it continue to evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."
Jones did acknowledge that the Cowboys' start to the season has been less than ideal.
"Obviously very disappointing," he said . "Frustrated. But at the same time, we got a lot of football to play. We've got resolve. We just got to go back to work. We like the players. We like the coaches."
The Cowboys showed no resolve on Sunday night, especially on offense . While Dallas' much-maligned defense (which recently added former NFL head coach Mike Pettine to the staff as a senior advisor) showed signs of growth, its offense had arguably its worst game of the season. That's saying something, given the egg it laid in Week 5 against the previously winless Buccaneers .
Schottenheimer had no answer for what the Packers were doing defensively.
For a second straight week, the Cowboys' offense was held to under 20 points. They set season lows with 13 points, 303 total yards and 48 yards rushing. The unit also coughed up the ball twice and was just 5-of-13 on third down.
Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott's night was particularly odd. He was alarmingly casual late in the game with the Cowboys trailing by double digits. He seemed to have no interest in throwing deep (his longest completion was 21 yards), which led to him averaging less than five yards per pass attempt. His only sense of urgency appeared to be his hasty postgame exit from Lambeau Field .
"It's just frustrating to not get going," Prescott said afterward . "Getting hit, getting blitzed is part of the game. But not executing our answers for it, and only leaving the game with 13 points...Yeah, it's very frustrating. But we've got to fix it, and all the guys in that locker room are capable of it."
One of the most surprising things from Sunday night's game was how Green Bay's receiving duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden outperformed Dallas' CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Watson and Golden combined for nine passes for 164 yards and a score, compared to Lamb and Pickens' combined stat line of 15 catches for 143 yards and no scores.
Their body language on the sideline spoke volumes as well. The Cowboys didn't appear to believe that they could win, even when the game was still in reach.
"It is surprising in terms of how we're performing on offense," Jones said .
While the Cowboys look nothing like a championship contender now, Jones is right in that it is too early to throw the white flag, especially when you look at the Cowboys' upcoming schedule. Dallas' next three games are against teams currently at 2-4. If the Cowboys were going to right the ship, this would be the time to do so.
If Dallas' struggles continue, however, don't be surprised if Jones and Co. change their tone regarding Schottenheimer, who acknowledged following Sunday night's loss that his team's recent performances are not up to par.
"We've got to fix the mistakes that we've talked about," Schottenheimer said . "This is something that we've addressed and talked about. Again, it starts with myself and the coaching staff to understand, again, the ball matters more than anything in the National Football League. It's the ball. Second, it's the line of scrimmage. And we haven't been very good in the last two games, so that's what we're responsible and accountable for. And I stand up here and accept that."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Why Colts fired Chris Ballard: Seven moves that contributed to GM's downfall
summary: Messy coaching changes, one-sided trades and ill-fated quarterback signings led to Ballard's downfall
full_text:
A change in leadership is underway for the Indianapolis Colts , as the franchise announced the firing of general manager Chris Ballard after 10 years in the role. His results over a decade at the helm were modest at best and more accurately described as frustrating and disappointing, given that he was the longest-tenured general manager in NFL history to have a losing record and one or fewer postseason wins. Time ran out following a string of moves that aged poorly and a run of on-field mediocrity.
Late owner Jim Irsay remained committed to Ballard until his death in May 2025, and Carlie Irsay-Gordon put pressure on Ballard upon her rise to leadership, detailing last offseason that the urgency to deliver results has never been higher. That shift in expectations, paired with untimely, poorly executed moves, was Ballard's downfall.
From his role in coaching hires to trades that did not withstand the test of time, failures dotted Ballard's resume by the end of his tenure. The inability to find a long-term answer at quarterback in the wake of Andrew Luck's retirement in 2019 was a prevalent issue across his lengthy run as general manager, too. Underwhelming draft picks did not help his cause, either. All of those decisions compounded on each other and largely explained why the Colts went just 72-82-1 under his reign and missed the playoffs each of the last five years.
Here are the costliest moves that contributed to Ballard's firing.
Indianapolis needed a new coach after Chuck Pagano's firing in 2017. Ballard led the search process, identified New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels as his primary target and held multiple interviews with him before selecting him as the man for the job at the end of his Super Bowl run. The sides agreed verbally to terms on a contract, and the Colts announced McDaniel as their coach and scheduled an introductory press conference. But then McDaniel backed out.
Ballard was left blindsided and found himself scrambling to find a new candidate while other teams filled their vacant coaching positions. The Colts ultimately settled on Frank Reich, whose hiring panned out well given the circumstances. He accounted for both postseason appearances of the Ballard era and logged three winning seasons in four and a half years until his firing in 2022. But while Reich oversaw a period of success on the field, the wins always came with the context that he was not Ballard's first choice.
Philip Rivers , the second starting quarterback of the post-Luck era, announced his retirement at the end of the 2020 campaign and left Ballard in search of a signal-caller for the third consecutive offseason. While he did not lead the charge for Carson Wentz , he ultimately signed off on a trade that brought the Super Bowl champion to Indianapolis in exchange for a 2021 third-round pick and a 2022 conditional first-rounder. Reich was the primary force behind the acquisition as he hoped to reunite with the quarterback that helped him win the Super Bowl during his time as the Philadelphia Eagles ' offensive coordinator, and Ballard gave the OK to invest multiple years of early-round draft capital to bring him in.
It did not work out. Wentz helped keep the Colts in the postseason hunt but delivered a clunker of a performance in a do-or-die Week 18 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars that dashed their playoff hopes. Irsay was irate with how Wentz failed to deliver a win in that critical spot and publicly bashed both him and the decision to trade for him. Ballard and Reich were left with egg on their faces when their team owner forced Wentz out of town, rendering the trade to acquire him a total failure.
For the third consecutive year, Ballard put his faith in an aging quarterback in the decline phase of his career. He gave up a third-round pick to acquire Matt Ryan from the Atlanta Falcons , absorbed the final two years of his contract and guaranteed the remainder of his deal, which committed $54 million to a player who ultimately spent only one season on the roster and made him one of only three quarterbacks in the league at that time with a fully guaranteed contract.
Ryan played some of the worst football of his career over the first seven weeks of the year and paced the NFL in interceptions with nine when Reich announced a quarterback change. The Colts then fired Reich and brought in Jeff Saturday on an interim basis, and he reinserted Ryan into the lineup only to watch him play a role in Indianapolis falling on its face with the largest blown lead in league history later that season. That was the end of his run as the starter, and the Colts released him at the end of the year and had to eat the remaining money on his guaranteed deal.
Following Irsay's failed experiment with Saturday as the interim coach, Ballard reprised his role as the leader of a coaching search and landed on Shane Steichen as the man for the job. Ballard saw Steichen's success as an offensive coordinator and his ability to develop quarterbacks, and tasked him with doing the same for a Colts franchise that desperately needed stability at the most important position. Steichen ultimately outlasted Ballard, but he is in hot water, too, for the 2-4 start to the 2026 season and for last year's collapse.
If Steichen does not right the ship in the weeks to come and concludes his tenure without a single postseason trip, his failures will be another mark against Ballard's record of coaching hires.
It became clear over the previous seasons that a veteran quarterback could not take the offense to the next level, so the Colts tore everything down and started from scratch in 2023 and, for the first time in Ballard's career, used the draft to find their long-term answer at the position. Ballard landed on Anthony Richardson as his target with the No. 4 overall pick, which raised eyebrows at the time, considering the Florida product had just one year of starting experience in college and was nowhere near refined as a passer. Richardson's uncanny athleticism masked the throwing concerns in the pre-draft process, but it was not enough to prevent him from flaming out as an NFL starter.
An AC joint sprain cut Richardson's rookie year short after five games, and he struggled the following year en route to a benching that inserted Joe Flacco into the lineup as his replacement. Richardson then lost a position battle to Daniel Jones in 2025 and missed the majority of the season with a fracture in the orbital bone in his eye. While he remains on the roster, Richardson is a bust of a first-round pick at this stage of his career.
When the Colts started last season at 7-1, Ballard saw it as his opportunity to go all-in. What was supposed to be a game-changing trade to elevate the defense and push Indianapolis into the postseason, however, ultimately became a large part of Ballard's undoing as general manager. He paid the New York Jets two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell in exchange for cornerback Sauce Gardner . At the time, it seemed like a high price to pay but a potentially worthy one considering Gardner's status as a two-time first-team All-Pro honoree and rising 24-year-old superstar.
With the benefit of hindsight, the trade was a complete failure. The Jets turned the first of two draft picks into a potentially foundational tight end in Kenyon Sadiq , made Mitchell a key piece of their passing attack and are poised to add to their young core in 2027 with the second first-rounder. The Colts, meanwhile, mortgaged their future for an underperforming cornerback who is not nearly living up to his contract as a top-five earner at his position.
Gardner bounced in and out of the lineup last season with a calf injury, which did not help the Colts in their failed push for a playoff berth. That alone rendered the trade an early failure, because one of the main reasons Ballard made it was to strengthen the 2025 roster, which looked potentially like the best one of his tenure. Gardner…

title: What's next for Eagles after Jalen Hurts injury? Three games could shape franchise's future
summary: The Eagles have little reason to intentionally tank, but an upcoming three-game divisional stretch will reveal whether they can salvage their season
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' season was already seemingly falling apart before the team boarded a plane to London. With two more losses since then, along with Monday's news that Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, the narrative that the Eagles are in freefall is in full effect.
In any other situation, the Eagles would embark on an organic tank, a byproduct of the team's mounting injuries and losses. Losing is never acceptable (especially in a city like Philadelphia, which prides itself on overcoming the odds), but it would be understood, given the amount of body blows the Eagles have already endured.
The Eagles won't intentionally tank, however. There's too much football left to play, the Eagles have too many good players on their roster, and they play in the NFL's easiest division to win.
Philadelphia's objective, at least to me, is clear: win as many games as you can with the players you have. Best case, the Eagles find a way to win a division that could be had with seven wins. Worst case, the Eagles stumble into a top-five pick in next year's draft.
Before we look ahead, let's look back at the Eagles' first six games. Four of their first five games were one-score outcomes (the only outlier was the embarrassing loss in Chicago in Week 3). On Sunday, the Eagles weren't put away until Bryce Young's second touchdown pass made it an 11-point game with 6:33 left. Philadelphia gave the defending NFC South champs a fight despite the absence of Hurts and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and losing Nolan Smith during the game (concussion).
In a losing effort, the Eagles received encouraging performances from DeVonta Smith (75 yards and a touchdown), Dallas Goedert (six catches for 61 yards in his second game back from injury), linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr . (six tackles and a half-sack) and defensive end Arnold Ebiketie (nine tackles).
Sunday was essentially Tanner McKee's first legitimate start (his first two starts the previous two seasons were in meaningless games where the vast majority of the starters rested). Given the circumstances, McKee's performance wasn't bad by any stretch. He attempted 45 passes (way too many for a player in his position), completed 26, and threw for 215 yards and a touchdown. His stat line did not include an interception, which is impressive given his lack of experience and the number of times he threw the ball up.
McKee's performance is even more impressive when you factor in that he was sacked 3 times and had no running game to take the pressure off him.
Tanner McKee throws DeVonta Smith a perfect ball for the touchdown CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6xngV0MgMW
The Eagles' next three games will likely determine how the rest of the season plays out. Each game is against NFC East division foes, with two of the games being played in Philadelphia. Philadelphia hosts Dallas this weekend, travels to Washington in Week 8, hosts the Giants in Week 9, and then heads into its bye week.
The Eagles are in second place in the NFC East, 1.5 games behind first-place New York. If the Eagles can win two of their upcoming three games (including the matchup with the Giants), they will still be in the hunt to win the division entering Week 11, when Philadelphia will host a Steelers team that hasn't won in the City of Brotherly Love since 1965.
The Eagles' next three games will determine how GM Howie Roseman handles the trade deadline, which falls during Philadelphia's bye week. If the Eagles show signs of revival during that span, Roseman may try to acquire a few players who can help them win a weak division. Roseman won't do anything that will mortgage the team's future, however.
The more likely scenario is Roseman either standing pat or dealing a few pricey veterans to teams hoping to make a playoff push. Roseman would surely like to add to his pile of future draft picks that includes a projected eight picks in 2027 and two first- and two second-round picks in 2028.
As bleak as it looks, the Eagles can win the NFC East if they right the ship during the next three weeks. Crazier things have happened, like in 2017, when the Eagles defeated Tom Brady and the Patriots in the Super Bowl with backup quarterback Nick Foles winning MVP honors.
If the Eagles can't turn things around in the next three weeks, Roseman can start making moves to improve his team's situation in 2027 and beyond.

title: Former Cardinals employees enter into lawsuit
summary: Two former Arizona Cardinals employees have filed a lawsuit against the team plus owner Michael Bidwill. The lawsuit is fairly broad, but alleges discrimination involving race relations and not being paid properly. RELATED: GRADING THE MARV HARRISON TRADE The lawsuit was filed by Don Shumpert, who was an offensive assistant coach with Arizona from 2020 […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Two former Arizona Cardinals employees have filed a lawsuit against the team plus owner Michael Bidwill. The lawsuit is fairly broad, but alleges discrimination involving race relations and not being paid properly. RELATED: GRADING THE MARV HARRISON TRADE The lawsuit was filed by Don Shumpert, who was an offensive assistant coach with Arizona from 2020 to 2021, and Kendra Hogue, who was the former assistant to the Cardinals’ COO, Jeremy Walls. Walls has been the team’s COO since 2023 and remains in this position. Hogue’s allegations are numerous and wide-ranging. The bulk of it involves racial discrimination. In the suit, she states that, as a black woman, she was subject to disparate treatment and that the workplace environment was intolerable. She also alleges constructive termination, defamation, harassment, retaliation, and intentional infliction of emotional distress. This forced her to resign from her position. Shumpert’s allegations are less vague and pretty much to the point. He states in the suit that he joined the team as a coaching fellow in 2019, then joined the staff. Several years later, he was finally promoted to running backs coach, but also had the responsibilities of his former position. This meant he was working two positions and being paid for one. When Shumpert, who is black, met with the front office to discuss a pay raise, he met with GM Steve Keim and Cardinals head coach Kliff Kingsbury. According to the suit, he was told they weren’t in a position to discuss the matter. He points out in the suit that several white coaches on the current staff had been given new titles that came with pay increases. Shumpert specifically mentions two white coaches who were given title increases, yet without actually having their responsibilities change. Shumpert did mention a few other isolated instances, including ones with Bidwill. A week after he met with Keim and Kingsbury, he was fired. He has alleged that the Cardinals made false statements about the circumstances of his departure. The Cardinals responded to the lawsuit, stating that none of the allegations are factual. In the meantime, the lawsuit went before a federal judge. He then ruled that a discrimination lawsuit must be settled via a third party rather than in open court. This meant the decision would be made by a magistrate instead of being handled in a courtroom, thus limiting the financial damages if the team is found liable. This in itself is considered a victory for the franchise to keep the case out of the courtroom. But it had a solid foundation. Both former employees had signed agreements when they were hired stating: “that any dispute, controversy, or claim related to their employment be resolved through binding arbitration rather than a lawsuit.” NFL teams are not billion-dollar entities without knowing how to defend themselves before any lawsuit ever comes into play.

title: Word is, Chad Ryland’s mom had a hand in Cardinals win
summary: Last weekend, after the beatdown from the Detroit Lions, a lot of souls were searched and the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had to rethink an area or two that needed to be addressed. Kicker wasn’t one of them, although Chad Ryland did miss a 53-yard field goal against the Lions. RELATED: RYLAND OUTSCORED THE RAMS […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Chad Ryland #38 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrates after his game winning field goal in his team's 18-16 win against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last weekend, after the beatdown from the Detroit Lions, a lot of souls were searched and the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had to rethink an area or two that needed to be addressed. Kicker wasn’t one of them, although Chad Ryland did miss a 53-yard field goal against the Lions. RELATED: RYLAND OUTSCORED THE RAMS BY HIMSELF In this weekend’s game, Ryland had a different experience. From his mom. On Sunday, Ryland received a rare, early-morning game-day text from his mother, Deb Ryland. Knowing how anxious her son was from missing a kick the game before, Deb wanted her son to know something. The text told Chad to have a good game, to trust his process, and command the field. That struck something inside Ryland, who had only missed one field goal all year until the Detroit contest. Against the Los Angeles Rams, Ryland accounted for all of Arizona‘s points by connecting on all six field goal attempts, including the 43-yarder as time expired as the Cardinals won 18-16 in an important divisional matchup. HE DON’T MISS 🎯 all 6️⃣ FGs from @C_Ryland38 vs the Rams pic.twitter.com/a76xVpPFiQ — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 19, 2026 Ryland became the 10th kicker in NFL history to kick six field goals in a single game successfully. He is now ranked #4 on the franchise list for “scoring the most points by a single player in a single game,” behind Ernie Nevers’ 40 points in 1929, K Jay Feeley’s 25 points in Week 10 of the 2010 season, and K Jim Bakken’s 21 points in 1967. Arizona did to the Rams what other clubs have been doing to them for the past two seasons: take a sure loss and switch it to a win. Los Angeles had tied the contest 15-15 on a late touchdown with 47 seconds remaining. Their new kicker, Blake Grupe, became injured during the game with an ACL tear. Their punter, Ethan Evans, was forced to attempt the PAT and made it as the Rams went ahead 16-15. The Cardinals moved the ball down with just 47 ticks on the clock and got into field goal range with the help of a 21-yard reception by backup receiver Jalen Brooks and a subsequent unnecessary roughness penalty. Now on LA’s 25-yard line, Ryland trotted out and nailed the game-winner. Remember what mama said: trust his process, command the field, and have a good game. This same story is what has been happening to the Cardinals this year and in seven contests last season. Suddenly, the plot flipped. Obviously, the entire Cardinals fanbase learned that this year’s edition has zero quit in them, and they are not out of any game and can capitalize on every opportunity they have. Because Ryland’s mother said so.
author: Barry Shuck

title: Arizona Cardinals news: Cards given ‘B’ in massive upset over Rams
summary: The Cardinals fought and fought and fought in what many believed would be a lopsided victory for the Rams. Instead, the Cardinals kicked six field goals en route to upsetting LA 18-16 inside SoFi Stadium. With the win, both the Cardinals and Rams are 2-4, which also means the Rams are now in last place […]
full_text: The Cardinals fought and fought and fought in what many believed would be a lopsided victory for the Rams. Instead, the Cardinals kicked six field goals en route to upsetting LA 18-16 inside SoFi Stadium. With the win, both the Cardinals and Rams are 2-4, which also means the Rams are now in last place of the division. For their efforts, CBS Sports’ John Breech gave the Cardinals a “B” grade this week. Here’s what he had to say: “ The Cardinals beat the Rams without scoring a touchdown and they did it because their defense played its best game of the season. After surrendering at least 36 points in three straight games, the Cardinals clamped down against the Rams, holding them under 300 yards of offense. The Cards went blitz happy and it worked because it kept Matthew Stafford from throwing the ball downfield. Holding the Rams to just 16 points was a stunning performance for a defense that had surrendered at least 30 points in four straight games. With the defense playing so well, Chad Ryland’s six field goals were enough to pull out the win. The Cards used defense and special teams to rule the day, and thanks to this win, they’re now tied with the Rams in the AFC West standings. ” Do you think this is the correct grade for the Cardinals this week? Should it higher? Lower? Let us know all of your thoughts below! This defense is still one of the worst in the league, but the offense can keep them afloat against most sub-par opponents. Atlanta Falcons (2-4) Week 6 Result: Falcons 23 – Bears 21 Week 7 Opponent: San Francisco 49ers The Falcons have lost two games in a row for the second time this season. The offense came out flat, scoring only one touchdown in the first three quarters, and the defense is playing guys at the bottom of the roster across multiple positions. The late effort was good to see, but it was too little too late. This offense struggles under pressure, and it struggles as a unit. The play calling in these scenarios often relies on long developing routes and lacks quick hitters. Penix is struggling to diagnose pressure and is holding the ball too long, and the offensive line is struggling to win one-on-ones and sort out the blitz. Caleb Williams' first drive back ends in a TD to Colston Loveland 🐻 CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/krhXYNpu6F — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 The Panthers are the only winning team in the division, and if others can’t find their footing soon, it looks like the cats will run away with it. There’s still more than half a season to play, but this could be the least dramatic finish we’ve seen in the NFC South in a long time.

title: Kendal Daniels injury: Falcons rookie LB carted off with apparent head/neck injury vs. Bears
summary: UPDATE: Monday, 4:13 p.m. ET Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Monday and shared an update about Daniels’ condition, saying it was “all positive news” and that Daniels was in the building with the team. “Feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got and we feel really good about where he […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta linebacker Kendal Daniels (53) reacts during the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UPDATE: Monday, 4:13 p.m. ET Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Monday and shared an update about Daniels’ condition, saying it was “all positive news” and that Daniels was in the building with the team. “Feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got and we feel really good about where he is,” Stefanski said, per ESPN’s Mark Raimondi. Stefanski: All positive news on Kendal Daniels. He's here back in the building today. … Feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got and we feel really good about where he is. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) October 19, 2026 UPDATE: 6:06 p.m ET Kendal Daniels has apparently been released from Grady Memorial Hospital and returned to the Falcons’ locker room postgame. According to Will McFadden of AtlantaFalcons.com, Daniels was walking on his own, which is a relief considering how dangerous the injury looked. While we were wrapping up with Bijan Robinson in the locker room after the game, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels came in with a couple of trainers. He was walking on his own, which is obviously a good sign after the scary scene today. — Will McFadden (@willmcfadden) October 18, 2026 UPDATE: 3:53 p.m. ET The Falcons released a statement on Daniels. Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels is alert and has movement in all his extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels was carted off the field in the third quarter of the Falcons’ Week 6 matchup against the Bears. The top of his head collided with another player during a tackle on Bears TE Colston Loveland, and he immediately reacted like he was in intense pain. Daniels’ injury comes after fellow linebacker Divine Deablo left the game with an arm injury. Deablo has been ruled out for the remainder of the matchup. Losing both of these players is a blow for sure, but I have to think it’s especially to focus after seeing a player who’s been so central to what this defense does well go down with such a scary injury. Prior to leaving the field, Daniels was secured to a backboard. Prior to the medical staff getting involved, right after the hit, Daniels did appear to be moving his arms and hands, so hopefully that’s a good sign. Daniels has been a fantastic fit for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense, and he’s very quickly developed as a leader on the field. When Deablo went down with the arm injury, it was the rookie Daniels who took over the green dot. Josh Woods swapped out his helmet while the medical team was attending to Daniels to take over the green dot, according to The Athletic’s Josh Kendall . The Falcons defense has been hit hard with injuries of late. In addition to Daniels and Deablo, cornerback AJ Terrell is on injured reserve, and his counterpart CJ Henderson is out Sunday with a groin injury. We will update this post as more information becomes available, and we’re wishing Daniels all the best.
