title: NFL Week 7 Power Rankings: Teams Trending Up or Down?
summary: With the conclusion of Week 6, we are inching closer and closer to the midway point of the season. While the league’s elite and bottom-feeders have started to identify themselves, there’s still plenty to be learned in the coming weeks and months about how the NFL’s playoff picture will start to take shape. With six […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during the second quarter of the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the conclusion of Week 6, we are inching closer and closer to the midway point of the season. While the league’s elite and bottom-feeders have started to identify themselves, there’s still plenty to be learned in the coming weeks and months about how the NFL’s playoff picture will start to take shape. With six weeks in the books, it’s time to take a stock-watch approach to each team’s season so far and see how it’s trending against preseason expectations—and more in our Week 7 installment of WCG NFL Power Rankings. 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-0) Trending: Up Whew, what a game on Monday night, huh? The only thing stopping some from fully buying into this team is their rash of injuries that just won’t stop. That said, they’ve kept winning, and usually have done so convincingly. This is a very well-rounded team, albeit one of the oldest rosters in the league. With a three-game lead in the division, it’s hard to imagine a scenario where the 49ers aren’t at least in the NFC Championship game, barring a major step back. 2. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) Trending: Up Six weeks and five games in, it’s safe to say t025 was the outlier and the Chiefs’ window hasn’t closed. While many expected a bounce-back, few saw a perfect 5-0 start coming. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has looked good coming off a torn ACL, and running back Kenneth Walker has been a game-changer. With the Raiders fading and the Broncos’ offensive issues, the AFC West looks like theirs for the taking. 3. Buffalo Bills (5-1) Trending: Up It hasn’t always been pretty, and there are still plenty of questions remaining on the defensive side of the ball, but the Bills continue to find ways to win games. Even though the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, the Bills look like the perennial contender that they are, especially if they can get the defense playing at a higher level. One thing is for sure: having an MVP-caliber quarterback in Josh Allen helps, and he continues to make mind-boggling plays for his team each week. 4. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) Trending: Up No matter how the offense has performed to this point, a 5-0 start is about as much of a dream come true as anything Vikings fans could have asked for. Their defense under Brian Flores continues to play at an elite level. If they can become more productive and consistent offensively, this will be a very dangerous team. Their schedule is about to tighten up, so we’ll see how “for real” their undefeated start proves to be. 5. New England Patriots (4-2) Trending: Up At 1-2 and Drake Maye struggling, it must have felt like the sky was falling in New England. A three-game winning streak later, and the Patriots are just one game out of first place heading into a Thursday night showdown in Chicago. The talent is there, but health has been an issue. We’ll see if they can keep building on their current streak or come back down to earth in the coming weeks. 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Trending: Up Overall, the Jaguars have been one of the league’s more impressive teams. That said, they tend to play down to their competition, which has led to a few tight games. The talent is there, even if the defense isn’t as good as they showed last year. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has picked up where they left off, but it’s hard not to feel like they blew an opportunity to really run away with the NFC South on Sunday in London. 7. Green Bay Packers (4-2) Trending: Up After a shaky 1-2 start, the Packers have found their stride over the past two weeks, dominating both the Bears and Cowboys at home. Their schedule tightens with matchups against the Lions, Panthers, Patriots, Vikings, and Rams over the next six weeks. If they continue to play as they have, there’s reason to believe they’ll come out of that stretch with a winning record. 8. Detroit Lions (3-2) Trending: Up (if they can figure out their defense) There’s no questioning the offense at this point, but will the return of Brian Branch be enough to get their defense back on the right track? The NFC North is a gauntlet, and Detroit is the only team that hasn’t played a divisional game yet. That changes over the next two weeks with games against the Packers and Vikings. Their matchup against Green Bay will challenge this defense. We’ll see how they respond. 9. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) Trending: (Slightly) Up The Ravens are an odd team to track. On paper, they should be much more dominant than they are, but because of an injury to quarterback Lamar Jackson and their defensive inconsistencies, they’ve produced an up-and-down product so far. On paper, they are the best team in the AFC North. So far, they haven’t consistently played like it. Once Jackson is back, I expect them to round into form. 10. Chicago Bears (4-2) Trending : Up (Caleb Williams is back) Chicago is now 2-1 with Caleb Williams as their starting quarterback, and 2-1 with their backups. Some might look at that as an indictment of Williams, but a deeper dive into the offensive numbers tells a much different story. Assuming he can stay healthy, the primary concern will be the defense. They’ve been about as Jekyll and Hyde as it gets through six weeks. The talent is there, but the consistency has lacked. 11. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) Trending : Up (With some questions) The defense is clearly improved, and their two losses were against a pair of 4-2 teams. The issue is that their wins have come against teams with a combined 3-14 record. The talent is there, but so far, the weekly consistency hasn’t been. The Bengals remain one of the league’s more intriguing teams. 12. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) Trending : Down Coming into the season, Seattle was one of the more overlooked Super Bowl winners in recent history. Despite a strong start to the season, quarterback Sam Darnold has been turning the ball over at a highly concerning rate. The defense also hasn’t been nearly as dominant. It’s clear they miss running back Kenneth Walker, but the offense needs to figure it out soon if they plan to keep pace with San Francisco in the NFC West. 13. Denver Broncos (4-2) Trending : Teetering (without better QB play) The Broncos were a Bo Nix injury away from making it to the Super Bowl and at least being competitive. That feels weird to say, especially given how this season has started, but the offense has been an issue in almost all six of their games. It starts with quarterback play, but the run game has left a lot to be desired. It’s quite remarkable that they’ve been able to win four games playing like this, but it goes to show just how well-rounded this roster is. If Nix can figure it out, they might ultimately be the favorites in the AFC. 14. Cleveland Browns (4-2) Trending : Up (The league’s biggest surprise… So far) As usual, a few teams are surprises, and a few weeks ago, my vote would have been for the Raiders. That said, the Browns defense has continued to play at a high level without Myles Garrett, and their offense is doing just enough to win them games. No matter how the season ends, sitting at 4-2 and in first place is an outstanding start to the Todd Monken era. 15. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) Trending : Up (Somehow) Even without Mike Tomlin, this team feels eerily similar to the last 10 Steelers teams we’ve seen. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers continues to hang around and play well enough, and overall, they are getting enough from their aging roster to have a winning record. That said, I’m just not convinced this lasts over 17 games. We’ll see if they can last. 16. Carolina Panthers (3-2) Trending : Up Is Bryce Young a legitimate MVP candidate? It sure feels like it. In a weak NFC South, the Panthers are set up well to repeat. Really, the…

title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Falcons
summary: The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let’s get to it! 1. Competitive Fire Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, ‘want-to,’ whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) reacts during the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let’s get to it! 1. Competitive Fire Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, ‘want-to,’ whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the closing seconds, the Chicago Bears simply wanted this game more than Atlanta. Despite what many people realize, that matters even at this level. Chicago came out to play in this one, and you could tell it meant something to them in all three phases. I’d be remiss not to mention the masses of Bears fans that traveled to Atlanta for this one too. From the kickoff teams blowing up ball carriers, to the punt team perfectly executing some “Banana Balls” to Caleb Williams igniting the offense on the field or defense on the sidelines, these Bears were going to go down swinging. An encouraging sign after last week’s defeat at Lambeau. Zavier Scott looks like an absolute keeper on this team, and his juice on special teams stands out. Daniel Hardy had himself a game both in the third phase AND on Defense with Montez Sweat out. Noah Sewell made his presence felt as well and the contrast between what Kalif Raymond brings to what his predecessor Olamide Zacchaeus brought is night and day – and that’s only the reserve players! When you have your stars putting forth that same selfless effort to win games (spoiler alert – like the two guys listed below) then you have a fighters chance every week. And when your stars are as talented as they are in Chicago, good things can happen. REALLY good things. I might even call them super. 2. Iceman Caleb heard all the noise, yes. But in my opinion, his biggest motivating factor is and has always been winning ball games as starting quarterback and leading his team to new heights. Well, he made quite the impression Sunday, completing over 80% of his passes with zero turnovers and 1 TD pass, in addition to a career-best mark for consecutive completions with 12 straight complete throws. And that doesn’t count the multiple throw aways he had either. Caleb was on fire. When he is healthy and playing like that, this offense will be hard to stop. Remember, Chicago didn’t even have their RB1B in Kyle Monangai this week either. I said it on Bears Over Beers last week that I hoped he learned from Case Keenum how explosive this offense can be even without him playing Superman in the pocket and not only did he allude to it leading up to this game, but it showed on the field. Chicago has playmakers at each position. All he has to do is get it to them. On Sunday, he did just that with EIGHT players securing at least 2 catches. Caleb is back, people. Cannot wait to see him at home this week against last year’s MVP runner-up and fellow 2024 rookie classman, Drake Maye. Expect fireworks. 3. Spidey Not to be outdone by the epic return of Caleb Williams AKA Iceman, Kyler Gordon AKA “Spider Man” or “Spidey” had arguably the most impressive performance of the afternoon. Easing back into full-time action this week, Spidey played only 16 defensive snaps. In those snaps, he accumulated 4 tackles, 3 sacks, 3 tackles for a loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 2 QB hits. Spider Man is an absolute terror for opposing offenses, and we didn’t really even get to see him in coverage, where he is equally as dangerous. After all he’s been through with the public outcry over missing so much action and reports of tension in the locker room, it was huge to see his performance this week and earn himself a game ball from Ben Johnson postgame. With the struggles this defense has had to start the season, particularly in the secondary, Gordon’s return couldn’t have come at a better time as Chicago has the Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers before the Week 10 BYE – and ALL in Primetime. What about you? What stood out most in your mind when watching The Beloved come away with the win?

title: Report: Chicago Bears Jonah Jackson week-to-week with a hip flexor
summary: According to a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Chicago Bears starting right guard Jonah Jackson is dealing with a hip flexor and is considered week-to-week. Jackson left Sunday’s win against the Atlanta Falcons in the second half and was ruled doubtful to return. Second-year pro Luke Newman entered the game for Jackson and finished the game. […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears offensive line Jonah Jackson (73) against the New York Jets at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect According to a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , Chicago Bears starting right guard Jonah Jackson is dealing with a hip flexor and is considered week-to-week. Jackson left Sunday’s win against the Atlanta Falcons in the second half and was ruled doubtful to return. Second-year pro Luke Newman entered the game for Jackson and finished the game. Fowler added that Jackson’s availability for the Bears’ Thursday Night Game against the New England Patriots is “in doubt,” but the injury “shouldn’t be long-term.” Offensive coordinator Press Taylor met the media earlier today, and he discussed the possibility of replacing Jackson for Thursday’s game with either Newman or Jordan McFadden. “We’re excited about the depth we have,” Taylor said. Newman came in, did a good job to finish that game out for us. I think it’s worth noting McFadden started for us last year in the playoffs, and we were very comfortable with him starting at guard. And he did a good job in that game, so we’re excited about the depth of those guys. And we’ll see where Jonah’s at and if he’s got a chance to play on Thursday or not, but we are excited about some of the depth we have behind those guys as well on the inside.” The Bears did release an injury report today, allbeit it was just an estimation on how it would have been if they held more than a walk through, and Jackson was listed as a DNP with the hip and a quad injury. Also listed as did not practice were linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (consussion) and running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). Linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) and corner Tyrique Stevenson (hip) were listed on the injury report but as full participants. And that’s it. Quarterback Caleb Williams wasn’t listed at all.

title: Bears vs. Falcons Game Balls: Two Massive Returns
summary: I have been writing the game balls column here at Windy City Gridiron for the last three seasons, and these are easily the most obvious selections I have had over the course of that time period. The Chicago Bears marched into Atlanta, GA on Sunday for a crucial match-up with the Falcons that was going […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Chicago Bears defensive back Cam Lewis (21) and defensive back Kyler Gordon (6) celebrate during the third quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I have been writing the game balls column here at Windy City Gridiron for the last three seasons, and these are easily the most obvious selections I have had over the course of that time period. The Chicago Bears marched into Atlanta, GA on Sunday for a crucial match-up with the Falcons that was going to potentially set the tone for the rest of the season. Lose, and you find yourself at .500 with a tough schedule ahead. Win, and you have some key players back to potentially go on a run. For the most part, the Bears took control of the game and never looked back. They never trailed, and the game was seemingly never in doubt, except for a few minutes toward the end of the game when things got a little dicey due to the Bears substituting out their defensive starters a bit (a lot) early. Plus, there was a costly Roschon Johnson fumble. The return of superstar QB Caleb Williams went about as well as possible, and the defense came alive with the return of an often-injured but game-changing defensive back. Let’s get to the game balls! Offense Game Ball: QB Caleb Williams Duh. Williams came back with an edge, looking a bit more feisty than we’ve ever seen him. If it wasn’t made clear enough during his media availability during the week, it was certainly clear during the game on Sunday that Williams took everything that happened in his absence personal. He began his revenge tour at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Caleb Williams reaction after the TD. Goes up to Austin Booker fired up This man is coming back different pic.twitter.com/QLzN98s7FA — Dave (@davebftv) October 18, 2026 Caleb was intense and dialed in right from the start. He completed his first 12 passes in a row and ended the game 30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown pass. That was good for a 111.2 passer rating and a 52.2 QBR. Also of note: Williams’ touchdown pass was the 50th his of NFL career. In doing so, he became just the third QB in NFL history to throw for 50 touchdowns while having 15 or fewer interceptions. The other two? Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson. Look at these numbers while you’re at it: Caleb Williams was a perfect 24/24 for 248 yards from a clean pocket in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Falcons. His 24 attempts are the most without an incompletion from a clean pocket in a game since at least 2018. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/Vrx6fZNBRu — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 18, 2026 As far as game balls go, let’s give an honorable mention to Darnell Wright. He saw his QB take a cheap shot and retaliated with one of the damndest pancakes you will ever see. how about Darnell Wright getting some revenge. Jeff Joniak was speechless @darnellwright @JeffJoniak pic.twitter.com/E2UzVGeWRR — BEARSKIFILM (@BearskiFilm) October 18, 2026 Darnell Wright sent 25 to the shadow realm pic.twitter.com/iXQDLtDktf — Dave (@davebftv) October 18, 2026 Defense Game Ball: DB Kyler Gordon Once again, duh. It’s not a secret that Gordon is an impact player whenever he’s on the field. But just seeing him on the field has been a challenge the last couple years. This week, Gordon made more of an immediate impact in his first game back than he ever has before when returning from injury. Instead of playing primarily as a defensive back in coverage, Gordon was brought in by D.C. Dennis Allen in spots to rush the quarterback and wreak havoc in the backfield. He recorded three sacks, four tackles, three tackles for loss, two QB hits, and two forced fumbles. To give some context, Gordon’s three sacks were more than DE Montez Sweat has ever had had in game. The only other Bears defensive back to record three sacks in a game was Todd Bell on October 2, 1983. Gordon is also only the second DB in NFL history to record three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game, the other being Rod Kush who did it for the Houston Oilers on September 15, 1985. Gordon did all of this playing just 17 snaps on defense (nine on special teams). surprise! it's Kyler Gordon! pic.twitter.com/gTlaFaXI5k — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 19, 2026 WELCOME BACK, KYLER GORDON 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/mLaoOqQgPt — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 18, 2026 Bryan Orenchuk and myself will have plenty to say about this game this week on a new episode of Bears Over Beers on Wednesday evening. It will be available on the 2nd City Gridiron YouTube channel or via your favorite podcasting platform. title: Pro Football Focus hates Caleb Williams. He keeps balling anyway.
summary: At this point, it just feels personal from Pro Football Focus as far as Caleb Williams is concerned. Okay, not really. But these Week 6 grades just feel like trolling. When I saw that Williams, who completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown, wasn’t among the five highest-graded quarterbacks of the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after defeating the Atlanta Falcons in the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images At this point, it just feels personal from Pro Football Focus as far as Caleb Williams is concerned. Okay, not really . But these Week 6 grades just feel like trolling. When I saw that Williams, who completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown, wasn’t among the five highest-graded quarterbacks of the week— Drake Maye led the list with an offensive 92.1 grade —but J.J. McCarthy (74.3) did, I knew I was in for a laugh. I wasn’t (or was?) disappointed. Williams’ efforts, which included a perfect 24-of-24 passing from a clean pocket, earned him a 65.0 offensive grade, a 70.7 passing grade, and the cover photo of PFF’s “Statistical Review of NFL Week 6,” which takes us “ WAY beyond the box score ” (likely in an attempt to show us why Williams wasn’t as impressive as we think he was). We’ve already seen this from PFF in regards to Williams this season, as his Week 1 performance earned him a similarly “meh” grade despite 269 yards passing, four total touchdowns, and a passer rating of 124.1. And sure, aside from the 83.3% completion rate and clinical operation of the offense, the box score wasn’t that groundbreaking. Also, as the graders would likely point out, the four sacks he took in this game and high time-to-throw probably didn’t help his cause. That brings us back to the goalpost-moving when it comes to Williams’ game in general, and why he’s so difficult to quantify for conventional evaluators and social media naysayers alike. Last year, the knock on Williams was that he didn’t complete enough passes, despite being one of the most explosive playmakers in the game. Now that he’s cleaned that up—his 72.5% completion rate currently leads the NFL—he’s getting dinged for taking too many sacks, throwing the ball away too much when under duress, and not taking more chances down the field. It’s always something. He’s never going to be a statuesque surgeon from the pocket who lives by the 2.5-second stopwatch benchmark, either, which is going to make people question his decision-making when he holds the ball and creates. But no matter what the graders and haters say, he doesn’t have to. Though he’s had a limited sample size thus far in 2026 due to injury, Williams has shown he can improve the biggest area of need people identified for him heading into his third season: operating within structure. Give him a clean pocket, and he’ll destroy you in a way he might’ve struggled to last season. And you already know what he can do when it’s time to make magic. Bottom line: let the PFF graders talk about Williams however they want to. Let people talk down about him because of his passing charts. All of it is just fueling Williams to snatch souls and keep the Bears pushing toward Super Bowl contention. Hopefully, a date with Maye and the New England Patriots on Thursday night, two years after the Pats humbled Chicago at home, serves as more motivation to prove the doubters wrong. If these performances are “mid,” then I can’t wait to see what “good” looks like.

title: The 2026 Chicago Bears just had their statement game
summary: We just got our first glimpse of the real Chicago Bears on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. That statement doesn’t just reflect the fact that Chicago played arguably its most complete game of the season (notwithstanding the defense played by the backups in the fourth quarter) in their 31-23 win. It’s about who was on […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears looks on against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We just got our first glimpse of the real Chicago Bears on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. That statement doesn’t just reflect the fact that Chicago played arguably its most complete game of the season (notwithstanding the defense played by the backups in the fourth quarter) in their 31-23 win. It’s about who was on the field making that victory happen, and how. Yes, Caleb Williams was back, showing Bears fans what they were missing during his absence by completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. His perfect 24-of-24 completions on throws from a clean pocket in this game were the best mark by any quarterback since 2018—a testament to both his protection and his accuracy. His clinical operation of the offense helped the Bears possess the ball for more than 40 minutes and build a 31-7 lead at one point. But that wasn’t all. Kyler Gordon reminded everyone he’s one of the best nickel corners in the league when healthy, obliterating the Falcons offense for three sacks and forcing fumbles on two of them. Luther Burden III (eight catches for 95 yards) and Colston Loveland (six catches for 65 yards and a touchdown) had their way with a beleaguered Falcons secondary. Burden, in particular, continues to look like the clear WR1 for this Bears offense and is currently on pace for a 1,000-yard season. Ozzy Trapilo, against all odds, returned to action after suffering a torn patellar tendon nine months ago—still can’t get over that. Once he gets his legs under him, the 2025 second-round pick might regain his stranglehold on the starting left tackle spot, locking down Caleb Williams’ blind side opposite Darnell Wright. Rookie Logan Jones got some brief game action in relief of Garrett Bradbury, who has struggled often this season. While it’s no guarantee Jones will be the starter on Thursday night when the Bears face the Patriots, head coach Ben Johnson might be getting the team ready to make the change. While the Bears are still missing some notable contributors at the moment—Kyle Monangai, Montez Sweat, and TJ Edwards to name a few—this lineup, from the youth movement to missing game-changers like Gordon, is the one that will keep the Bears pushing toward the playoffs for the second year in a row. Will there be some growing pains along the way, especially for the young players? Probably. Not every defense the Bears face will be as amenable to getting scored on as Atlanta’s, for example. And, as we unfortunately were reminded of on Sunday, injuries are inevitable in this sport. Good health is far from guaranteed. But the Bears you saw on Sunday in Atlanta? That’s a playoff team. The fun part? They’re probably not even close to as good as they can be yet.
author: Khari Thompson

title: 10 Bears Takes: Caleb’s Comeback, Kyler’s Big Day, an Averted Collapse
summary: The seven-day break between their 31-7 beatdown loss in Green Bay and a second-straight game away from home in Atlanta was enough to make even the most level-headed of Bears fans lose it. In three hours, the Chicago Bears went from a great story that had started three quarterbacks in four weeks to a team […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 and Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The seven-day break between their 31-7 beatdown loss in Green Bay and a second-straight game away from home in Atlanta was enough to make even the most level-headed of Bears fans lose it. In three hours, the Chicago Bears went from a great story that had started three quarterbacks in four weeks to a team that might not be very good. As usual, the narratives fly any time those two teams play, which can make it hard for anyone to turn the page. Luckily for head coach Ben Johnson and his team, they did just that. It helped that they got their starting quarterback back in the mix, but for the better part of four quarters, they looked like the same dominant team we’ve seen in four of their six games so far in 2026. Before quickly turning the page on this one for a Thursday night showdown with the New England Patriots, let’s take a deeper dive into Sunday and where they go next in Week 6’s edition of 10 Bears Takes. 1. Caleb Williams’ return on Sunday was much-needed, even after a weird media session earlier in the week– why fans should feel optimistic about his play after a three-game absence. Williams ended last week’s Friday practice session as a limited participant, before doing plenty of work in Green Bay before the start of last weekend’s game. Speculation all along has been that he would be close to ready for Atlanta, and despite a Wednesday walk-through, it was clear they felt they had given Williams’ hamstring injury enough time and were ready to ramp him up. Then came Thursday, when his first media day in three weeks featured a long opening speech, some pointed statements, and a somewhat contentious set of answers. As always, people rarely take things at face value. Instead, everyone runs with their reactions, and it blows up into something bigger than it was. In the end, Williams came out on Sunday with some clear motivation to prove his critics wrong and did exactly that. His 83.3% completion rate was a career-high, and he eclipsed 300 passing yards for just the sixth time in his career. Taking out the anomaly that was the Vikings game in Week 2, so far we’ve seen a new version of Williams where he’s not wildly missing throws. Even more impressive, he’s continued to take what the defense is giving him. Even if those checkdowns aren’t turning into explosives, they are keeping opposing defenses honest, which is allowing for more shots downfield. To dive a little deeper into his six incompletions: four were throwaways, one was Colston Loveland overrunning a route in the end zone, and the last was a pass where his arm was hit mid-throw. Simply put, he didn’t come close to putting the ball into danger, and there were no egregious misses as we saw so often last season. Even though the offense scored 31 points, it’s easy to see how much was once again left out on the field. Between the penalties and missed opportunities in Atlanta territory, there’s plenty of meat left on the bone for this offense to continue to get better. That should give fans plenty of faith that they’ll keep improving as a unit, and ultimately, 40-point games are far from out of the question moving forward. No matter how you slice it, it was a great return for the Bears’ franchise quarterback. More importantly, the best is yet to come for this offense, assuming their core pieces stay healthy through the last 11 regular-season games. 2. Speaking of returns, Kyler Gordon’s first game of 2026 was a stark reminder that when he’s healthy, he’s one of their best defenders. Much has been made about his recent injury history and lack of ability. Frankly, it’s been justified considering these issues started after he signed his lucrative extension to make him the highest-paid nickel in the league. Despite his lack of availability going back to the start of last season, it’s impossible to debate that when he’s in the game, he’s one of, if not the best defensive players the team has. Gordon was activated off PUP earlier this week, which made Sunday his first game of the 2026 season. Despite only playing 16 defensive snaps, his three sacks and two forced fumbles were the most that have been tracked from a defensive back dating all the way back to 1982. Even if Gordon isn’t the most dynamic coverage guy in the league, his versatility is a huge value to any defense. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has always been known for getting the most out of his nickelbacks, and when Gordon has been on the field, the results have been no different. With the team’s secondary in flux due to injuries and their mix-and-match style, fans can expect Gordon’s snap count to rise each game until he’s settled into a full-time role. That likely means Tyrique Stevenson will go back to the bench, but considering how much both he and Jaylon Johnson have struggled down the field, I’m not sure that’s a bad thing. Fourth-round rookie Malik Muhammad should continue to see snaps on the boundary, and if that’s the end goal for him beyond this season, it makes sense to continue to play him there. We’ll see how things look once everyone is healthy (if that ever happens), but the offseason plan is starting to show. Once Coby Bryant comes back (hopefully this season), this could be a very different-looking group than the one we saw to open up Week 1. 3. With a short week upcoming, it will be hard for this team not to look too far ahead to their 10-day mini-bye. It might only be six games into the regular season, but these last few weeks have taken a toll on this team’s health. It started with Braxton Jones a few weeks ago, and has since led to Dayo Odeyingbo going on Injured Reserve, while other players like T.J. Edwards, Stevenson, and even Kyle Monangai are on the “week-to-week” timeline. At first glance, the only notable injury the team sustained on Sunday was right guard Jonah Jackson leaving with a hip injury. I guess that we won’t get a better idea of what that injury looks like until closer to their game on Thursday, but combine that with Montez Sweat’s suspension, and this team is missing a lot of starting talent heading into their Thursday night showdown with a very good Patriots club. The Bears are in the midst of a tough three-game stretch that started with a road game in Atlanta, followed by a short turnaround with the Patriots, and then a Monday night showdown with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. Before their win in Atlanta, going 2-1 felt like the “goal”. It would leave them at 5-3 overall, and ideally, it would give them tie-breakers over Carolina, Philadelphia, Atlanta, and Seattle, plus a 4-2 conference record heading into a stretch where they’ll see a 1-5 Buccaneers team, a Week 9 bye, followed by another favorable matchup against a 2-4 Saints team. That said, Week 9’s bye feels like a long time away, which means the early focus will be on getting through Thursday night and hoping for improved health during their 10-game break before heading to Seattle to face the Seahawks. No one would blame the Bears for looking ahead, and ultimately, if they can get some other important pieces back, it’s a win. The goal now should be to get as many wins as possible before heading into the bye week. For instance, going into their bye week at 6-3 would put them in a prime position to push for the division, or at least a playoff spot, heading into the second half of the season. The regular season is in full swing, and the Bears, like every other team in the league, must find a way to weather the storm and come out better on the other side. A small reprieve is just days away, but first, there’s a big game on a national stage waiting for them at Soldier Field on Thursday night. 4. Following an ugly 31-7…

title: Bears vs. Falcons: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and Caleb Williams’ Completion Percentage
summary: The Atlanta Falcons tried to make that one interesting, but the Chicago Bears regrouped and slammed the door on the Falcons’ comeback attempt, winning 31 to 23. The Bears pulled the defensive starters in the fourth quarter while up by 24, but had to put them back in to close out the game after a […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams (18) drops back to pass during the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons tried to make that one interesting, but the Chicago Bears regrouped and slammed the door on the Falcons’ comeback attempt, winning 31 to 23. The Bears pulled the defensive starters in the fourth quarter while up by 24, but had to put them back in to close out the game after a Falcons score and a Bears fumble. Head coach Ben Johnson addressed his end-of-game thinking about trying to win while also resting his players with the New England Patriots coming to town on Thursday Night Football. “I mean, you’re trying to thread the needle a little bit. If we didn’t have the Thursday night game, I don’t know that we’d do things like we did,” he said . “So that’s part of the equation. I do believe if we hadn’t had that fumble on offense (Roshon Johnson had it punched out with 7:21 left in the game) that maybe we would have gotten out of there the way that we wanted to, but you know, things happen and we got to keep playing. We know that’s the case, especially with an offense like that. So, once again, we’re trying to thread the needle and do what’s best for us. We had to win this game first and foremost, which we did, but of course, we want to think long term also.” Johnson’s fumble came at midfield after picking up the first down, so they likely could have run some more clock, which was something they were good at in the game, having the time of possession edge (40:08 to 19:52). The Bears also had more yards (368 to 257), more first downs (20 to 13), and ran more plays (73 to 50), but they also committed far more penalties (12-133 to 4-31). Chicago had the turnover edge (3 to 1) and were much better on third downs (52.9% to 25.0%). The Bears’ defense also stopped Atlanta on all three of their fourth-down attempts. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing-time breakdown and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE We’ve only seen Caleb Williams in two full games and part of another one in a steady rain, but he’s leveled up his play. He’s still pushing the ball downfield, but he’s taking the check-down when it’s there more often, as his league-leading 72.5 completion percentage can attest. According to Next Gen Stats, Williams was 24 of 24 for 248 yards on throws from a clean pocket in Atlanta, and those 24 attempts are the most without an incompletion from a clean pocket in a game since at least 2018. Kudos to the game plan, which featured more quick passes from the pocket; possibly to take some stress off his hamstring. His average depth of target (3.6) was the second-lowest of his career; we saw fewer rollouts, and he scrambled only once for 2 yards. His completion percentage (83.3%) in Atlanta was the best ever by a Bears quarterback with at least 30 passing attempts. Four of his 6 incompletions were on throwaways. Another was on a play where he was hit. Then there was the goal-line miss, where he threw the ball expecting Colston Loveland to settle near the sideline. Pretty, pretty, pretty, pretty good, despite what some of the rage-bait haters are trying to say about him now being a checkdown merchant. The goalposts will constantly move when it comes to Caleb, and I think he likes it. He is inevitable after all. #Bears left tackle Ozzy Trapilo on playing Sunday for the first time since his patellar tendon injury in January. “It was great. It was good to be back out there, it’s been a long time coming.” pic.twitter.com/22up5nK3bT — Michal Dwojak (@mdwojak94) October 18, 2026 DEFENSE The Bears were without defensive starters linebacker T.J. Edwards, cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, and defensive linemen Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo, so Dennis Allen dialed up some blitzes, and defensive backs recorded 4 of their 5 sacks. Rookie Dillon Thieneman recorded his first sack. Kyler Gordon’s stat line in his return was unreal, but lost in his overall game impact was the holding penalty he drew blitzing off the edge. Dennis Allen did a great job showing blitz, getting the Falcons to commit the pass protection one way, then sending free rushers or players with favorable one-on-ones. SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was wide left on a 56-yarder and made a 50-yarder. He hit all 4 extra points. Tory Taylor had 5 punts with a 44.8 average (41.0 net), and 3 punts inside the twenty. Josh Blackwell had 2 special teams tackles and recovered a fumble after Taylor’s banana-ball punt caused a muff. Zavion Thomas returned 4 kickoffs for 85 yards. Kalif Raymond had 3 punt returns for 54 yards. Chicago’s practice squad call-ups both scratched the stat sheet on special teams. Zavier Scott forced a fumble and made 3 tackles, and Buddy Johnson made 2 tackles. To check out the complete Bears vs. Falcons box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Bengals progress report: Grading special teams
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 3-2 coming out of their bye week, and depending on which side of the bed you wake up on, there’s plenty of reason for optimism or pessimism. The offense has had its moments. The defense has had its moments. Unfortunately, so have the special teams, and not necessarily in a good […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 3-2 coming out of their bye week, and depending on which side of the bed you wake up on, there’s plenty of reason for optimism or pessimism. The offense has had its moments. The defense has had its moments. Unfortunately, so have the special teams, and not necessarily in a good way. Outside of Evan McPherson, who apparently decided missing field goals is for lesser mortals, Darrin Simmons’ special teams units have been a frustrating combination of mediocrity and outright disaster. Let’s start with the one guy who’s been keeping the lights on. Field Goal/Field Goal Block With 11 guys on the field working together, every play has a lot of moving pieces, but the field-goal unit is fairly simple. As long as the long snapper, holder, and kicker do their jobs, everyone else just needs to keep the defense out of the way for a second or two. Outside of a penalty that pushed the Bengals out of field-goal range, Evan McPherson and the rest of the field-goal unit have been perfect. McPherson now owns the franchise record for most consecutive field goals made with 22, a streak that stretches back to the 2025 season. In 2026, McPherson is a perfect 10-for-10. What’s most impressive, though, is that five of those kicks have come from 50 or more yards, with a long of 58. Obviously, the offense wants to walk away from every drive with seven points, but that’s not always possible. The Bengals are extremely fortunate to have a kicker who is so accurate from beyond 50 yards. Nobody really cares about the kicker until a field goal can win or lose the game in the final minutes. On the defensive side of things, the only major issue so far this season came in Week 5. Dexter Lawrence was flagged for roughing the snapper against the Dolphins, giving Miami a fresh set of downs after a successful field goal. The Dolphins eventually scored a touchdown, turning three points into seven. The Bengals won that game, but those four additional points helped keep Miami within striking distance late in the fourth quarter. Field Goal Unit: 98% (A+) Field Goal Block Unit: 85% (B) Overall Field Goal Unit: 92% (A-) Punt/Punt Return Here’s where the real problems begin. As far as punt coverage goes, the first major mistake came in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals’ defense stopped Pittsburgh in the third quarter and forced a punt, but Cedric Johnson was called for an obvious roughing-the-kicker penalty. That gave the Steelers a fresh set of downs, and what should have been a defensive stop turned into a Pittsburgh touchdown a few plays later. In the same game, former punt returner Ke’Shawn Williams muffed a punt that Pittsburgh recovered at the Bengals’ 14-yard line. The defense managed to hold the Steelers to a field goal, but instead of Cincinnati getting the ball back with an opportunity to score, Pittsburgh walked away with three points. Those two mistakes handed the Steelers possessions that resulted in 10 points in a game the Bengals lost by three. Ryan Rehkow’s punting, meanwhile, has been unspectacular. His 44.9 yards-per-punt average ranks among the lowest in the NFL. Nine of his 16 punts have been downed inside the 20-yard line, and he hasn’t recorded a touchback. There haven’t been any major mistakes on Rehkow’s part, but his overall production has been below average. The real issue with this unit isn’t necessarily the punter. It’s the mistakes being made around him. A roughing penalty and a muffed punt aren’t just bad plays. They’re the kinds of mistakes that can cost a team a game, and against Pittsburgh, they helped do exactly that. Punting Unit: 74% (C) Punt Return Unit: 49% (F) Overall Punting grade: 61 (D-) Kickoff/Kickoff Return Kickoffs are so different now than they used to be. With touchbacks generally bringing the ball out to the 35-yard line, teams have more incentive to kick short of the end zone and force a return. That means more opportunities for explosive plays, but it also means more opportunities for mistakes. For the Bengals, the most glaring mistake came in Week 5 against the Dolphins. Rookie wide receiver Dohnte Meyers fielded a kickoff at the four-yard line, but his momentum carried him out of bounds almost immediately, setting Joe Burrow and the offense up in the shadow of their own goalposts. The offense managed to move the ball out near midfield, but the drive ultimately ended with a punt. While the mistake didn’t directly cost Cincinnati points, it put the offense in a difficult position and eliminated any chance of starting that possession with favorable field position. To be fair, Meyers also started that game with an 81-yard kickoff return that set the Bengals up at Miami’s 10-yard line. Burrow and the offense took advantage, scoring a touchdown just three plays later. That’s the frustrating thing about the kickoff return unit. There’s clearly potential for big plays, but the execution hasn’t always been consistent. On the coverage side, the Bengals haven’t suffered any major breakdowns comparable to what we’ve seen from the punt units. They’ve generally done a respectable job of limiting opposing returners and avoiding the kind of disastrous plays that can completely flip field position. Kickoff Unit Grade: 82% (B-) Kickoff Return Unit Grade: 79% (C+) Overall Kickoff/Return Grade: 80% (B -) Darrin Simmons has been the Bengals’ special teams coordinator since 2003. He was named assistant head coach in 2020 and has held both positions ever since. Special teams typically haven’t been a major problem for the Bengals under Simmons, but this season has been different. Outside of McPherson, the unit has made several costly mistakes, and some have had a direct impact on the outcome of games. Look no further than Pittsburgh. The Bengals lost that game by three points, and two special teams mistakes gave the Steelers possessions that resulted in 10 points. It’s impossible to say with certainty how the game would have unfolded without those errors, but it’s hard not to wonder what Cincinnati’s record would look like if those mistakes hadn’t happened. It’s not all on Simmons. Players have to execute, and there are only so many things a coach can control once the ball is snapped. However, Simmons is responsible for preparing his units, and right now, those units aren’t consistently getting the job done. A 4-1 record, including a 1-0 start in the division, would sound a hell of a lot better than 3-2. Hopefully, the Bengals got things straightened out during the bye week. Because without McPherson’s excellence, Cincinnati’s special teams would be earning a solid D. Overall Defensive Grade: 77% C

title: DJ Turner is having a good season, even if you’re not noticing it
summary: A sign of a great cornerback is if you don’t notice him. It sounds weird, but if you don’t notice him, it means that the opposing quarterback isn’t throwing in his direction. Bengals cornerback DJ Turner hasn’t been noticed in most of the Bengals’ first five games this season. The only time he really has […]
full_text: A sign of a great cornerback is if you don’t notice him. It sounds weird, but if you don’t notice him, it means that the opposing quarterback isn’t throwing in his direction. Bengals cornerback DJ Turner hasn’t been noticed in most of the Bengals’ first five games this season. The only time he really has was when he drew a holding call against DK Metcalf late in the game at the Steelers in Week 3. Turner hasn’t let potential distractions regarding a contract extension impact him, and that goes all the way back to this offseason. The proof has been in his play so far this season. Bengals CB DJ Turner is making a strong case to be a potential All-Pro corner this year. Has been very sticky in coverage and surrendered very few yards per coverage snap. (also: MY WORD, Trent McDuffie!!) pic.twitter.com/fMd5xS6B8l — Ben Baby (@Ben_Baby) October 14, 2026 For those in the analytics crowd, this is for you. Admittedly, I’m not an analytics guy. But this illustrates the season Turner is having through five games. He’s allowing barely a half-yard per coverage snap, which is impressive. Turner has five passes defensed this season and 12 tackles. Impressively, nine of those are solo tackles.

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will be heading to take on the Baltimore Ravens this week for their second AFC North game of the season. The Ravens just lost 13-10 to the Cleveland Browns, but the big news there was quarterback Lamar Jackson missing his second game in a row with an ankle sprain. Here is what head coach Jesse Minter had to say after his quarterback was ruled out on Friday : “It’s day-by-day, I would say,” Minter said on Friday. “I think it’s just a decision for [Lamar Jackson]’s best interest. That’s really what every decision’s always going to be about.” The team seemed optimistic that Jackson would be ready for the Browns game on Sunday, but that obviously did not come to pass. It is important to consider that his recovery time might take a bit longer, as his best quality is his dual threat to run and pass. If Jackson isn’t 100 percent as a runner, it makes things a lot easier for the defense he is facing. title: Bengals vs. Ravens odds: Opening lines for Week 7 may hint at Lamar Jackson’s status
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week with a 3-2 record and are hopefully healthy, rested, and have all their kinks ironed out. They’re 0-1 in the AFC North, having lost to the Steelers in Week 3, but will get a chance to even their division record out in Week 7 when they […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week with a 3-2 record and are hopefully healthy, rested, and have all their kinks ironed out. They’re 0-1 in the AFC North, having lost to the Steelers in Week 3, but will get a chance to even their division record out in Week 7 when they travel to Baltimore to face the 4-2 Ravens. The Ravens are coming off a division loss of their own, dropping an ugly 13-10 loss to the Browns in Cleveland, but they’ve been without two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, who suffered a rare medial sprain of his left ankle in Week 4. Jackson missed the entire week of practice before the Ravens’ Week 6 game and was ruled out prior to the game. It’s unclear as to whether or not he’ll be available against the Bengals, but his projected return is Week 7 or Week 8. As of right now, the Bengals are going into their Week 7 game as three-point underdogs in Baltimore, according to the FanDuel Sportsbook . This makes sense if Lamar plays, considering the ups and downs we’ve seen from both the Bengals’ offense and defense so far this season. But if Tyler Huntley were to start, the Bengals would likely be favored. If nothing else, the game would be closer to a pick ‘em, so it seems like the oddsmakers expect Lamar to suit up. Hopefully, the bye week gave Cincinnati time to figure things out. Stay tuned throughout the week for updates on both the Bengals and Ravens before their Week 7 matchup on Sunday in Baltimore. title: Browns offense still needs a spark, but these two players stepped up against Ravens
summary: There’s something about the Browns’ offense in the second half that gets clicking. 237 yards of offense on the day doesn’t sound too impressive, but take into consideration that they only had 46 yards of offense in the first half. Ultimately, they actually out-gained the Ravens, thanks to a strong defensive performance. The team playing […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Jaleel McLaughlin #38 of the Cleveland Browns runs the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the fourth quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something about the Browns’ offense in the second half that gets clicking. 237 yards of offense on the day doesn’t sound too impressive, but take into consideration that they only had 46 yards of offense in the first half. Ultimately, they actually out-gained the Ravens, thanks to a strong defensive performance. The team playing complete football (i.e. sticking with things to the end) has worked for four close victories, but to take the next step, they have to obviously break out of that trend to the upside. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 6 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 63 100% 16-of-26 (61.5%) for 164 yards. 8 carries, 29 yards (3.6 YPC). It’s tough to say whether things are processing slower for Deshaun Watson , or if players simply weren’t getting open and he doesn’t want to force the turnover because of that. The announcers kept calling out that players weren’t open, and the few replays that they showed were indicating that as well. I think it’s a mixture of both. I don’t see panic from Watson, but at times, he takes off with what looks to be a decent opening to get some positive yardage. That has worked against some teams, but against the Ravens, their defensive front seemed quicker to close the gap and prevent him from escaping. So if that’s the case against a certain defense, Watson has to discover that balance of perhaps hanging in an extra tick and delivering the ball somewhere. I feel like part of the problem was the gameplan to try pushing the ball downfield too much early. Watson has been at his most efficient when he mixes in short read passes through his progressions with the intermediate throws, which we saw him get back to in the second half. PFF graded Watson out to a 56.4 on the day. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Jaleel McLaughlin 39 62% 9 carries, 41 yards (4.6 YPC). 4 catches, 14 yards (4 targets). RB Audric Estime 19 30% 9 carries, 19 yards (2.1 YPC), 1 TD. FB Michael Burton 10 16% 1 carry, 2 yards (2.0 YPC). 0 catches (1 target). It was a solid running day for Jaleel McLaughlin , who offers that ability to shift his way through a small gap. Again, it wasn’t anything crazy, but it was something that made me feel like we have a chance on squeezing some extra yards out via the ground. I feel like Quinshon Judkins would’ve been stuck in that 3.0 YPC territory on those same plays, based on how he’s played this year. McLaughlin was the Browns’ second-highest graded player on offense, grading out to a 76.6. Audric Estime , just signed, got the team’s lone touchdown of the day down at the goal line. Fullback Michael Burton got his first touch of the season, moving the chains on a fourth down play off of a fullback handoff. Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 58 92% 1 catch, 15 yards (5 targets). WR KC Concepcion 51 81% 4 catches, 37 yards (6 targets). 2 carries, 2 yards (2.0 YPC). WR Jerry Jeudy 39 62% 4 catches, 69 yards (4 targets). WR Tylan Wallace 10 16% 1 catch, 12 yards (1 target). WR Isaiah Bond 9 14% No stats registered. WR Malachi Corley 7 11% No stats registered. Welcome back, Jerry Jeudy , He secured the passes thrown to him well, and they all seemed to come at big moments. His snap count usage ticked up a hair from two weeks ago, and he was the Browns’ top-graded receiver this week by PFF, with a grade of 76.1. KC Concepcion also had a big catch late off of a short laser. I liked trying to incorporate him on a jet sweep, but the defensive back played it well. Cleveland was also going to try a trick play with him throwing the ball, but he wisely aborted the play when it was covered. It was the first game where Denzel Boston was a relative non-factor, although Watson did try to loft a touchdown pass to him in the fourth quarter (but it was out of bounds). Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 56 89% 1 catch, 9 yards (3 targets). TE Blake Whiteheart 17 27% 1 catch, 8 yards (1 target). Not much action for the tight ends again this week. After a relatively hot start for Harold Fannin , it seems unusual to not have him targeted or involved much the past two weeks offensively, despite all the snaps he plays. He ended up being the lowest-graded player on offense by PFF, grading out to a 51.6. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 63 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 63 100% OL Austin Barber 63 100% OL Zion Johnson 63 100% OL Tytus Howard 63 100% The offensive line was healthy and played the whole game. Cleveland allowed 5 sacks on the day, but PFF only charged one of those to the offensive line (being on C Elgton Jenkins ). The Browns’ top-graded player on offense this week? Left guard Zion Johnson , although it was mostly for his run-blocking grade, as his pass blocking grade was below everybody else. Tytus Howard and Austin Barber also received solid grades for their job against the Ravens.

full_text: As much as the NFL dominates the sports calendar, it is the shortest season of the three historically major sports in the United States. It seems like just yesterday the Cleveland Browns were setting their initial 53-man roster and getting ready for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season . The Browns are now six games into their season, have crossed the quarter pole of the year a couple of weeks ago, and have two other schedule markers just ahead: The NFL trade deadline and their bye week. Could GM Andrew Berry be big game hunting at the deadline, with the potential of a very high pick coming from the Los Angeles Rams due to injury ? Will the roster be resting up for a late playoff push? Will fans, and Cleveland natives like Jason Kelce , have the Browns on their minds at Thanksgiving with family? Here is Cleveland’s schedule, including the deadline and bye week, heading into Turkey Day: 10/25: Away versus the Tennessee Titans 11/1: Away versus the Pittsburgh Steelers 11/8: Away versus the New Orleans Saints 11/10: NFL trade deadline at 4 PM Eastern 11/15: At home versus the Houston Texans 11/22: Bye Week 11/26: Thanksgiving Day A lot to happen between the end of Week 6 and Thanksgiving, especially with three straight road games. The positives are facing the one-win Titans, the Steelers the week after they return from the first game in Paris (amid civil unrest happening in France), and a Saints team that has seen QB Tyler Shough come back to earth pretty quickly. Winning two or all of their next three games could give Berry even more confidence to be aggressive at the deadline. The bye week happening later in the season could give the young Browns roster a chance to recover and any new additions more time to get acclimated to the team. If all that happens, Cleveland fans will be stuffing their faces with good food on Thanksgiving while opening their mouths to talk nothing but the Browns. I believe the young folk call that “wishcasting.” What jumps out to you about the upcoming Browns schedule until Thanksgiving? Join the conversation! summary: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2, and the bandwagon has room for a lot more to jump on or return to the orange and brown of their youth. While the Browns four wins have not been pretty, with all of them (and the loss to the New York Jets) potentially going the other way, learning to […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2 , and the bandwagon has room for a lot more to jump on or return to the orange and brown of their youth. While the Browns four wins have not been pretty, with all of them (and the loss to the New York Jets) potentially going the other way, learning to win is an important skill for a very young team to learn. Can Cleveland sustain this ? Are the Browns the biggest frauds in the NFL ? Who cares? At least for now, Cleveland fans have something to be excited about, including Jason Kelce. Growing up Browns fans, Jason’s brother Travis begged the team to draft him when he was coming out of the University of Cincinnati. Travis has also been a regular at many other Cleveland teams’ games and bought a ownership stake in the Cleveland Guardians. Jason has been a little less Cleveland-forward in his presentation, until Monday Night Football when he started using the term “we” and a lot of excitement to describe the Browns start to the season: Cleveland native @JasonKelce had a lot to get off his chest after the Browns' 4-2 start 😭 pic.twitter.com/UNHxQDUcT1 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 19, 2026 Given the Browns positive start, it is possible that the team could get their scheduled flexed in the near future, but probably not to Kelce’s Monday Night Football just yet. No matter what, a fun thing for Cleveland natives and fans is that the Browns are 4-2 and at the top of the AFC North. It is a big deal to see the elder Kelce join his brother in embracing the “we” that is their Cleveland upbringing. That moniker used to only be used by Jason for the Philadelphia Eagles. full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have won four of their last five games to reach first place in the AFC North Division. This is rarefied air for the Browns, as they have not been in first place this late in a season since the 2014 season. That was so long ago that rookie left tackle Spencer Fano, the youngest player on the current, was just 9 years old at the time. Cleveland has done it with an offense that has been good enough when the situation called for it, and a defense that has exerted its will on opposing offenses. (At least once the game’s first series is in the books.) There are a lot of numbers that stand out when it comes to the defense, but there is one area in particular that we want to highlight. The Carolina Panthers have scored more than 30 points three times this season, and put up 25 on Sunday against Philadelphia. But against the Browns? Just 18 points. The Baltimore Ravens had put up 30, 41, and 30 points in the three games that quarterback Tyler Huntley started before Sunday’s game. But against the Browns? Just 10 points, and none after the third quarter. At some point, the offense will have to carry the water for more than just the fourth quarter. But, for now, the defense deserves every bit of credit it can claim for helping a team with a -16 point differential find its way into first place. title: More major Rams injuries could boost Browns 2027 NFL draft pick position
summary: When the Cleveland Browns traded DE Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams this summer, many talked about the NFL draft picks coming back as “basically (a round later)” due to assumptions about the outcome of the 2026 NFL season. Then the Rams lost and lost Garrett in Week 1, dealt with an injury to […]
full_text: When the Cleveland Browns traded DE Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams this summer, many talked about the NFL draft picks coming back as “basically (a round later)” due to assumptions about the outcome of the 2026 NFL season. Then the Rams lost and lost Garrett in Week 1 , dealt with an injury to WR Puka Nacua , saw DT Aaron Donald miss a game , and dropped to 2-4 after Week 6 . Through six weeks, Los Angeles’ first-round pick coming back to Cleveland is closer to the Top 5 than the team is to making the NFL playoffs. Garrett has not returned to practice yet, and now the Rams are dealing with four other major injuries, starting with WR Davante Adams being out potentially to the end of the season: Bad to worse: #Rams star WR Davante Adams, who sustained a hamstring injury in last night’s loss to the #AZCardinals , is out 6-10 weeks. pic.twitter.com/FO80VAb5NM — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 19, 2026 On top of that, DT Poona Ford ruptured his triceps and will miss the rest of the season, with fellow DT Kobie Turner set to miss four to six weeks with a groin injury. The icing on the cake is that newly signed kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL making a tackle and will now miss the rest of the season. Let’s see if we have the injury roundup correct: Best defensive lineman in the NFL (Garrett) still not back from surgery One of the best route runners and redzone threats (Adams) out for most of the season 2 very good defensive tackles injured, with one (Ford) out for the year and the other (Turner) missing a month to a month and a half Second kicker of the year is now out, and a third will need to be signed Given their 2-4 record and all of these injuries, where do you think the Rams finish the season? full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 07: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks to pass during the third quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 07, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns opened as 1.5-point road favorites against the Tennessee Titans ahead of their Week 7 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under on the game is 37.5. The Browns (4-2) are coming off of a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens . It was a unique game for the team, as the defense allowed 10 first quarter points, but then pitched a shutout the rest of the way, including forcing a key turnover on RB Derrick Henry . The offense, meanwhile, was a mess to the point where it seemed like no one could get open. Then, in the second half, they gained a little traction, before the momentum swung further in their favor half-way through the fourth quarter. The Browns now lead the AFC North, and are favorites for the first time in seven games, due to the quality of their opponent. The Titans (1-5) are coming off of a 26-20 win against the Indianapolis Colts for their first win of the season. They were dominated in the first half, being down 13-0, before scoring 20 unanswered in the second half, and tacking on a few more field goals, to win for the first time. However, they were out-gained in yards 399 to 186, and QB Cam Ward was 11-of-22 for 102 yards. The game seemed more like an indictment on the state of the Colts than good play from Tennessee. They rank at the bottom of the league in offense, so Cleveland should be ready to feast. Even with the Browns being on the road, it makes sense for them to finally be favorites here. title: NFL trade deadline: Browns might have some big-game options if they go hunting
summary: With six weeks down in the 2026 NFL season, there are not a lot of things that are certain around the NFL. Can the Cleveland Browns hold on to the top spot in the AFC North, or are they the biggest frauds among the good records in the league? Almost every team still has similar […]
full_text: With six weeks down in the 2026 NFL season, there are not a lot of things that are certain around the NFL. Can the Cleveland Browns hold on to the top spot in the AFC North , or are they the biggest frauds among the good records in the league? Almost every team still has similar or bigger questions than those that surround the Browns, but some teams are already at the point of knowing their season is likely heading toward a high 2027 NFL draft pick . The Los Angeles Chargers are winless, the Philadelphia Eagles lost QB Jalen Hurts for the season due to blood clots, the Indianapolis Colts just fired their general manager, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Washington Commanders have one win each despite preseason expectations, and the Los Angeles Rams are closer to a Top 5 pick than a playoff spot currently . The Miami Dolphins are also winless, but that was to be expected, and they traded away much of their veteran talent already. While Week 6 may have proven why WR Jerry Jeudy may not actually be available for teams, no matter the fit , the Browns win might have accelerated GM Andrew Berry’s desire to add talent to the roster . Given all of the struggling teams above, Cleveland could go “big-game hunting” during the ramp-up to the NFL trade deadline next month. Whether reported, rumored, or just suggested, the Browns could have a plethora of available talent if they want to get aggressive with the cupboard full of draft picks Berry has accumulated. Browns potential trade targets RB Saquon Barkley The Eagles are no longer competitive and RB Quinshon Judkins has struggled this year. When healthy, Barkley is one of the best all-purpose backs in the league, but he’s also about to turn 30, has been used heavily, and has had a myriad of health issues in his career. With just $2.5 million guaranteed left on his contract, the Eagles might be looking to move the running back a year early. DE Khalil Mack We’ve covered the possibility of trading for Mack multiple times . It still seems like a good option for, likely, nothing more than a Day 3 pick. RB Jonathan Taylor and DE/DT Deforest Buckner Taylor is another big-name running back option, while Buckner would add more flexible talent to the defensive line: It'll be interesting to see if pricey Colts veterans like DeForest Buckner and Jonathan Taylor now become available for trade. Remember, Miami moved guys after firing GM Chris Grier before the deadline last year. — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) October 19, 2026 Guard Quinton Nelson has also been mentioned as a potential trade candidate from Indianapolis, but Cleveland seems unlikely to add at that position at this point. DE Dorance Armstrong A smaller name compared to the above, finding an edge rusher available in a trade is tough. Armstrong is not having a great statistical season, but is an experienced pass rusher with five or more sacks in each of the last five seasons. The Commanders seem headed nowhere, but the NFC East is too weak for them to sell early. DE Tuli Tuipulotu Perhaps the most expensive trade value on this list, Tuipulotu is in the last year of his rookie contract after having 13 sacks last year and 8.5 the year before. Could Berry work on a trade and sign deal for a young pass rusher with upside? If the Chargers decide to sell completely, or the Browns blow them away, Tuipulotu will be at the top of most teams’ want lists. Big names are always exciting for fan and media conversations. Cleveland might get involved with some of the guys above, but adding a really good blocking tight end might have a bigger impact, at least this season. For now, the 4-2 record makes it at least interesting to imagine what Berry might be able to pull off to add to the Browns roster. Do you think the Browns should aggressively add any of the names above? Any other big game-type players they should pursue that could be available? Join the conversation! full_text: After the Cleveland Browns’ 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens , they now sit atop the AFC North with a 4-2 record . The AFC North remains extremely competitive, with Baltimore and the Pittsburgh Steelers both holding 4-2 records and the Cincinnati Bengals trailing closely behind at 3-2. Only the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs have better records than the Browns right now, while several other teams also hold 4-2 records. Their 2-0 record in the division will be extremely helpful as the season goes on and gives them an advantage. While it is still early in the season, the Browns have placed themselves in the conversation. Beyond the Bills and Chiefs, teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars, New England Patriots, and Denver Broncos will all continue to lead the conversation for contenders in this conference. The Browns’ next game is against the Tennessee Titans, who just secured their first win of the season. This game will be a massive opportunity for the team to pull ahead in the AFC North. The Steelers will be playing an international game against the New Orleans Saints, which is always a challenge regardless of the opponent. The Ravens and Bengals will face off in Baltimore, a matchup that will further shake up the division regardless of the outcome. Now, there is a difference between a team’s record in the standings and where fans and media will rank them. The subjective ranking measure is about what could be coming, while the standings is about what has already happened. title: Browns Week 6 win in review: 4 downs lead us to shifting narratives
summary: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2. Yes, you read that right. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season. It wasn’t pretty (in any way), but like before, the team […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2. Yes, you read that right. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season . It wasn’t pretty (in any way), but like before, the team found a way to win when it mattered the most . 1st Down: Another uneven offensive performance It’s going to be a persistent topic, but Cleveland’s offense struggled once again. Granted, the team wasn’t playing in a monsoon like last week, but the same issues that have been persistent all season were prevalent today. The run game has been nonexistent, and the passing game has been inconsistent, at best. Head coach Todd Monken didn’t do his offense any favors in the first half with his play-calling. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter pretty much bottled up the passing game by playing primarily zone, and the Baltimore defense did a great job dropping and getting to their spots. The Browns receivers struggled to get open, and Watson was hesitant to pull the trigger. Watson needs to just let it rip and be okay with making mistakes. Watson isn’t costing the team with his play, and he’s doing enough when they need him. Is it sustainable? No, but the consistency has to appear at some point. Overall, the offense was ineffective for most of the game but found a way to get something going late in the fourth quarter, again . 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the QB more In terms of the quarterback performance, Watson didn’t play well at all. However, when the team needed him, he found a way to get the job done. On paper, the stats are fine and not the worst. The film tells a different story. The flashes are brief, but his flaws are more noticeable. However, the team is finding a way to win despite that. Watson’s level of play isn’t necessarily sustainable, as I’ve mentioned before, but I do believe the Browns will be hesitant to pull the trigger on a quarterback change unless the team starts to lose. Everyone knows that the future quarterback isn’t on this team, but for years fans complained about not having competent quarterback play, which is what Watson is giving you. It’s not pretty, and it’s not flashy, but it’s better than what the team had previously, including from Watson. I am not saying that Watson has played well throughout the entire season, but he’s not playing at a level that screams “he needs to be benched.” Can the play be better? Yes. But I don’t believe that the team needs to bench him right now and winning games will certainly keep him in place. 3rd Down: This defense might be really good How about this defense? Going into the offseason, I said that going from Jim Schwartz to Mike Rutenberg was going to be an upgrade. Six weeks in, the take seems to be aging well. Scheme-wise, it’s a major improvement from last season. One of the many complaints I had about Schwartz’s defense was how the scheme was predictable. Rutenberg’s scheme is anything but that. It’s more unpredictable, with much more chaos, and the players are thriving in it. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger had a fantastic game, and defensive tackle Maliek Collins continues to be a force in the interior. The Ravens running game was nonexistent today, and the passing defense did enough to contain wide receiver Zay Flowers. Granted, the Ravens didn’t have quarterback Lamar Jackson, but this was another strong performance by a legit defense. Is it better than last year’s? 4th Down- 4-2 is 4-2. The Cleveland Browns being 4-2 right now is a surprise, and we don’t have to lie to ourselves about it. The win wasn’t pretty, but the Browns are 4-2. With that being said, no one knows how good this Cleveland Browns team is right now. I don’t. You don’t. Are they a playoff team? As of now, they have the fourth seed, but on the field they are not playing playoff-level football. The offense still has issues, but the defense is playing at an elite level. It’s a question whether or not this team can find consistency on the offensive side of the ball or will the offense just stay at this level for the entire season. Being 4-2 is a lot better than being 1-5. Or 0-6. It’s a week-to-week league, and Cleveland is finding ways to win. Can’t complain about that. Extra points Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is giving valid reasons why the Browns shouldn’t trade him. He’s well respected in the wide receiver room, and the team probably loses if he doesn’t have the game he had on Sunday Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion both struggled today, but it happens for young players. Jared Verse played well in the run game; need the pressures to convert to sacks soon. Might as well stop talking about the running game; it was already broken before the season, and it might be a while before it actually gets fixed. Whenever Cleveland sports teams play on the same day, it feels like a guarantee both teams will not win. Wish that had been different on Sunday. A day later, what are you thinking about the Browns, their Week 6 win, and the changing narratives around the team? Join the conversation!
