title: The NFC North is dominant, but each team has a fatal flaw
summary: Through six weeks of the 2026 NFL season, it looks like the NFC North may be the best division in football. Only the NFC and AFC North have all four teams with winning records, and when compared to the rest of the NFC, there is no comparison. The NFC North has four teams above .500, […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark (97) sacks Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) during the third quarter of their game Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Through six weeks of the 2026 NFL season, it looks like the NFC North may be the best division in football. Only the NFC and AFC North have all four teams with winning records, and when compared to the rest of the NFC, there is no comparison. The NFC North has four teams above .500, while the other 12 teams in the NFC have a combined three teams with winning records. But while the NFC North is certainly impressive right now, each team has a pretty significant flaw that could sink their chances at a championship. Detroit Lions Let’s start with the easiest one. The Detroit Lions have one of the most potent offenses in football (No. 2 in scoring), including a decent running game and a very efficient passing attack. Defensively, it’s not as promising, but there have been some decent performances in stopping the run. However… Fatal flaw: Secondary The Lions’ pass defense has been abysmal through five games, and it largely falls at the feet of the secondary. Detroit’s pass rush has actually been among the best in the NFL. They still lead the NFL in sacks despite not playing a sixth game, and their 90 pressures rank sixth. But the secondary has not been properly complementing their play, leading to several coverage busts or just one-on-one losses. Through six weeks, the Lions rank 29th in EPA/pass, 29th in passer rating allowed, 22nd in yards per attempt allowed, and 30th in dropback success rate. Green Bay Packers Earlier in the year, it looked like the Green Bay Packers couldn’t do anything well. They ranked in the bottom quarter of the league in all four phases. However, they’ve started to find some success, particularly on defense, where they went from one of the worst in the NFL to holding two of the most potent offenses (Bears, Cowboys) to a combined 20 points. Just look at these defensive splits: Weeks 1-3 30.3 PPG allowed (t-29th) 0.092 EPA/play allowed (25th) 46.5% success rate allowed (23rd) Week 4-6 11.3 PPG allowed (first) -0.150 EPA/play allowed (13th) 42.3% success rate allowed (13th) I will say this, though: they remain a team that can be beaten on the ground. Even in these last three games, they’ve allowed a 42.6% rushing success rate, which ranks 27th. But that is not their fatal flaw. Their fatal flaw is… Fatal flaw: OL, no run game The Packers have had offensive line issues all season. In terms of pass protection, they have the eighth-highest pressure rate allowed (40.2%) and the shortest time-to-pressure (2.36) in the NFL. But Jordan Love has been able to avoid sacks. The real struggles on the offensive line are felt in the run game. The Packers rank 32nd in rushing yards per game (59.8), 32nd in rush yards per carry (2.9), 32nd in rush EPA (-0.299) and 31st in rushing success rate (32.5%). The return of Josh Jacobs this week should certainly help, but it won’t fix the underlying offensive line issues. Green Bay ranks 31st in team run blocking PFF grade (47.3) and 20th in ESPN’s run block win rate (73%). Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are a terrifying team when it comes to their defense. They’re first in points per game allowed (12.8), third in yards per play (4.6), first in passer rating allowed (62.9), and fifth in rushing yards allowed (86.6). They also sport an unbelievable 67.0% blitz rate, which is 24% higher than any other team in the NFL. But the Vikings are still very much figuring things out on offense. Quarterback Kyler Murray missing time early certainly has something to do with that, but even in the three games back, the Vikings haven’t scored more than 23 points in a game—even when largely assisted by the aforementioned defense. Fatal flaw: No offensive identity The Vikings don’t really do anything well on offense. Let’s split it by unit: Pass offense: 23rd in dropback EPA 32nd in dropback success rate Run defense 24th in rush EPA 27th in rush success rate Overall, the Vikings rank 30th in yards per drive and 24th in points per drive despite starting with the fifth-best average field position. Chicago Bears Admittedly, the Bears are the most well-rounded team when it comes to performances on each side of the ball. They rank 12th in points per game (25.0) and sixth in points per game allowed (19.8). When you consider that they didn’t have their starting quarterback for half of their games so far, it seems likely they’ll climb into the top-10 in both categories as long as Caleb Williams can remain healthy. But there is one aspect of their game that has been low-key very inefficient, but effectively hidden through six games. Fatal flaw: Run defense On the surface, the Bears’ run defense looks fine. They’re allowing just 90.5 yards per game (seventh best). However, on a per-rush basis, the Bears have actually been quite terrible at stopping the run. They’re ceding 4.5 yards per carry (24th) and ranked 28th in run defense DVOA. Week 6’s game against the Atlanta Falcons is a perfect example of how the Bears have been able to mask this problem. Chicago jumped out to a 21-7 halftime lead, forcing the Falcons out of their game script. While Bijan Robinson still had an efficient day—rushing for 6.8 yards per carry and a decent 44% success rate—he only carried the ball NINE TIMES . The Bears are facing just 20.2 rushing attempts per game, which is the fewest in the NFL. But under the hood, the Bears rank 25th in rush EPA allowed, 23rd in rushing success rate allowed, and 32nd in PFF’s run defense grade.

title: Lions vs. Packers odds: Opening lines for Week 7 matchup
summary: The Detroit Lions (3-2) will host their division rival Green Bay Packers (4-2) in Week 7, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -3.5 points. The Packers finished their 2025 season by snagging the seven seed in the playoffs, but the Bears eliminated them in the Wild […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jameson Williams #1 of the Detroit Lions scores a touchdown during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (3-2) will host their division rival Green Bay Packers (4-2) in Week 7, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -3.5 points . The Packers finished their 2025 season by snagging the seven seed in the playoffs, but the Bears eliminated them in the Wild Card round. Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley was hired to be the next head coach of the Miami Dolphins, and Green Bay hired Jonathan Gannon (previously the head coach of the Cardinals) as a replacement. With Gannon came a new 3-4 defense and a whole bunch of changes on the defensive side of the ball. EDGE Rashan Gary was traded to the Cowboys, NT Colby Wooden was traded to the Colts, while EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, MIKE Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs departed in free agency. EDGE/LB Micah Parsons continues to recover from an ACL tear and is not expected to be available in Week 7. Being up against the cap, the Packers elected to promote from within, inserting EDGE Lukas Van Ness and ILB Isaiah McDuffie into the starting lineup, trading for LB Zaire Franklin (who is starting in place of injured Edgerrin Cooper), and drafting starters CB Brandon Cisse (second round) and NT Chris McClellan (third) on Day 2 of the NFL Draft. On offense, the Packers lost QB Malik Willis, RB Emanuel Wilson, WR Dontayvion Wicks (traded to the Eagles), WR Romeo Dobbs, LT Rasheed Walker, and LG/C Elgton Jenkins; like on defense, they elected to mostly promote from within, elevating RB Marshawn Lloyd into a bigger role (especially with Josh Jacobs suspended—he is expected to return in Week 7), WR Savion Williams and LT Jordan Morgan into the starting lineup, and shifting Sean Rhyan inside to center. Their guard spots have been a massive problem, and the Packers have been searching for answers, with their most recent pairing being RG Travis Glover and former Lion LG Laken Tomlinson (starting in place of the injured Aaron Banks). After a slow start to their 2026 season, the Packers have settled down as their offense has found its groove. The Packers opened the season with a loss after allowing the Vikings to drop 39 points on them, rebounded in Week 2 by beating the Jets by three points, only to lose again in Week 3 as the Falcons dominated them on the ground to the tune of 35 points. In Week 4, the Packers once again found a way to win by three points, this time over the Bucs, then smashed a Caleb Williams-less Bears team 31-7. In Week 6, the Packers took on the Cowboys’ 31st-ranked defense on “Sunday Night Football,” and while they jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the first half, they only scored six points in the second half. Fortunately, their defense held strong and allowed only 13 points, and the game ended in a 23-13 win. With the Packers offense in a groove, the Lions secondary is certainly going to be tested. Will they be able to carry over the success they had against the Cardinals in Week 5? Will Brian Branch return? If so, how big of a factor will he be? With so much unknown about the Lions’ defense, there’s a real chance the Packers continue their run of putting up points, and Detroit will need their top-scoring offense to keep pace and lead the Lions to victory. title: Green Bay Packers News: Packers battling penalty onslaught
summary: I’m of two minds when it comes to talking about the refs and penalties and everything that goes into officiating a professional football game. On the one hand, officiating an NFL game is a massively complex undertaking. Have you read the NFL rulebook? Have you tried? A page turner it is not. The section for […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - DECEMBER 14: A yellow penalty flag is picked during the game at Jacksonville Municipal stadium on December 14, 2008 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Sam Greenwood/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m of two minds when it comes to talking about the refs and penalties and everything that goes into officiating a professional football game. On the one hand, officiating an NFL game is a massively complex undertaking. Have you read the NFL rulebook? Have you tried? A page turner it is not. The section for roughing the passer alone is 950 words. I know this for a fact because I checked after Sunday night’s impromptu roughing the passer festival, and now I’m actually surprised it isn’t called more considering the broad leeway officials have. It’s genuinely hard to know what to call and what not to call. But on the other hand, shouldn’t it be…I don’t know…better than this? Every game is a flag fest and every play takes place under a looming yellow specter. Did a cool thing just happen? Better hold your breath until you see whether or not there’s laundry on the field. You never know when the capricious gaze of black-and-white striped justice will turn your way. I know there’s plenty of data out there about the increase of penalties, but if you’ll allow me to get a little more squishy about it than just looking at the numbers, it feels bad out there. The vibe, as they say, is off. There’s little reason to assume any game you watch is going to unfold without at least one or two completely arbitrary penalties. Discussing any game inevitably hinges on what penalties were or were not called. It’s not a fun way to watch a game! And I don’t know how you fix it. The genie is out of the bottle, in a sense, because you can’t just go back to not throwing as many flags. We’ve already seen what draws a penalty and what doesn’t. Walking it back now is just setting a different paradigm. That might be the only way, though. If nothing’s getting called, everything could feel less arbitrary. That’s small comfort in an NFL landscape increasingly ruled by seemingly random flags. Packers lead league in roughing penalties; Matt LaFleur would like more equity | Packers News ($) A subtext to the Packers’ roughing the passer woes is the fact that none of their opponents seem to get flagged for doing the same thing. title: Josh Jacobs will practice with the Packers this week; Micah Parsons won’t
summary: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur announced during his Monday press conference that the team will have running back Josh Jacobs in practice this week, but that edge defender Micah Parsons will not be practicing, another sign that Parsons has yet to be medically cleared by the training staff. According to LaFleur, Jacobs has […]
full_text: (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur announced during his Monday press conference that the team will have running back Josh Jacobs in practice this week, but that edge defender Micah Parsons will not be practicing, another sign that Parsons has yet to be medically cleared by the training staff. According to LaFleur, Jacobs has been training with the team, which is allowed while he was on the commisioner exempt list, but the team is going to give him a full week of practice before deciding on whether or not he’ll be active against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Jacobs was taken off the commisioner exempt list on Monday, allowing him to return to the active roster after he spent the first six weeks of the regular season on the list while going through a legal battle involving charges of battery and criminal damage to property that Jacobs pleaded no contest to. Recently, it was reported that Jacobs has met with the league on the issue , but the case is not fully resolved, as both Jacobs and the victim, identified as his then-girlfriend, are suing the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department in an attempt to keep evidence from the case sealed . With the addition of Jacobs, the Packers’ active roster is up to 51 players out of the allotted count of 53. Reports also claim that defensive lineman Mazi Smith has signed with Green Bay’s practice squad , which is currently full. Depending on whether or not the Packers release a practice squadder to make room for the addition of Smith or if they move a practice squadder to the active roster, the team has one to two open roster spots on their full 70-man squad (active roster and practice squad) going into the week. Last week, the Packers only needed to make four scratches on their active roster: cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (who was ruled out with an injury on Friday) and three offensive linemen. They backfilled from the practice squad with the game-day elevations of edge defender Aaron Mosby and receiver Coleman Owen, who only saw playing time on special teams in Week 5. On the topic of guard Aaron Banks, who came into the season as the Packers’ preferred option at left guard, LaFleur said that Banks’ practice last week was the “best he’s looked” in a long time. A looming question in Green Bay is whether or not Banks or Kevin Zeitler will end up taking over as starting guards at some point in 2026, especially after Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover didn’t play great against the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football . The Tomlinson-Glover combo was certainly better than the Donovan Jennings-Jacob Monk combo that the team started the season with, but the team is clearly hoping for continued improvement up front. — Update: Jacobs is not currently on the 53-man roster, as the Packers have a one-week exemption for him to return to the active roster from the commissioner exempt list.

title: Green Bay Packers work out former 1st-round pick Mazi Smith
summary: According to the NFL’s transaction wire, the Green Bay Packers worked out defensive lineman Mazi Smith on Monday. Smith is a former first-round pick who was taken 26th overall by the Dallas Cowboys back in the 2023 draft and has played in 43 games (20 starts) in the NFL, including one game for the Miami […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to the NFL’s transaction wire, the Green Bay Packers worked out defensive lineman Mazi Smith on Monday. Smith is a former first-round pick who was taken 26th overall by the Dallas Cowboys back in the 2023 draft and has played in 43 games (20 starts) in the NFL, including one game for the Miami Dolphins this season. Smith was displaced from his starting nose tackle role in Dallas when the Cowboys traded for former Packer Kenny Clark in the Micah Parsons trade. In November of 2025, he was sent to the New York Jets in Dallas’ trade for defensive lineman Quinnen Williams. Last offseason, the Jets turned down Smith’s fifth-year option and released him at the cutdown deadline. Initially, Smith signed with the Dolphins’ practice squad for the 2026 season, but he was released last week by Miami. Mazi Smith was drafted with pick 26 of round 1 in the 2023 draft class. He does not qualify for a #RAS due to a lack of measurements. https://t.co/DHatUCO4Gk pic.twitter.com/ElWygSpPG2 — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 28, 2023 Notably, the Packers are particularly thin at the defensive line position right now, despite entering the regular season with plenty of bodies at the position. Nazir Stackhouse was claimed off waivers by the Tennessee Titans at the cutdown deadline. Jaden Crumedy, the Packers’ first practice squad lineman, was poached by the Houston Texans in-season. On top of that, Javon Hargrave, Jonathan Ford and Warren Brinson are all already on the team’s injured reserve list going into Week 7. The only positive news on the defensive line is that Jordon Riley, who tore his Achilles in 2025, is already practicing with Green Bay — despite still being a member of the physically unable to perform list. Right now, the Packers have a 51-man active roster, even after running back Josh Jacobs was activated from the commisioner exempt list on Monday. They have two roster spots to play with. Their 17-man practice squad is full, though, meaning that if Smith is signed to the team’s practice squad, a corresponding roster most will need to be made — either the promotion of a practice squadder to the active roster or a straight release of a practice squadder. Currently, the team only has four interior defensive linemen on the active roster — Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell — despite playing a 3-4 base defense. The practice squad has one interior defensive lineman, David Blay Jr., who was signed by the team in Week 4 following Crumedy’s poaching and a short stint for Eric Johnson II. Each of the Packers’ interior defensive linemen played at least 30 snaps for Green Bay against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football , even though Campbell had only played nine total career NFL snaps going into the game. McClellan took over as the starting nose tackle in 3-4 looks (which, to be fair, were limited), a role that was previously filled by Ford. — Update: The team is planning on signing Smith to the practice squad, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. The Packers will need to make a corresponding roster move, as the 17-man unit is already full. Update: The Packers are planning to sign him to the practice, per source. https://t.co/MEKguKFGvQ — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 19, 2026

title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 6 win over the Cowboys
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6. Offense The Packers have switching up their personnel groupings quite a bit on a game-by-game basis, which […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6. Offense The Packers have switching up their personnel groupings quite a bit on a game-by-game basis, which I always like to see. Stay unpredictable. Become ungovernable. Against the Bears in Week 5 , we saw the Packers dial back their usage of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) quite a bit. In that game they were out of 11 personnel 54.2% of the time. This week they dialed that up: It was a good attack plan, as that personnel grouping was their best group while passing… …and while running. It’d be nice to get a rushing attack that could actually be decent, but the passing game has really improved as the offensive line has solidified. Who knew?! In this game, Jordan Love averaged 2.7 seconds to throw and had an ADOT (Average Depth of Target) of 9.7 yards. That’s a good, functional passing offense. That felt impossible only a few weeks ago. The Cowboys played primarily Cover 3 in this game, and Love shredded that coverage, going 10/14 for 142 yards (+0.38 EPA per Play). He also shredded the blitz, going 8/12 for 100 yards (+0.52 EPA per Play) when blitzed. The Packers pass rate of 62.9% feels about right. They would have been over 65% for the game if they didn’t take the air out of the ball in the 4th quarter (46.7% pass rate in the 4th). With as inept as the run game has looked this year I’d like to see that pass rate up just a bit, but hovering around 65% feels right with where this team currently is. Sure would be nice if Matthew Golden got his hands figured out (which is baffling, considering that seemed to be one of the stronger points in his game), but he still turned in a nice game. He notched 6 catches on 13 targets for 104 yards and a TD (+1.74 EPA per Reception). His average depth of target of 15.62 yards was 4.9 yards above the NFL average. Just imagine what his numbers would have looked like if he didn’t drop two TD passes. They continue to switch up their run attack depending on the opponent. They went about 50/50 this week, with 46.1% of their run game fitting into zone buckets and the rest into man/gap buckets. Did it work? Man, not really, but I like their attack plan. They’ve shown some improvement up front in terms of blocking, but the run game just hasn’t been good this year. Defense The Packers defense did a great job keeping the Cowboys offense off-balance all game, and they did that by generating pressure on Dak Prescott. Gannon has done a nice job at switching up defensive tendencies each week. This week the Packers blitzed on 35.71% of snaps, and generated pressure on 41.07% of dropbacks. Beyond blitzes, the stacked front looks bothered Prescott whether the Packers brought pressure or not. On the game, Prescott wasn’t good whether he was blitzed (-0.16 EPA per Play) or not blitzed (-0.24 EPA per Play). Those numbers would look even better for the Packers defense if they didn’t get hit with a couple pretty ticky-tack roughing the passer calls. In terms of passing zones, Prescott had a couple underneath zones he had success throwing to, but there’s a lot of red in this chart. Dani Dennis-Sutton continues to show up every week. This week he had a pressure rate of 22.7% (8.56% above NFL average), with an average time to pressure of 2.67 seconds. Albums listened to: Eels – Cookie Happened

title: How bad is Marshawn Lloyd, historically speaking?
summary: Marshawn Lloyd is a PROBLEM (derogatory). While the early woes of the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line have prevented any running back from really getting going, Kaleb Johnson at least averages 3.7 yards per carry, and Chris Brooks, prior to his injury, hit a solid 4.7 yards per carry. Now, those numbers are bolstered by […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - OCTOBER 11: Green Bay Packers running back Marshawn Lloyd (32) scores a touchdown during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on October 11, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Marshawn Lloyd is a PROBLEM (derogatory). While the early woes of the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line have prevented any running back from really getting going, Kaleb Johnson at least averages 3.7 yards per carry , and Chris Brooks, prior to his injury, hit a solid 4.7 yards per carry. Now, those numbers are bolstered by a few long runs, and they have both been bad on a per play basis, but at least they’re bolstered by something . Marshawn Lloyd has no juice. If there was some sort of vampire plant that sucked all the juice out of useful plants, that is what he would be. He has anti-juice. He’s just pulp. How bad is it? Since the merger, there are only seven running backs ever to average 2.5 yards or less per carry for their career while having over 50 carries . Four of those backs ran in 1982 or earlier (Willie Spencer, Reece Morrison, Odell Lawson, and Michael Morton). Marshawn Lloyd, along with Keaontay Ingram and Isaiah Spiller) is one of only three to pull this off since 1982. It gets worse! The NFL’s wonderful NextGenStats site tracks how many yards a running back should have gotten each carry based on the blocking, quality of defense, and several other factors. Marshawn Lloyd is dead last in Rushing Yards Over Expected per Attempt (RYOE/ATT) with -1.55 . Yes, on average, every single carry he has gained 1.5 fewer yards than an average back who simply followed his blocking and then fell down. Alvin Kamara is second worst in this category with -1.19, which is WAY better than Lloyd. Lloyd also unsurprisingly “leads” the league in negative total Rushing Yards Over Expected (RYOE) with -75 , just edging JK Dobbins (-72). Lloyd has gained more yards than expected on just 27.1% of his total carries, or 13 of his total carries. And he’s doing all of this against light boxes, as only five running backs have faced light boxes less than Lloyd in the 2026 season. NextGenStats also tracks a metric simply called “Efficiency.” Efficiency tracks how many yards a back travels per yard gained. A lower efficiency metric indicates a more “North-South” runner. Marshawn Lloyd averaged 6.06 yards run per yard gained, the second least efficient total in football (Keaton Mitchell somehow averages 6.27). This is indicative of Lloyd’s tendency to bounce runs outside even when putting his head down and charging forward is clearly the best idea. While the passing game is more important than the running game in football, you cannot survive with this level of play for very long. I wrote a piece a few weeks ago about some of the worst Packer rushing teams of all time, including a bit on running back Michael Haddix, who played for Green Bay from 1989-1990. Haddix holds the NFL record for the lowest career Y/A (3.0) for any player with over 500 carries. I am sure Lloyd will have his carries cut (especially if Josh Jacobs returns), but he is on pace for 136 carries this season at 2.5 Y/A, a full yard shy of the worst high volume back of all time. Continuing to play him after he ran for 10 yards on 8 carries against Dallas this week is inexcusable.

title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 6 vs. the Cowboys
summary: The Green Bay Packers keep on rolling and are now 4-2 after a convincing 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. When the schedule was released, a lot of folks marked their calendars for this game. There was a small chance Micah Parsons could return from his torn ACL to face off […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Matthew Golden #0 of the Green Bay Packers attempts to make a catch against Ameer Speed #23 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers keep on rolling and are now 4-2 after a convincing 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. When the schedule was released, a lot of folks marked their calendars for this game. There was a small chance Micah Parsons could return from his torn ACL to face off against his former team —though that ended up not happening last night. The two teams had quite the battle last year during a game that ended in a 40-40 OT tie, and it felt like something similar could happen again this weekend — that ended up not happening last night. Jordan Love has historically performed well against the Cowboys — that ended up happening. Let’s dive in on this victory Monday. Winner: Trey Smack The last few weeks, I’ve been holding my breath every time the rookie kicker goes out there for an attempt. It hasn’t been too bad so far, but that’s mostly because the rest of the team seems to have gotten it together, so the missed kicks aren’t “deciders”. On Sunday night, Smack was finally perfect, with 2 made XPs and 3 FGs (longest 44). In a 10-point win, it’s good to see the kicker get all 11 possible points. Winner: Carrington Valentine When CB Brandon Cisse left the game with what is being described as a stinger , Valentine subbed in. I proceeded to say these exact words: “They’re going to throw right at him.” “He’s going to give up a 20 yard play; watch.” And you know what? I was right—about the first part. Cowboys QB Dak Prescott threw right at him. What did Valentine do? Caught it, AND returned it for 21 yards. The play was unfortunately negated due to an absolutely AWFUL roughing the passer penalty on Lukas Van Ness, but Valentine’s play shut me the hell up either way. On the very next play, he was thrown at again, and this time forced a PBU. Valentine finished the day with 4 total tackles and 1 PD. Carrington: I’m sorry for doubting you. I won’t let it happen again (I probably will.) Carrington Valentine’s first play in the game #ART pic.twitter.com/a9Vib7289n — Oliver Davis II (@I_Am_OD3) October 19, 2026 Winner: Brandon Cisse Speaking of Brandon Cisse: Brandon Cisse! The “welcome to the NFL” moments have come and gone for the rookie, and he’s improving week after week. This week, he snagged his first career interception, and it came as the Cowboys were inching closer and closer to the endzone. He had some really great tackles on Sunday night, finishing with 4, plus 2 PDs. Oh! He also allowed a passer rating of…9.4. The Packers’ first draft pick of 2026 looks like a good one so far. did you CISSE that?! 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/pOwCpZyVDe — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 19, 2026 Winner: Javon Bullard Plain and simple, S Javon Bullard brings a level of physicality to the team that they just would not have with anyone else at his spot. He’s gotten better each year he’s been in the league, and last night was routine for him. His biggest play of the night came on 4th and 2 in the 4th quarter, when he batted down a pass meant for WR CeeDee Lamb. Bullard finished the night with 6 total tackles and 3 PDs. With next season being a contract year for him, the Packers should probably start working on locking him down soon. Javon Bullard deflects the 4th down pass away! DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yAXwn9jtgN — NFL (@NFL) October 19, 2026 Winner: Evan Williams Since we’re on the topic of guys who the Packers should definitely re-sign: Evan Williams. Williams is having a phenomenal start to the 2026 season, and if this continues, he might get to call himself an All-Pro safety in January. Williams had an impressive pick last night on 3rd and 8 as the Cowboys were inside the 20 and looking to tie it up. He read Dak like a book here. Williams finished the night with 6 total tackles, 1 PD, 1 INT, and 1 QB hit. EVAN. WILLIAMS. 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/H2dBumCPkg — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 19, 2026 Winner: Jordan Love I could probably just leave it at this: by the end of the Packers’ first drive, QB Jordan Love had 109 passing yards. But I can never just leave it at that. Love’s season of playing well “despite it all” continued last night, as his receivers dropped pass after pass. He could’ve had 4 TD passes. WR Matthew Golden dropped two, and WR Christian Watson dropped one. All of these were in the endzone. All of these were perfectly thrown balls which hit the receivers only where they could catch it. Love finished the night 23 of 41 (56%) for 276 yards, 1 passing TD, 1 rushing TD, and 1 INT. Love and Watson pick up another first! DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TtkXxWC08n — NFL (@NFL) October 19, 2026 Passes dropped this season: 1. Jordan Love – 18 The next closest quarterback has 11. — Daire Carragher (@DaireCarragher) October 19, 2026 Jordan Love had three touchdowns dropped on Sunday night: -Matthew Golden dropped 38-yard TD -Golden dropped 26-yard TD -Christian Watson 26-yard TD (it was slightly tipped to be fair) pic.twitter.com/b8Gh9AzsS7 — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 19, 2026 Woser: Matthew Golden It’s like if prime Davante Adams got into a Freaky Friday situation with Jameson Williams, but only twice per game. Golden had some really bad drops last night, but didn’t let it phase him as he led the team in every receiving category. His QB backed him up after the game. Love and Golden are developing some pretty amazing chemistry on the field, and as a result, the receiver logged his second-straight 100+ yard game. Golden had 6 catches on 13 targets for 104 yards and 1 TD (could’ve been, should’ve been 3!) AGENT 0 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/g9gZwas6JN — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 19, 2026 The second drop by Matthew Golden tonight. pic.twitter.com/r38uRVDdyh — BenJarmin Munguia (@JustJarmin) October 19, 2026 Loser: MarShawn Lloyd I’m sorry for ever asking to see more of this. It simply cannot continue. It just can’t. 8 rushes. 10 yards. 1 sigh of disgust. The 2nd place Packers have a big divisional matchup next week as they head to Detroit to face off against the 4th place Lions. With the Bears on a short week as they play the reigning AFC champs Thursday night, this may be the Packers’ chance to pull ahead and start to create a gap. The Packers and Lions play at 4:25 ET/3:25 CT on FOX .

title: The Packers overcame disastrous first down results in win over Cowboys
summary: The Green Bay Packers had plenty of bright spots in their victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, but the team’s first down offense was not among them. The Packers consistently shot themselves in the foot at the start of offensive series throughout their 23-13 victory, regularly losing yardage and requiring Jordan Love […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Marshawn Lloyd #32 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball against Donovan Ezeiruaku #6 of the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had plenty of bright spots in their victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, but the team’s first down offense was not among them. The Packers consistently shot themselves in the foot at the start of offensive series throughout their 23-13 victory, regularly losing yardage and requiring Jordan Love to go into hero mode on second- and third-and-long situations. Fortunately, Love did just that, as he threw for 276 yards and a touchdown while adding a second score on the ground, all while being pressured on nearly 50 percent of his dropbacks. With the Cowboys’ defense consistently seeing big numbers on the yards to go category on the scoreboard, they were able to tee off on Love, hitting him several times and recording three sacks. The fact that the Packers were able to score 23 points — a number that probably should have been more like 30, had their receivers caught the football in the end zone consistently — is truly remarkable given the disaster that the Packers put up on first down. Of the Packers’ 27 plays run on first down (not including one defensive penalty), the team failed to gain yardage on 13 of them, either via incomplete pass, no gain or loss of yardage on the ground, or an offensive penalty. That’s roughly half of the time that the team still has double-digit yards to gain after a first down play. In those 27 snaps, the Packers managed to have a “success” (defined as picking up at least 40% of the required yards to gain) on just 5 of them. That’s a hilariously bad 18.5% success rate on first down, and consistently setting themselves up in long distance situations required Love and the Packers to have a 65% success rate on 3rd and 4th downs to make up for it. Indeed, Love was 2/7 passing for just nine yards on first downs; on all other downs, he was 22/34 for 269 yards and a touchdown. (His rushing touchdown, a quarterback sneak, did come on first down). The run game was no better than the passing game, either. MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson combined for 15 carries on first downs, gaining a net of just 25 yards. Because of the long distances, I counted only six true running plays on other downs. Furthermore, the run game had as many plays go for no gain or negative yardage on first downs as they had gains of four yards or more (four each). And then the Packers also had three first-down penalties and a sack, only adding to the ugliness. Here’s a look at the play-by-play results on first downs on Sunday night. As a warning, you may want to find an eyewash station after looking at this. Time Down/Dist Description Yardage Result 11:13 Q1 1st-10 Lloyd run -2 2nd-12 9:42 Q1 1st-10 Lloyd run -3 2nd-13 8:09 Q1 1st-10 Strong run 0 2nd-10 7:28 Q1 1st-10 Love pass incomplete; PENALTY – ineligible man downfield -5 1st-15 7:22 Q1 1st-15 PENALTY – Neutral zone infraction 5 1st-10 7:22 Q1 1st-10 Love pass incomplete 0 2nd-10 6:08 Q1 1st-10 Strong run 1 2nd-9 2:36 Q1 1st-10 Love sacked -2 2nd-12 14:15 Q2 1st-10 Strong run 2 2nd-8 13:12 Q2 1st-10 Love scramble; PENALTY – holding -10 1st-20 12:44 Q2 1st-20 Love pass to S.Williams 7 2nd-13 11:17 Q2 1st-10 Love pass incomplete 0 2nd-10 8:11 Q2 1st-Goal (6) Strong run 5 2nd-Goal (1) 1:50 Q2 1st-10 Love pass incomplete 0 2nd-10 1:22 Q2 1st-10 Love pass to Strong 2 2nd-8 0:53 Q2 1st-10 Strong run 4 2nd-6 0:25 Q2 1st-Goal (1) Love run, touchdown 1 TD 14:55 Q3 1st-10 Love pass incomplete; PENALTY – holding -10 1st-20 14:52 Q3 1st-20 Love pass incomplete 0 2nd-20 9:14 Q3 1st-10 Strong run 2 2nd-8 7:45 Q3 1st-10 Love pass incomplete 0 2nd-10 6:06 Q3 1st-10 Lloyd run 4 2nd-6 3:29 Q3 1st-10 Lloyd run 2 2nd-8 13:30 Q4 1st-10 K.Johnson run -2 2nd-12 12:19 Q4 1st-10 Strong run 5 2nd-5 10:55 Q4 1st-10 Strong run 2 2nd-8 5:00 Q4 1st-10 Lloyd run 2 2nd-8 4:49 Q4 1st-10 Lloyd run 3 2nd-7 Again, it’s shocking that the Packers were able to put together a successful offense with such dramatic ineptitude on first down. Credit Jordan Love for being fearless and accurate in the pocket for this team being able to put together five scoring drives to reach the 20-point mark, and for putting still more balls in places where his receivers should have made plays and pushed the team closer to 30. If the Packers can clean up their execution and start getting positive yardage on first downs with more regularity, this offense could very easily take a big step forward.

title: Packers vs. Lions odds: Opening lines for Week 7 matchup
summary: Ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the Green Bay Packers saw an unusual amount of movement on the point spread. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers calls a play at the line of scrimmage during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the Green Bay Packers saw an unusual amount of movement on the point spread. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the game approached, at least a handful of books had switched back to having the Cowboys favored. The Packers cruised, however, earning a convincing 23-13 victory to move to 4-2 on the season. That record puts them in second place in the NFC North, 1.5 games behind the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and a half-game up on the 3-2 Detroit Lions. Both of those two teams were idle in Week 6, but the Packers have a chance to make some significant movement in the division next Sunday. Week 7 brings the Packers their third game against an NFC North opponent this season, as they will travel to Detroit to play the Lions in the late Sunday afternoon time slot. Look for that game to be FOX’s game of the week, particularly with the Packers’ recent resurgence back into serious playoff contention. However, the books are giving the Lions a reasonable advantage in this game thanks to it being played on their own home turf. FanDuel sportsbook opened the line at Lions -3.5 for next Sunday in the first of two meetings between these teams in 2026. Books are also expecting another high-scoring game between these two squads, setting the over/under for total points at 52.5. Last year saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time since Dan Campbell took over as Lions head coach. Green Bay took the season opener at Lambeau Field 27-13, then got another Thanksgiving Day victory in Detroit in a high-scoring, 31-24 affair. Prior to 2025, the 2020 season was the last time Green Bay went 2-for-2, when they won similarly high scoring games in weeks 2 (42-24) and 14 (also 31-24). Stay tuned to see if the line shifts before the end of the week. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! title: Green Bay Packers News: Defense is impressing thanks to Gannon’s aggressiveness
summary: Happy Monday, Wisconsin sports fans! The Milwaukee Brewers will open up the World Series on Friday (yes, that’s a true statement) and the Green Bay Packers just beat the Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys convincingly in back-to-back weeks. What a time it is to be alive. Although the Packers’ defense got to feast on Chicago’s […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 24: Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon calls a play during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Atlanta Falcons on September 24, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Happy Monday, Wisconsin sports fans! The Milwaukee Brewers will open up the World Series on Friday (yes, that’s a true statement) and the Green Bay Packers just beat the Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys convincingly in back-to-back weeks. What a time it is to be alive. Although the Packers’ defense got to feast on Chicago’s backup quarterbacks last week, that was not the case on Sunday night, when Dallas trotted out its full-strength offense at Lambeau Field. All Jonathan Gannon did was dismantle it piece by piece, using a heavy dose of zone coverage and some well-timed, creative blitz packages to make life a living hell for Dak Prescott. By the fourth quarter, it seemed like Prescott didn’t even want to be there. His throwaway on 4th down from inside the red zone looked like a give-up play, and although Dallas scored a late touchdown to pull back to within ten points, it didn’t really feel like the Cowboys ever had a serious chance of making a comeback. Instead, the Packers have now gone three games without allowing more than 14 points, their first such streak since 2016, and they posted the third game of that streak against a team thought to have one of the best offenses in the NFL. And, to make things even more encouraging, they won convincingly despite not playing their A game. The offense left points on the board thanks to drops, penalties, and a decent amount of slippage in line play, to say nothing of the lack of a run game. But Jordan Love is hanging tough under pressure and slinging the ball around to his talented receivers, who would have even more impressive stat lines if they’d just hold onto the football. It feels like this team is rounding into form just in time for a tough stretch on the schedule. If they can clean up some of the execution issues on offense, this Packers team will have a chance to do much more than just be the 7th seed in the playoffs once again. Game notes: Packers’ blitzes and takeaways dominate Cowboys | Packers.com Gannon’s aggressiveness was notable, and it helped lead to a pair of interceptions at critical junctures in the first half. Packers’ Defense Is Clicking on All Cylinders at Just the Right Time | SI.com What more can you really say? The secondary played well, the pass rush was in Prescott’s face early and often, and the run defense did its job. Packers use timely turnovers, third-down conversions to beat struggling Cowboys | ESPN The offense boosted its ranking from 32nd to 25th on third down conversion rate with an 11-for-18 performance on Sunday night. Dak Prescott: Cowboys offense ‘didn’t hold our own’ in loss to Packers | NFL.com There were a couple of bizarre decisions by the Cowboys offense, which got its only touchdown drive when they went with heavier personnel early in the second half but shifted right back to trotting out mostly 11 personnel after that. LISTEN — The Repack: Packers’ defense dominates Dallas in 23-13 win | Frozen Tundra Frequencies Tex and Justis look at last night’s game and ask what needs to happen for the NFL to finally acknowledge and then do something about the officiating issues. title: The Day After The Day After: Houston Texans beat Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 in London
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 6 Love Defense? This was not your game: Neither Matt Burke nor Anthony Campanile had a […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: The players of the Houston Texans celebrate victory at full-time in the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 6 Love Defense? This was not your game: Neither Matt Burke nor Anthony Campanile had a great flight back after this game. Consider: 65 combined points, 618 combined yards passing, 220 combined yards rushing, 8 total touchdowns (7 passing), 52% 3rd Down conversion rate, only 2 INTs (both in the end zone) and ZERO, yes, ZERO sacks! Granted, few quarterbacks are playing as well as Trevor Lawrence and CJ Stroud, but with the respective defensive talent on the field, especially with pass rushers like Danielle Hunter, Will Anderson Jr., Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen, you figured someone would’ve gotten one sack. Houston’s Rushing Attack: Jacksonville came into this game with a historically good run defense. They had yet to allow a single rusher to gain more than 40 yards in five game. They had the #1 rushing defense in the league. So of course, the Houston Texans and their 31st ranked rushing offense, which had only broken 80 combined rushing yards in a game once all season, managed to outgain the Jags on the ground with 114 combined yards. Houston’s top RBs went for over 40 yards each (Marks 56 on 15 carries, Jordan 43 on 6 carries). You could argue that Marks has been the more explosive back for the Texans’ attack vs. Montgomery, who seemed a bit more tentative before his injury in Week 5. Jordan offered just as much explosiveness as a rusher, especially on his 25-yard TD rush in the 3rd Quarter. Houston must really hope this is a trend and not a fluke. The Kicks for the Kickoffs were good. The coverage, uh, well…it was: On a day with so much scoring, the kick coverage units got a lot of work. For the Texans, it seems that Fairbairn has been working on landing his kicks short of the end zone to force a return. Only one of his six kickoffs was a touchback, and that was the kick at the end of the 1st half. That was the good news. The bad news was that of five Jacksonville kick returns, three started past the JAX 35, including one in Houston territory. All three of those drives got to the Houston red zone, with 2 TDS and one end zone INT. Yes, Ameer Abdullah is a quality kick returner, but that is not exactly the standard Houston fans have come to expect from a Frank Ross unit. THE CRITICAL PLAY: 4th Quarter (2:24), JAX Ball @ HOU 48, 1st and 10; Trevor Lawrence pass for TE Brenton Strange incomplete. S Calen Bullock on the pass defense In this game, most of the big plays came on offense, from Jaylen Noel’s 50-yard reception inside of a minute left in the 1st half that secured Houston a TD to the Woody Marks’ catch-and-run setting up Fairbairn’s walk-off FG. However, we will consider a defensive play. After the Stroud INT, the Jags had moved the ball 32 yards to Houston’s side of the field on three straight Lawrence completions. On this play, Lawrence was looking to TE Strange, who had a solid game to this point, down the intermediate middle of the Houston defense. However, the pass was nearly picked off by Calen Bullock, who couldn’t quite wrap up the ball. Yet, it stemmed Lawrence’s momentum. An incompletion and short pass later, the Jags settled for a tying FG. This gave Houston the ball back with plenty of time to win it, which they managed to do. Given how Houston has lost three games with a lead inside of the final two minutes with teams and given how neither defense was making all that much an impact, Bullock’s near INT was enough to hold Jacksonville and set up the Texans for the win. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 8: Number of 4th Quarter/OT game-winning drives led by Stroud for Houston : That number could and should be higher this season. Stroud has done this twice against Jacksonville, the other happening in 2024, when he led Houston to a win via a last-second TD pass to RB Dare Ogunbowale. 1388: Days between a CJ Stroud/Marvin Harrison, Jr. reception: Prior to the second quarter of the London Game, the last time that Marvin Harrison Jr caught a pass from CJ Stroud, it was in the first half of the 2022 Peach Bowl/CFB semi-final between Ohio State and Georgia. Georgia would win that game 42-41, but a “what if?” that haunts Ohio State fans is what if Harrison hadn’t left the game after a concussion. Harrison and Stroud were slicing up the Georgia defense (Harrison: 5 receptions/106 yards/2 TDs), but when Harrison went out of the game, Georgia was able to get back into contention and eventually took the lead for good. 60: Distance of Longest FG ever made against the Texans: When Cam Little got all of that kick to tie the game at 31, he set a record against Houston. The previous long, 59, happened in 2020, when the-then Jags kicker, Josh Lambo, made his kick to end the 1st half of a game in Jacksonville (also against Houston). GAME BALLS: QB CJ Stroud: Great numbers (24-of-34 for 312 yards, 3 TDS, 1 INT, 0 sacks) and rebounded from a bad INT to lead a game-winning drive. WR Jaylin Noel: Noel continues a breakout run with this day at the office: 4 receptions/107 yards/1 TD; 2 kickoff returns/74 yards.; 1 punt return/2 yards LT Aireontae Ersery/LG Keylan Rutledge: In a game where Houston rushed for over 100 yards against the top rushing defense in the league, as well as not surrendering a single sack, a lot of credit must go to the Texans offensive line. In particular, Houston had most of their success running along the left side of the offensive formations (70 of their 114 rushing yards). These two youngsters did much of the heavy lifting to make this game work. OC Nick Caley: If you are going to slam him for the bad, gotta give credit for the good. The critical 3rd down conversion for the Texans on the final drive when Stroud hit Marks for a catch-and-run was one of his best calls. SHOULD BE FORCED TO EAT NOTHING BUT BRITISH COOKING FOR THE REST OF THE WEEK WHILE LISTENING TO DUUUVAAALLLL CHANTS IN A BAD BRITISH ACCENT ON REPEAT S Reed Blankenship: The rough start for the once-lauded free agent signing continues. Jags TE Brenton Strange was feasting on Blankenship’s coverage in the 1st half, and Blankenship missed a key tackle on a Jags TD. To top off the bad trip, he left the game due to a concussion. MJ Stewart replaced him in the lineup, and while the defense still had a tough day, Stewart seemed to play a bit better. TE Brevin Jordan: Not entirely fair, but if you sat through the entire Texans game Sunday and just stayed seated, you had more receiving yards than Brevin Jordan. He had more receptions (1 to 0), but you had more yards (-1 to 0). Wembley Groundskeepers: Few stadiums are as venerated as Wembley. The host of the 1966 World Cup Final, the 2012 Olympics and tons of other massive events, you would think that the groundskeepers would be among the best in the world. Uh, about that. The field seemed unnecessarily slick, which cost the game its umpire early in the 1st quarter due to slippage/leg injury. Additionally, Dalton Schlutz could not maintain his footing on a key 1st half reception on a third down, forcing Houston to punt. A key talking point throughout the game as it impacted both teams. With that win, Houston moves to 2-4, two games back of Jacksonville for the AFC South. They return home to face the New York Giants of New Jersey. Kickoff is this Sunday at noon CDT at Reliant Stadium.
