title: Rams ‘dream season’ being derailed by poor play and injuries
summary: The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie not to be 2-4 through six weeks, but to compete for a Super Bowl. But the Rams plans have been derailed by poor play, penalties and injuries as the Rams continue to lose key pieces. Garrett hasn’t suited up since Week 1, McDuffie missed […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie not to be 2-4 through six weeks, but to compete for a Super Bowl. But the Rams plans have been derailed by poor play, penalties and injuries as the Rams continue to lose key pieces. Garrett hasn’t suited up since Week 1, McDuffie missed week 6, Davante Adams is hurt, Aaron Donald has missed time, Jaylen Watson has missed time, Puka Nacua has missed time and more. Alaric Jackson was suspended so we’ll file that one under poor decision making. Either way, the Rams had a plan, and they are punching themselves in the mouth and need to come up with the new one. I am not saying the season is over, it’s not, but it’s currently being derailed, and it’s up to the Rams to get themselves back on track. Can they do it? Yes. Will they do it? We have to keep watching to find out. Rams star Kobie Turner likely going on IR due to groin injury (ramswire) “On top of that, star defensive lineman and team captain Kobie Turner will likely have to go on injured reserve , keeping him out of action for the near future. Turner injured his groin and will be out 4-6 weeks, according to Michael J. Duarte of the California Post. Turner played in only 23 snaps during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals . That was the second-lowest out of the position group, with Ty Hamilton’s 18 snaps rounding out the count.“ Cardinals Have Sent Rams Into Full-Blown Meltdown After Week 6 Upset (sports.yahoo) “”Throughout the McVay era, beating the Cardinals was about as ‘sure’ as it gets. This was supposed to be a ‘get right’ game and start a run going into the bye. Instead, they lose 18-16 to a Cardinals team that had waved the white flag on this season,” wrote Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak. The national stories aren’t about an incredible achievement from Arizona, who saw Mike LaFleur emerge as the second coach in NFL history to have his first two wins come on the road at the same stadium, but rather about how things are going sideways quickly in Los Angeles:“ Full list of Rams’ terrible injury updates following Week 6 loss (ramswire) “Davante Adams, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner and Blake Grupe all got injured in the game and will miss extended time, ranging from a few weeks to the rest of the season. When it rains, it pours, and it is torrential in Los Angeles right now. Here’s a full list of injury updates from McVay following Monday’s press conference.“ Davante Adams set for lengthy layoff as LA Rams rocked by injury blows (aol.com) “In his 13th NFL campaign, the 33-year-old wide receiver has recorded 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns this year. Adams previously missed three late-season contests with a hamstring issue last year before coming back for postseason play. “It’s significant when you don’t have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust,” McVay said. “His contributions can’t be measured. You don’t replace somebody like him, and so what you’ve got to do is you’ve got to be able to figure out what’s the next right thing? What does that look like in terms of our vision? We’ll have to adjust and adapt.” NFC West update: LA Rams in injury crisis mode with several long-term absences (fieldgulls) “It bodes well for Seattle, who—like Los Angeles have dropped back-to-back games and have looked like a shell of themselves as of late. However, it certainly helps one of the most dangerous forces in the NFC has as well. Despite the injury news, the Rams are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and the Cardinals over their next four games—a favourable upcoming stretch of games by all means. Given the star power on their roster, it’s difficult to count Los Angeles out of the playoff picture, even nearing the halfway mark of the season, but there’s certainly work to be done if they want to keep up in the NFC race.“ What has gone wrong for the 2-4 Rams after ‘superteam’ hype? Can they fix it? (espn.com) “Well, the alarms are now going off in Los Angeles. On Sunday, the Rams lost 18-16 at home to a 1-4 Cardinals team , the sort of defeat that inspires soul searching and painful self-reflection. Any team can lose when the turnovers don’t bounce its way or an injury unexpectedly costs it a key player, but neither of those were the case against Arizona. And while the Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe to an early-game knee injury , special teams weren’t really to blame for the loss, either. Are the 2-4 Rams, who were the prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after acquiring Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie and bringing Aaron Donald out of retirement this offseason, just not very good? Do we know enough after six games to say with confidence that the superteam Rams we expected to see heading into the season aren’t ever going to show up on the field in 2026? Is it time to write them off as Super Bowl contenders? One thing I can say for sure: To live up to the preseason hype and win the Super Bowl, the Rams will have to do something no NFL team has ever done before. If the Rams even make it to the Super Bowl, they would be the first team in NFL history to post a losing record through six weeks and still manage to win its conference in the Super Bowl era. Playing in an era with a 17-game regular season and 14 playoff teams makes a potential turnaround a little easier for the Rams, but they would have to break 60 years of precedent to overcome this slow start.“ 3 takeaways from Rams’ rash of major injuries suffered in Week 6 (ramswire) “With all their losses, here are three takeaways on what they mean for the Rams. Nacua needs to be at his absolute best Puka Nacua will be called upon even more with Adams being out for an estimated 6-10 weeks . In the last year of his deal, Nacua has found his form in recent weeks and is making the ultimate push to become the NFL’s highest-paid non-quarterback.“ Legendary band to play Rams-Packers halftime show on Thanksgiving Eve (sports.yahoo) “Netflix announced on Tuesday that legendary rock band U2 will play the halftime show during the Los Angeles Rams ‘ game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. That game takes place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, bringing the iconic band to the Rams’ house for a special performance. It’s the NFL’s first game ever on Thanksgiving Eve, and it comes after the Rams’ Week 11 bye. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET and will be streamed live on Netflix, just as the Rams’ season opener against the 49ers was. U2, led by Bono and The Edge, have won 22 Grammy Awards, including Best Album for The Joshua Tree in 1987.“ Rams’ devasting wave of Week 6 injuries might be the final blow (ramblinfan) “Defensive tackle Kobie Turner: groin injury. Out four to six weeks, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Kicker Blake Grupe: torn ACL. Done for the year. That’s on top of existing injuries to star cornerback Trent McDuffie, who missed the game against Arizona and is in question for Week 7. Myles Garrett, McVay said, will not return to practice this week. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has been on injured reserve since Week 1. The Horns’ season from hell is here. What’s next for the Rams after losing multiple stars Where does the team go from here? First things first, they’ll have to sign a kicker. McVay expects that to happen in the next day or two. “ Commanders-49ers on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 23-17 win (nfl.com) “ Niners survive second-half hibernation. Monday night’s showdown started off lopsided just as many prognosticated. The 49ers made Odyssey-length marches look commonplace, going 64 yards or longer on four of their first five possessions and turning them into 20 points. Brock Purdy…
author: Danny Stone

title: Fired Colts GM didn’t finalize potential Matthew Stafford trade
summary: The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday and the news surfaced an old report by Peter Schrager that the team could have acquired Matthew Stafford in 2021 instead of the Los Angeles Rams. Stafford wanted to go to the Rams, but would have approved a trade to the Colts if Ballard had […]
full_text: The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday and the news surfaced an old report by Peter Schrager that the team could have acquired Matthew Stafford in 2021 instead of the Los Angeles Rams. Stafford wanted to go to the Rams, but would have approved a trade to the Colts if Ballard had outbid Les Snead, which obviously didn’t happen. The Rams traded Jared Goff, two first-round picks, and more for Stafford. The Colts settled for Carson Wentz, a quarterback who would later backup Stafford in L.A. in 2023. What could have happened differently for either franchise and GM if Ballard had made a better offer to the Detroit Lions for Stafford instead of Snead? Matthew Stafford signed off on being traded to the Colts in 2021, but Chris Ballard wasn’t willing to meet the Rams’ winning price. A moment in time where Indianapolis would’ve solved the Andrew Luck retirement, but the QB carousel continues on today. pic.twitter.com/zoFESMAYoe — Evan Sidery (@esidery) October 19, 2026 The Colts obviously wouldn’t outbid two first-round picks, so what did they do instead? Colts first-round picks 2021 first-round pick: DE Kwity Paye Ballard drafted pass rusher Paye in 2021 with the 21st overall pick. Paye had 30.5 sacks in five seasons with Indianapolis but is now a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. His success as a draft pick could be rated as a B- given that mid-first round pass rushers rarely become superstars. Paye wasn’t a bust, but he’s not as valuable as an MVP quarterback. 2022 first-round pick: Traded for Wentz in 2021 Because the Colts didn’t land Stafford, they traded a 2021 third-round pick and a conditional first-round pick in 2022, which went through because Wentz played in over 75% of the team’s snaps. The Colts went 9-8 in 2021 but didn’t qualify for the playoffs. That ended up being the 16th overall pick, which Washington used on receiver Jahan Dotson. What if the Colts had traded for Stafford? So the Colts traded a third and a future first for Wentz instead of matching or beating L.A.’s offer of first-round picks in 2022 and 2023, plus Jared Goff and a third round pick. Indianapolis didn’t have a quarterback to offer like Goff, and Lions GM Brad Holmes claimed that the team viewed Goff as another first-round pick. So what if they made this trade offer instead: 2021 first-round pick (21st) 2021 second-round pick (54th) 2021 third-round pick (84th) 2022 first-round pick 2022 third-round pick Consider that the Browns traded three first-round picks for Deshaun Watson and the Broncos traded two first and two seconds for Russell Wilson. These deals came after Stafford. It would have been bold for Indianapolis to make this trade, but it was just as bold for Snead to make the trade offering a starting quarterback and two first-round picks. Would the Colts have won the Super Bowl with Stafford? With this trade, the Colts would be starting Stafford in 2021 instead of Wentz, playing for Frank Reich. Stafford would be paired with the NFL’s leading rusher that season, Jonathan Taylor. His top receiver would be Michael Pittman. Wentz did well in this offense, throwing 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions and the Colts ranked ninth in scoring. The Titans won the AFC South at 12-5 and 10-7 would have guaranteed Indy a wild card. Just won more win would have done it. Isn’t Stafford worth at least two wins over Wentz? Maybe the Colts don’t win the Super Bowl, but they show improvement and perhaps that leads to an improved receiver addition in 2022. Indy ended up drafting Alec Pierce in the second-round in 2022. What would’ve happened to the Rams? There’s no guaranteeing what the Rams would’ve done if they hadn’t secured Stafford in a trade in 2021. Goff had been soft-benched at the end of the 2020 season. The relationship was in disrepair. Cooper Kupp needed help. A report by Ian Rapoport said that Sean McVay was prepared to open a competition between Goff and John Wolford that offseason . In other words, the Rams would’ve kept shopping. They may not have landed anyone and the Rams didn’t have a first-round pick in 2021 because of the Jalen Ramsey trade. It’s hard to imagine L.A. winning the Super Bowl without Stafford that season given how important the deep passing attack was, both in the season and in the playoffs, including three late heroic drives in the postseason, including the Super Bowl. It’s possible that Snead wouldn’t have lasted longer than Ballard in this alternate universe. Snead and McVay were both extended in September of 2022. Would that be the case if Goff had led the team to a 9-8 record in 2021? Being bold can get you fired. In Ballard’s case, being timid was probably the culprit.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Davante Adams to miss 6-10 weeks with hamstring injury
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will place receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring that he suffered at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, according to Sean McVay. The receiver will miss between 6-10 weeks, which opens up the possibility that Adams will not return to the team […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will place receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring that he suffered at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, according to Sean McVay. The receiver will miss between 6-10 weeks, which opens up the possibility that Adams will not return to the team this season. If that is the case, have we seen the last of Davante Adams in the NFL? In addition, the Rams announced that Poona Ford is out for the year with a torn triceps, and Kobie Turner will miss 4-6 weeks with a groin injury. Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that WR Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and now will be sidelined 6-10 weeks. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 Adams came up limping on a non-contact injury on Sunday, moments before the Rams scored a go-ahead touchdown in the final minute. The team did not give any information on what happened to Adams or the extent of his injury after the game, until McVay’s comments on Monday that now point to an extended absence for star receiver. In six games, Adams caught 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns. That includes over 300 yards and two touchdowns in the two games that Puka Nacua missed due to a core injury. The Rams will have to turn to other options now, which could include an increased role for Tutu Atwell , but also Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, and sixth-round rookie C.J. Daniels. L.A. has largely kept their passing offense contained to Puka, Adams, and Tyler Higbee lately. The team’s other tight ends have not been productive in the passing game and second-year pro Terrance Ferguson is also on IR. Adams is a free agent in 2027 after completing a two-year, $44 million contract he signed in 2025. The Rams signed Aaron Donald to boost an already-stout defensive line, but now they lose Ford and Turner with Myles Garrett already on injured reserve. Turner is a free agent in 2027, making his case for an extension even more complicated. Ford was a run-stopper only and now L.A. must rely on players like Tyler Davis and Ty Hamilton to step up next week. Donald has not been the player he was before, even at the tail end, so now is the time for him to bring back a bit of that magic.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams place new kicker on IR with torn ACL
summary: The Rams need a new kicker again. Blake Grupe suffered a leg injury during L.A.‘s loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, and now the team has placed their latest kicker on injured reserve with a torn ACL on Monday afternoon. Grupe was injured while attempting a tackle in the second quarter, and his condition […]
full_text: The Rams need a new kicker again. Blake Grupe suffered a leg injury during L.A.‘s loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, and now the team has placed their latest kicker on injured reserve with a torn ACL on Monday afternoon. Grupe was injured while attempting a tackle in the second quarter, and his condition after the game suggested the injury could keep him sidelined for an extended period. The news preceded an even more devastating update, as the Rams expect Davante Adams to miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring . LA Rams Transactions: • Reserve/Injured K Blake Grupe pic.twitter.com/eiyLAZ82GF — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 19, 2026 Grupe was seen in the locker room after the game on crutches and wearing a leg brace, raising immediate concerns about his availability moving forward. The Rams’ special teams unit has already struggled with consistency this season, making the loss of their kicker another potential complication as Los Angeles looks to get its season back on track. The injury occurred on a tackle attempt on a 2nd quarter kickoff. While the full extent of Grupe’s injury has not been detailed here, being placed on IR means the Rams will need another option at kicker for the foreseeable future, at least for the next four weeks if not longer. JB Scott detailed a few available options after Sunday’s loss . Los Angeles will now have to evaluate its available options ahead of Week 7. Whether the team turns to a free-agent kicker or brings in another player, finding a reliable replacement will be critical to avoiding further special teams issues.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams’ investments in tight ends isn’t paying off
summary: In a dull, lackluster Sunday matinee performance, the Los Angeles Rams dropped a second straight home heartbreaker, falling 18-16 to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. L.A. came into the game as the NFL’s top yardage-producing offense, but left in a confused state, without a confident identity. Are they a building around a power run game, […]
full_text: In a dull, lackluster Sunday matinee performance, the Los Angeles Rams dropped a second straight home heartbreaker, falling 18-16 to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday . L.A. came into the game as the NFL’s top yardage-producing offense, but left in a confused state, without a confident identity. Are they a building around a power run game, using between the tackles duo/inside zone concepts and attacking through the air with under-center play action? Or sitting back in shotgun formation and throwing the football 68% (the last four games) of the time in an underneath quick-read attack? When asked about the team’s identity at the post-game presser, Sean McVay said: “We’re figuring it out, I can’t answer that right now…” The Rams have Matthew Stafford, a gunslinger at quarterback and have thrown 20+% of passes at or behind the line of scrimmage in the these two consecutive losses. More importantly, they don’t mesh like an integral part of the offense, spreading it around to get playmakers the ball in space or taking advantage of numerical advantages over defenders. Maybe it’s a rhetorical question, but can the Rams realistically boast of another playmaker besides Puka Nacua? Going into the season, McVay’s offense was seen as the evolutionary next step in 13 personnel and tight end development. Instead, the Rams sputtered against one of the worst defenses in the NFL on Sunday and tight ends combined for nine catches on 10 targets with 53 yards, one touchdown, and a critical lost fumble by Tyler Higbee. If you’re reading this you have more fantasy points than Tyler Higbee pic.twitter.com/2KZ6NTbchY — betr (@betr) October 18, 2026 The Rams entered the season with five tight ends, including second-round picks in 2025 and 2026. The Rams enter Week 7 with Higbee’s 246 yards eclipsing the combined total of all four other tight ends (181 yards between Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson, and Max Klare) and he was supposed to be the one taking a step back. Higbee had the most tight end snaps for the team on Sunday, followed by Parkinson, who has just 55 yards in six games despite a $9 million salary cap hit. Ferguson is on IR. Klare is an occasional special teamer with one snap on offense. Can this get better? Fans have seen this before in the past, the offense compressing the passing game into the underneath areas too often and the run game becoming an afterthought. The antidote is complicated and would take discipline. Staying with the run game and using play action could loosen things up. Another thought is re-visiting the past, making the opposition defend the whole field again, both width and length, particularly the middle of the field against deep zones. Identify some secondary playmakers to give the offense variety, Nacua is a generational player, but a healthy offense needs more options. The McVay offense used to dictate the flow of the game, alternately taking the full time to snap the ball and going up tempo, L.A. appears to have gotten away from this. A good example is how the Rams have performed offensively in the fourth quarter of 2026 games. A quicker pace has led them to charting 40 percent of their total season yardage and scoring 43 percent of their total points in the final stanza. Sitting at 2-4 and staring up from last place in the division is not time to control and keep the offense in a grip, trying to gut out wins, it’s time to play like there’s nothing left to lose. Here’s a look at the snap count review from Sunday, players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (58, 100%) Is Staff the problem or the solution? Time to cut bait on the season and go with Ty Simpson or should the Rams circle the wagons until the bye week before making such a big decision? While the latter seems the most judicious path, the offense needs to unhook the brakes and let it rip until then. Staff can still bring it, as proven by his fourth quarter work this season. The game plan has to to be faster and less predictable. Running back Kyren Williams (42, 72%), Blake Corum (16, 28%) Although the run game showed the hint of being something to build on, the game plan goes away from it too quickly. As a duo, Williams and Corum put in solid work on Sunday, just would have liked to see them get more. A combined 92 yards rushing on 19 carries and five catches on eight targets. Williams had a drop and another tougher off-target attempt that hit of his hand. There was a lot of open field, had it connected. Blake Corum takes the screen pass into the end zone ‼️ AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8polUTpXGE — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Wide receiver Puka Nacua (52, 90%) , Davante Adams (43, 74%) Again, is Puka Nacua the Rams only offense? He is so damned tough and clutch, he demands the opposition to roll the defense his way, but he appears too often alone. Only three targets until five minutes left in the game is a criminal offense. Adams has proven that he still has something to contribute at 34. Hopefully that late-game foot injury is minor, the room is wafer thin. Konata Mumpfield (27, 47%), Jordan Whittington (8,14%) Creating a composite WR#3, Mumpfield and Whittington have been on the field for 285 of 410 offensive plays (70%) with 20 targets and 10 catches. Not a lot of return on investment on for an offense that wants to air it out. Tight end Colby Parkinson (36, 72%), Tyler Higbee (48, 83%), Davis Allen (18, 31%) The Rams have staked a lot on the use of multiple tight end formation, both money and draft capital. To this point, it’s fair to say that it hasn’t improved the the run game enough for the offense to lean into it. Nor has L.A. used it to attack downfield. As a group, they are averaging less than 10 yards per catch. Offensive line David Quessenberry, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (58, 100%) Quessenberry was a pleasant surprise on the blind side, most expected a disaster. With the Rams throwing so much, the line will give up some pressures. I see the biggest pass blocking problem as the Rams inability to adjust to blitz calls and Sunday was no different. Maybe it was unexpected, Arizona hadn’t blitzed much in the first five weeks. But it’s not a new problem, blitz calls, particularly delayed, have been a a burr under the L.A. saddle all year. We have seen Sand Deuce mostly vs. 3×1 this year, but here it is vs. 2×2. This is the blitz path of the year, teams have run it a ton through 6 weeks, and we will continue to see it https://t.co/yNWDkkvK0h pic.twitter.com/q9A7l5qes0 — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) October 19, 2026 Special teams P Ethan Evans, LS Joe Cardona, K Blake Grupe Talk about adding injury to insult. In his maiden Rams voyage, Grupe drills a mid-length field goal and because of poor coverage on the ensuing kickoff , is forced into a making a tackle as the fail-safe option and tweaks a knee. Evans was on the cusp of an outstanding punting game, he dropped two inside the the five and got good first bounces, but the cover team couldn’t cash in. You never hear much about Cardona, means he’s doing well as long snapper. Defensive interior Aaron Donald (42, 58%), Braden Fiske (36, 50%) Just an idea, the L.A. defensive braintrust could consider lining up up Aaron Donald or Braden Fiske out on the edge at 7T on a handful of reps per game. With the Rams deep rotation at DT, It would be very interesting to see AD and Fiske playing as at wide defensive end. Donald is starting to round into shape, showing his move skills and making impact plays against both run and pass. Fiske played well, particularly on the move, but can get washed out by bigger, stronger offensive linemen when trying to hold ground. Kobie Turner (23, 32%), Pooona Ford (25, 35%), Tyler Davis (28, 39%), Ty Hamilton (18, 25%) The interior wasn’t bad per se against the Cardinals, but they did allow Arizona to control the game on the ground. While the unit as a whole, seems less stout than…

title: Analytics: Tutu Atwell is key to Rams’ passing offense
summary: Tutu Atwell was inactive during the L.A. Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, but Matthew Stafford may need him to be on the field more often if Sean McVay wants the offense to become more consistent from drive to drive. Atwell’s brief appearances this season have coincided with a great EPA per play […]
full_text: Tutu Atwell was inactive during the L.A. Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, but Matthew Stafford may need him to be on the field more often if Sean McVay wants the offense to become more consistent from drive to drive. Atwell’s brief appearances this season have coincided with a great EPA per play for the Rams’ offense, according to Sumer Sports, so should McVay make sure the veteran receiver is on the field next week? With Davante Adams suffering an injury late in the loss, the door is open for Atwell to earn a significantly larger role in McVay’s offense against the Las Vegas Raiders this week. Or is it too little, too late? #Rams offense with vs. without Tutu Atwell on the field per @SumerSports When Atwell's on the field Plays 59 EPA per play +0.213 Success rate 50.8% When Atwell's off the field Plays 351 EPA per play −0.016 Success rate 47.9% Small sample size but intriguing… pic.twitter.com/qgRtw8rTA1 — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) October 19, 2026 The Rams have struggled to find consistency throughout their 2026 campaign, and getting Atwell more involved would provide a much-needed spark. While Puka Nacua and Adams have commanded much of the attention in the passing game, Atwell possesses the speed and downfield ability to stretch opposing defenses in ways that can create opportunities for the entire offense. Atwell’s biggest value comes from his ability to threaten defenses vertically. His speed can force opposing cornerbacks to respect the deep ball, potentially opening up underneath routes for Nacua, Adams when healthy, and the Rams’ tight ends. Los Angeles needs to find more ways to manufacture explosive plays rather than relying on the same targets throughout every possession. Although he has only been targeted four times this season, Atwell is averaging a team-high 16.7 air yards per target according to Next Gen Stats . That’s the time of stretching that Stafford and McVay really need for an offense with Nacua and Adams. And the data clearly shows that the Rams offense is more explosive when Atwell is on the field. At the very least, Atwell should be on the field for every obvious 3rd down passing situation. And yet for some reason he has only been active for three games and was inactive on Sunday as the Rams only scored 16 points against a Cardinals defense that is among the worst in the NFL this season. To put this Rams game in perspective: The Cardinals defense has allowed 31, 36, 36, and 45 points in their last four. The Rams somehow have 9. This is absolutely insane lmao — Frank Ammirante (@FAmmiranteTFJ) October 18, 2026 Adams’ late-game injury against Arizona makes that opportunity even more important. Depending on the severity of the injury and his availability for Week 7, Atwell could see an expanded snap count and more opportunities to establish himself as a reliable contributor. Even if Adams returns quickly, the Rams should consider giving Atwell a more consistent role. L.A. cannot afford to let their offensive personnel become predictable, particularly as they attempt to climb back into contention in the NFC playoff picture. Rotating Atwell into more offensive packages could give quarterback Matthew Stafford another weapon capable of changing the complexion of a drive with one play. Atwell does not need to replace Adams’ production entirely to make a difference. He simply needs more opportunities to use his speed and create separation. If the Rams want a more explosive and dependable offense, getting Atwell involved should be a priority moving forward.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams have favorable upcoming schedule to right their season
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have fallen to 2-4 and though their season looks bleak, Sean McVay’s team isn’t out of contention yet. Their next four games are against teams that before the season started, fans would agree they should beat them all. The Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals. That’s followed by a bye week to […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have fallen to 2-4 and though their season looks bleak , Sean McVay’s team isn’t out of contention yet. Their next four games are against teams that before the season started, fans would agree they should beat them all. The Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals. That’s followed by a bye week to reset at midseason, potentially at 5-3 or 6-4. It may feel like the Rams have lost hope after losing to Arizona at home on Sunday, but we’ve seen McVay write this story before and come back from it to make the playoffs. This is a team winning the yardage battle, but not the scoreboard. The Rams have out-gained their opponents by a league-best 644 yards this season. They are 2-4. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) October 19, 2026 It’s not the end of the season yet They still have another 11 games to define their season. Their last three losses have been decided by one score. No moral victories in the NFL, sure, but this team is still competitive as the Rams aren’t getting steamrolled. They are fighting, they aren’t winning. If the Rams can improve on their level of play even just a tad, that could translate to the wins they are looking for. That could turn their one score losses into one score wins, or better. Those wins, could turn their season from a lost one, to a winning one. There’s still time. Are the Rams dead in the water? Technically, no. At 2-4, the Rams don’t have the worst record in the NFL, they aren’t eliminated from the playoffs, but in a season where they were projected as the best team in the NFL, a 2-4 start is a massive disappointment. It’s so disappointing that people are ready to fairly write the Rams off . Now, whereas writing the Rams off may be fair after six weeks, is it right? You’re telling me there’s a chance for L.A. to make the postseason? Yes. The Rams can still make the postseason. Although L.A. is technically in 14th place, they only have one more loss than the team in eighth place, which is the Seattle Seahawks. They’re only two games back of the team in fifth place, which is the Green Bay Packers. The Rams could win their next two games — against the Raiders, who have lost three in a row, and the Chargers, who have lost six in a row — and be right back at .500. A 4-4 record would certainly put L.A. in position to be in a wild card position by midseason. Consider that the Eagles just put Jalen Hurts on season-ending IR, and that even the Seahawks are struggling have lost three of the last four. It would be hard to justify hope in a tough conference, but that’s not what the NFC is right now. Not even close. The Rams can still turn their season around and breathe new life into this season. Unfortunately, McVay’s slow starts could once again doom the Rams to a wild card instead of a division title, and that is a problem. Wild cards don’t win Super Bowls, usually, and division winners do. The 49ers are aiming to go to 6-0 on Monday night against the Commanders, and L.A. could fall too far behind to catch up. But with Myles Garrett set to return in the next couple of weeks, the Rams hope, the best version of this team may not have been set yet. Losing to the Cardinals is a gut punch. It’s not the end of the match.
author: Danny Stone

title: Potential Rams trade target appears to hit the block
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams want to continue going all in this season, they should make a call to the Jacksonville Jaguars about wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The third-year receiver was rumored to be available in the offseason after an underwhelming second season and the Rams appeared to be a natural fit, but the […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams want to continue going all in this season, they should make a call to the Jacksonville Jaguars about wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The third-year receiver was rumored to be available in the offseason after an underwhelming second season and the Rams appeared to be a natural fit , but the Jaguars look to be more open to a quick move after benching Thomas in Week 6. Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen told reporters that guys “have to make plays” after benching Thomas at halftime. Liam Coen on Brian Thomas not playing in second half: Guys have to make plays. https://t.co/jX9qABvUUT — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) October 19, 2026 The timing is more interesting after Davante Adams suffered a non-contact injury against the Cardinals. After a stellar rookie season in 2024, Thomas took a step back in 2025 and has been at times completely out of the game plan for the Jags, including in Week 6 against the Houston Texans when he had multiple first-half gaffes and then didn’t play in the second half of a three-point loss. A change of scenery could help a player who still has undeniable speed and who would give the Rams another weapon to try to boost the offense in the wake of another difficult game against the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams are at a crossroads The preseason Super Bowl favorites are now 2-4 and suffered a crushing loss to the Cardinals at home this Sunday, leaving the franchise in an increasingly difficult spot. The division isn’t getting any easier to manage (even as the Seattle Seahawks try to find their footing), and the rest of the NFC still has a number of dangerous teams, even if the NFC East appears to be a pillow fight division this year. Only complicating things further is Davante Adams’s status after the veteran receiver left Sunday’s game in the final minute with an apparent non-contact injury. Davante Adams Hobbles Off The Sideline As He Is Clearly Injured In The Final Minute Of The Game. Looks Like He’s Holding His Knee And It’s A Non-Contact. Not Good. 😬 pic.twitter.com/OcFc90rm1l — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 18, 2026 So, in terms of doing something different and not just following this season’s current status quo, there are two paths the Rams can take. One would be to effectively pack it in and see what they’ve got in the way of future pieces. Or, they could double down on this offseason’s plan: doing every single thing possible to increase their odds of making a run to the Super Bowl. Thomas isn’t a perfect player by any means. After all, there’s a reason his role and impact have steadily decreased since his breakout rookie campaign. His “fear of contact” has been blamed for multiple drops. 🚨BRUTAL🚨 #Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. DROPPED another pass because he was looking toward an approaching defender before securing the football. BTJ fear of contact continues to lead to costly dropped passes — This is completely unacceptable. 😬😬😬 pic.twitter.com/Xz59kNvNro — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 18, 2026 But he brings something new to the table that Los Angeles just doesn’t have right now in terms of a proven commodity. In terms of down-to-down production, the Rams haven’t been a complete disaster on offense this year. As pointed out by Sheil Kapadia of The Ringer, no team has outgained their opponents by more yardage this year than L.A. has. In terms of series conversion rate, which is a measure of how many series are converted into either a new first down or touchdown (compared to field goals, punts and turnovers), the Rams have the seventh-best rate in the entire NFL. Unfortunately, that’s largely buoyed just by first-down pickups; the Rams are merely 16th in touchdown rate. The idea of adding Brian Thomas Jr. isn’t to fix or completely overhaul the offense, though, it simply comes down to trying to accumulate as much talent as possible. If Adams misses time, he immediately steps in as a secondary weapon at wide receiver behind Puka Nacua. He’s not the same type of receiver as Adams, but he’s produced before, he has dangerous speed and, frankly, he’d be better than nearly any other replacement you could find at this date. If Adams isn’t lost for the year, a trio of Nacua, Adams and Thomas is an extremely versatile group that checks a ton of boxes in terms of available skill sets. Plus, with Matthew Stafford not looking quite like his MVP peak from 2025, more feasible pass catchers can’t hurt his attempts to ramp up his production. Davante Adams Left knee (non-contact) vs Hamstring He’s grabbing the medial / anterior aspect of the knee. There’s a couple possibilities here: Bone bruise + hyperextension MCL sprain (usually contact) Meniscus tear (medial) Unable to rule out ACL tear. Bone bruise… pic.twitter.com/GPmRIVuysm — Jesse Morse, M.D. (@DrJesseMorse) October 18, 2026 The working theory, should Los Angeles pursue Thomas, would be that at some point simply having the most raw talent in the NFL (when paired with a top-tier coach) is enough to win enough games to earn a playoff berth and make a run to a title. You can only lean into that strategy so much with roster limitations, salary cap constraints, etc. needing to be considered, but this would be the kind of move that most aligns with that strategy. What would a trade cost? Obviously, the elephant in the room that hasn’t been addressed yet is trade compensation. It’s hard to gauge exactly what Thomas will fetch on the trade market, which is where he almost certainly resides given the situation in Jacksonville. Marvin Harrison Jr. was shipped from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans for a second-round pick and a sixth-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft. Thomas’s best season was far better than Harrison’s best, but if the prices are anywhere near similar it could be too rich of a price even if it is for a theoretically better player. Still, nothing would be outright shocking out of the Rams’ front office as the trade deadline approaches. Historically speaking, this is one of the most aggressive front offices in the NFL in terms of taking swings on high-end talent, at least in recent vintage. Los Angeles has to decide on its strategy for the rest of the season immediately. If it decides to keep the trend going from the summer, then the best way to get as much talent as possible is to call the Jaguars about Thomas. It’s not a guaranteed fix, but if you want to do anything you can to make a Super Bowl push, especially given how this season has started, then making a sizable gamble is a requirement.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Rams PFF grades: Matthew Stafford outright bad vs Cardinals
summary: The 1-4 Arizona Cardinals stunned the Los Angeles Rams this week with a 18-16 victory. Both teams are now at 2-4 and in last place in the NFC West division. A better-than-expected Raiders team is on deck. Vegas currently has a 3-3 record. This is a game the Rams should win, although we also said […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 18: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) looses the ball during the NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Rams on October 18, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 1-4 Arizona Cardinals stunned the Los Angeles Rams this week with a 18-16 victory . Both teams are now at 2-4 and in last place in the NFC West division. A better-than-expected Raiders team is on deck. Vegas currently has a 3-3 record. This is a game the Rams should win, although we also said that about Arizona. Before we turn the corner to the Raiders, let’s take a look at the individual performances from Week 6. These are the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades on each side of the ball. Top five grades on offense 1 – David Quessenberry, LT: 83.0 Quessenberry replaced Alaric Jackson at left tackle, who was suspended because of a post-game altercation with the Buffalo Bills. The veteran fill-in allowed two pressures in pass protection and earned a grade in this facet of 84.8. He also fared well in run blocking with a mark of 78.7. 2 – Blake Corum, RB: 77.9 Kyren Williams led the Rams with 10 carries at 5.0 yards per pop. Corum added nine of his own at a 4.7 clip. TE Davis Allen also earned a rush on a failed fourth down attempt. Corum did not have a single rush that netted negative yards. He was met with contact on an average depth of 1.48 yards versus Williams at 2.5 yards. Corum created 3.22 yards after contact on average while Williams was at 2.5. Corum forced three missed tackles. He was the better runner on Sunday. Blake Corum takes the screen pass into the end zone ‼️ AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8polUTpXGE — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 3 – Puka Nacua, WR: 74.7 Nacua did his best work against slot corner Kalen King. He caught all three of his targets for 57 yards, although only one of those went for a first down. In total Nacua finished with six catches on seven targets for 80 yards. 53 yards came after the catch point. In the game’s final moments, Nacua did everything he could to put the Rams in a position to win. They couldn’t get the job done. 4 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 68.6 Second-year receiver Konata Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 15 yards. He took over the third receiver role from Tutu Atwell this week. 5 – Davante Adams, WR: 68.2 Adams suffered a leg injury in the game’s final moments and his status moving forward is uncertain. When healthy he caught three of four targets for 39 yards with a long of 16. Only nine yards came after the catch point. Other notes on offense Matthew Stafford was the third-worst graded player on offense in front of Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee. He finished with a mark of 50.6 with one big-time throw and three turnover-worthy plays. Stafford had an average depth of target (ADOT) of just 5.3 yards. With three receivers, a backup tackle, and a running back comprising the top five grades, Stafford is running out of excuses for his individual poor play. After applying a 50% snap threshold, Stafford is currently PFF’s 17th-ranked signal caller by passing grade and 18th in overall offensive grade. In front of him are Aaron Rodgers, Cam Ward, and Geno Smith. There has been talk of benching Ward. It’s time to acknowledge that the Rams should consider sitting Stafford down as well . Top five grades on defense 1 – Josh Wallace, CB: 84.7 Jacoby Brissett targeted Josh Wallace in coverage eight times and was punished for doing so. Wallace allowed four receptions for just 20 yards and 100% of the yardage came after the catch point. The Cardinals often leveraged screen plays. The backup corner was also active in run defense with four stops. 2 – Quentin Lake, DB: 81.1 Lake also had an active role in coverage. He was targeted six times, allowing five receptions for 44 yards (28 after the catch) with an interception. Lake tied Nate Landman for the team lead in tackles with seven solo. It was a nice bounce back performance after he struggled last week. Quentin Lake INT! AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SI43YVW2NQ — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 3 – Wesley Bailey, EDGE: 80.1 Bailey had virtually no pass rush production on seven rushes. He did his best work as a run defender on nine such plays. His PFF run defense grade was 81.9 and the highest on the defense against Arizona. 4 – Aaron Donald, DT: 78.9 Inversely, Donald finished with LA’s best pass rushing grade at 73.9. He pressured Brissett twice. Byron Young led the defense in pressures with three. Brissett was not sacked. 5 – Omar Speights, MLB: 70.6 Speights earned low marks in tackling (one miss) at 39.2 and coverage with 49.1 (allowed two catches for 22 yards). He made three run stops and earned a mark of 76.6. This was the second-highest run defense grade behind Bailey. Other notes on defense Second-year defensive tackle Ty Hamilton played 18 snaps and earned a lowly grade of 35.0. His season grade is at 32.9. The Rams should reconsider whether it’s wise to carve out a role for him.

title: The Rams might already be dead in the water
summary: At 2-4. the season might already be over for the Los Angeles Rams. LA may need to win 10 games in order to make the postseason. The playoffs would wipe the slate clean. All it takes it earning a spot in the tournament. The rest is a matter of taking care of business. But getting […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 18: Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) looking for the blocking during the NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Rams on October 18, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At 2-4. the season might already be over for the Los Angeles Rams. LA may need to win 10 games in order to make the postseason. The playoffs would wipe the slate clean. All it takes it earning a spot in the tournament. The rest is a matter of taking care of business. But getting there would mean a 8-3 record over the final 11 regular season games. Why are 10 wins needed? Because the Silver Bulletin is projecting three NFC teams (Rams, Packers, Bears) to finish with a 9-win record. The Rams could reasonably make the playoffs with nine wins, although their chances suddenly come down to factors outside of their control. The Packers and Bears are also 4-2 currently. Both have battled early season struggles—in Chicago’s case missing Caleb Williams—to bounce back in resounding fashion. The Rams would need to keep pace with these teams and pull ahead by year’s end. That isn’t easy either. So how likely would 10 wins be? It’s a difficult path. Week 7 at Las Vegas Raiders After starting 3-0, the Raiders have dropped three-straight to fall to .500. This is a game the Rams should win, although they were also expected to trounce a 1-4 Cardinals team. We know that didn’t happen. Why should we be optimistic about their chances in Vegas? Week 10 at Arizona Cardinals The Rams would likely be favored in a rematch. Assuming Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett play in this game after missing the first matchup, these changes would seem to favor LA. However, we can’t count this as an automatic win after the Rams just suffered a disappointing loss to this team. Week 12 vs Green Bay Packers One of the most non-NFC West games left on the Rams’ schedule. Winning the NFC West is probably out of the picture at this point. LA is instead competing against the likes of the Packers, assuming they don’t win the NFC North and enter the playoffs as a division winner. The Rams will need this game for head-to-head and strength of schedule tiebreakers. In turn, losing this matchup would be catastrophic. Week 13 vs Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are undefeated at 5-0. Similar to the 49ers, they haven’t really been challenged much yet this season. They have a point differential of 57, which means on average they are winning by more than 10 points per game. Week 14 at San Francisco 49ers Getting back on track means the Rams must fare well in their divisional matchups. Three games remaining against the 49ers and Seahawks gives LA upside potential. It also means three contests against formidable foes. We know Week 1 against San Francisco wasn’t particularly close. LA’s injury woes have only gotten worse. Why should we expect a different outcome this time? Week 16 at Seattle Seahawks Week 18 vs Seattle Seahawks The Rams will finish the regular season facing Seattle in two of the last three games. The currently 1-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers are sandwiched in between. There is a chance that Seattle already has a playoff berth locked up heading into the season finale. That could benefit the Rams if they choose to rest starters. But if the Seahawks are in full force this will likely be a close game.

summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams. Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick didn;t […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams. Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick didn;t play after throwing eight passes in a mop-up role in a lopsided Week 5 defeat. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played all 68 defensive snaps. He bounced back after being picked on at New England last week. it was a good sign for his overall growth as a starting player. Being resilient is paramount for a defensive back. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick was was active after missing Week 5 with a knee injury. He played four snaps on offensive and six on special teams, which has been about the norm for him. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick didn’t play on defense against Buffalo after he played 12 snaps on defense, his second defensive action this season, in Week 5. He did play 15 snaps on special teams. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played a season high 23 snaps a week after playing a season-low five offensive snaps. Washington had 43 yards on nine carries and had two runs of 10-pus yards. Getting Washington more involved is key to igniting the Raiders stagnant running game. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the fifth team in six games. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played is definitely not a starter anymore, losing his job to Darien Porter, who began the season as a starter before losing his job to Masses briefly. Masses played just 19 percent of the snaps after playing 33 percent in Week 5. He was mostly in dime packages against Buffalo and was benched after pass interference call. Let’s see how much he plays against the Rams. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played played just eight offensive snaps with no targets. The training camp star has two catches for 12 yards on eight targets this season.

The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. The Raiders traded Adams […]
full_text: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images A long-awaited reunion game will not occur Sunday. The Los Angeles Rams announced that starting wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring in a loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday and he will miss the next 6-10 weeks. The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. The Raiders traded Adams to the New York Jets in 2024 after he requested to be traded from the team he worked to join in 2022. The Raiders sent a first and second round pick to the Green Bay Packers for Adams in 2022 to reunite him with Fresno State teammate Derek Carr. Adams played well for the Raiders, but his relationship with the franchise soured after Carr was released after the 2022 season. Adams, who turns 34 in December, in his second season with the Rams. The Rams are battered. They will also be without defensive tackles Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. Myles Garrett will not return this week, either.

title: Las Vegas Raiders aren’t getting enough from Tyler Linderbaum, especially in Week 6 loss to Buffalo Bills
summary: Two things can be true about the Las Vegas Raiders’ 3-3 start to the 2026 season. One, the Raiders are playing better than expected, where the rebuild is at least on pace and may even be slightly ahead of schedule. Two, after starting 3-0, dropping three games in a row against legitimate AFC playoff contenders […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two things can be true about the Las Vegas Raiders’ 3-3 start to the 2026 season. One, the Raiders are playing better than expected, where the rebuild is at least on pace and may even be slightly ahead of schedule. Two, after starting 3-0, dropping three games in a row against legitimate AFC playoff contenders is disappointing and makes any postseason hopes feel like more of a pipe dream than a reality this fall. Las Vegas was at least competitive in a three-point loss to the Buffalo Bills, giving room for optimism when it comes to the Week 6 winners and losers. But, at the same time, there are still plenty of holes to patch up, starting with a few offseason free agent signings. LOSER: Tyler Linderbaum To be clear, Linderbaum hasn’t been “bad” this season and by no means should be replaced in the starting lineup. But the Raiders didn’t make him the highest-paid center in NFL history by $9 million a year to be Pro Football Focus’ 22nd-ranked center with a 58.8 grade through the first six weeks of the campaign. Sunday was an especially bad outing, as he looked outmatched against Bills’ defensive tackle Deone Walker, posting a season-low 46.8 mark . “I didn’t feel good about it,” Linderbaum replied when asked about his Week 6 performance, via Raider Nation Radio on X/Twitter . “I let 96 (Walker) dictate the game one me. Great player, credit to him, he came out ready to play. I’ve just got to play better for the team. [The Raiders] brought me here to be a great run blocker and a great pass protector; I just feel like I let a lot of my teammates down today.” While Walker is having an excellent season, the free-agent addition is supposed to be a Top 5 center in the NFL. That, plus the massive contract, comes with a higher level of expectations, where he, at least, needs to hold his own against top competition. So far, Linderbaum hasn’t held up his end of the bargain and needs to pick it up over the next 11 games, especially since he was brought in to elevate the rest of the offensive line. He also committed his third penalty on a tush-push play. He needs to clean that up as well. LOSER: Quay Walker For the second week in a row, Walker got picked on in coverage. He was targeted six times and gave up six completions for 76 yards and a touchdown for a perfect 158.3 passer rating. Also, 60 or nearly 80 percent of the yards came after the catch, per PFF . The free-signing is having a good year as a run defender, but he continues to have issues in coverage that opposing offenses have started to exploit. WINNER: Treydan Stukes It’s hard to find silver linings on a defense that gave up 33 points, but Stukes had an impressive outing after having the worst game of his young career the week before. The rookie was all over the field with nine total tackles (third-most on the team), posting a season-high three “ defensive stops ”, per PFF . That helped him post another personal best with a 74.2 run defense grade, and he was solid in coverage as well. Stukes drew five targets and did allow four completions but for just 17 yards. The one notable reception he gave up was an 11-yard grab to wide receiver Keon Coleman, where the defensive back was in position to contest the catch and just lost at the catch point. So, the four other targets resulted in just six yards and a pass breakup. That’s something the second-round pick can build on moving forward. LOSER: Darien Porter On the other end of the spectrum in the secondary, Las Vegas is struggling to find its second starting cornerback. While Eric Stokes had arguably his best game of the season, Porter might have had his worst. The latter was targeted five times and gave up 59 yards on three completions, while the two incompletions were drops. That led to Hezekiah Masses getting more reps in the second half, who also had issues, drawing a penalty on his lone target. Inconsistency has been the story of Porter’s young career. He’ll look like the best corner on the roster one week and then lay an egg in the next game. At some point, that has to get ironed out if the 2025 third-round pick is going to become a reliable starter moving forward. LOSER: Ashton Jeanty One of the themes for this week’s losers is players who aren’t living up to the billing, and Jeanty falls into that category. Yes, the offensive line leaves something to be desired, but the No. 6 overall pick hasn’t shown that he’s the caliber of back to help overcome issues up front and collect rushing yards over expected (RYOE). This season, he ranks 25th at the position with negative 15.2 RYOE, per Muffed.ai , and is tied for 26th in missed tackles forced with nine, according to PFF . The latter was especially bad on Sunday, as Jeanty failed to record a single MTF. That’s understandable if he’s dealing with an injury. But, at the same time, if a bum ankle and/or foot are causing him to be ineffective on the field, then it’s time to sit and heal up. On top of that, the Boise State product dropped his fifth pass of the season and second in as many weeks. It’s time to increase Mike Washington Jr.’s and Dylan Laube’s workloads because Jeanty simply isn’t getting it done right now. WINNER: Michael Mayer On a more positive note, Mayer continues to have a career season after getting an early contract extension. His seven catches for 95 yards tie for the third-most and the most he’s had in a single game. Also, the fourth-year pro is seven catches and 62 yards away from setting personal bests in both metrics for an entire season, and there are still 11 games left to play. Mayer did a lot of work after the catch against the Bills, recording 67 yards — or over 70 percent of his total — with the ball in his hands. That gives him 158 YAC on the season and puts him second behind Travis Kelce (196) for the most among tight ends, per PFF . WINNER: Tre Tucker Las Vegas’ wide receiver room has been a big talking point during the 2026 campaign, with many waiting for someone in the position group to step up and be productive. With Brock Bowers not having the same impact on Sunday as the Raiders have come to expect over the last month, the fourth-year wideout stepped up and led the team with five catches for 97 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Among the scores was an explosive 44-yarder that cut the fourth-quarter deficit to three points, giving the Silver and Black a chance to tie or win the game after a successful onside kick. The latter didn’t happen, but Tucker did his part to put the opportunity on the table. LOSER: Defensive Tackles It’s no secret that the Raiders’ defensive tackles leave a lot to be desired. But it feels like the Bills game was another reminder of just how big an issue that position group is. Running back James Cook III had 22 carries for 95 yards (4.3 ypc) and a touchdown, and a lot of his production came from runs that were right up the gut. Meanwhile, Adam Butler led the Raiders’ DTs with a 60.4 PFF run defense grade , just 0.4 points above the baseline. The defense is clearly missing a gap filler in the middle of the trenches right now. Perhaps getting Tonka Hemingway back from a concussion this week will help.
author: Matt Holder

title: Close but no cigar as visiting Bills eke out a 33-30 win over Raiders
summary: Those inside Allegiant Stadium on Sunday afternoon were treated to an old-fashioned third-quarter magic show as Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills offense pulled a rabbit out of their hat on a wild touchdown toss in the red zone. The dazzling display of never giving up on a play resulted in the Bills quarterback Josh […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Those inside Allegiant Stadium on Sunday afternoon were treated to an old-fashioned third-quarter magic show as Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills offense pulled a rabbit out of their hat on a wild touchdown toss in the red zone. The dazzling display of never giving up on a play resulted in the Bills quarterback Josh Allen flicking the ball to wide receiver Keon Coleman for the 12-yard score to vault Buffalo’s led to 23-16 — an advantage it would hold the rest of the way — highlighting the visitors resilience while also showcasing the host Las Vegas Raiders’ lack of coaching and player execution on defense as the Silver & Black fell 33-30. Las Vegas didn’t go away quietly, however, finally going with deep throws culminating in wide receiver Tre Tucker’s 44-yard diving touchdown catch on a throw from quarterback Kirk Cousins, but the onside drop kick went way too high with Buffalo kneeling the ball to run out the clock. Credit to the Raiders for keeping it close. The team put forth a better effort in a three-point loss than the shellacking in New England in Week 5. However, close isn’t good enough in the NFL and valiant showings don’t necessarily reflect in the final score — and more importantly, the standings — as Klint Kubiak’s Raiders have dropped three-straight games after Sunday’s defeat. “I just want to say very disappointed. Very disappointed that we didn’t get it done today,” Kubiak began his postgame press conference. “Credit to Buffalo; they played a great game. As a team, we did not close the game, and there’s plenty of improvement. But we are not satisfied with any moral victories, and we’re a 3-3 football team with everything ahead of us. Avoided injuries today, so we’re moving forward, but we didn’t get it done today.” lol. pic.twitter.com/afZJM11h7D — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 18, 2026 Forgive Kubiak if the moral victories portion of his presser opener stings a bit. He’s not steeped in the Raiders’ patented ineptitude as many long-time fans are. And for those ardent folks in Raider Nation — buried underneath a mountainous pile of losing the team has done — “close” and “almost” are gargantuan leaps to what they’ve had to bear witness too. Kubiak’s standard is way higher, but the constant pummeling the loyal fanbase has taken, the miniscule crumb that’s the slightest glimmer of hope is a five-course meal for the famished. That noted, it’s difficult to not feel Kubiak’s disappointment. Throughout the game, the Raiders briefly took a lead and tied the contest against a high-octane Bills defense. But miscues in all three phases of the game haunted Las Vegas even when its red zone defense stymied Buffalo. Joe Brady’s Bills offense went 3-of-5 in the red zone while Kubiak’s attack went 2-of-5 and having just one more end zone visit in the area between the opponent’s 20-yard line and goal line was a big difference. As was the lone turnover of the contest, committed by the Raiders. Which makes the mistakes in a variety of aspects — on offense, center Tyler Linderbaum’s false start on 4th-and-short; on defense, eye violations that left Allen and running back James Cook open for a 29-yard catch and run on 3rd-and-3 in the 4th quarter (led to touchdown); on special teams a facemask penalty on Segun Olubi on a punt return — highlight bad complementary football stand out for the Raiders. And the third quarter duds from Las Vegas offense only compounds matters. “It’s happened three times, and it’s killing us, absolutely killing us, and I have not fixed it. So, shame on me. It’s on me to get it fixed,” Kubiak said of Linderbaum’s false start and penchant to do so in short-yardage situations. “I’m really upset with how we’re starting the third quarter. Go three and out. That’s disappointing,” Kubiak added about the team’s third stanza performance. “Every game has adversity. The game’s not over in the third quarter when you go three and out, but it really kills more than that.” The Raiders didn’t get dog walked in Week 6 like it did in Week 5, so progress is being made. And like previous games, there’s plenty of teach tape for coaches and players to pour over and correct as the team preps for Week 7. "WHOAAAAA" "Incredible!" Kirk Cousins to Tre Tucker had Jim & @JJWatt fired up 🚀 @Raiders pic.twitter.com/yGaFa5YZvC — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Tucker torched the Bills secondary on his fourth-quarter touchdown: —Tremendous credit to and effort by Bills cornerback Christian Benford who was tasked quite often with one-on-one coverage on Raiders elite pass catcher Brock Bowers. Benford won more matchups than he lost against Bowers and when Buffalo didn’t have their top corner on Las Vegas’ tight end, Bowers hauled in back-to-back 18- and 29-yard passes on the Raiders’ nine-play, 91-yard fourth-quarter touchdown drive to tie the game at 23. —Both Tucker and tight end Michael Mayer came close to eclipsing the 100-yard receiving mark with 97 and 95, respectively. The fleet-footed wide receiver hauled in five passes and two touchdowns on seven targets while the tight end caught seven passes on nine targets. —Cousins finished 23 of 41 for 313 yards and two touchdown passes with one awful interception. He did avoid getting sacked but took a few hits from Buffalo’s defense. His counterpart, Allen, finished 23 of 33 for 255 yards and two touchdown passes. He was sacked twice. —Raiders defensive end Kwity Paye finally got back in the sack column with his takedown of Allen. Linebacker Quay Walker collected the team’s other sack on a perfectly called blitz in the first quarter. But overall, it was an up-and-down performance from the unit. —The kickers for both teams got plenty of work in this contest as Buffalo’s Tyler Bass went 4-for-4 on field goals with a long of 47. Las Vegas’ Matt Gay finished 3-for-3 with a long of 35. Raiders punter AJ Cole III ended up with three punts for 166 yards (55.3 yards per boot average) with one dropping inside the Bills’ 20-yard line (long of 57). Quote of Note “Yeah, there’s no doubt that, that’s what it is. We got to find ways to close. You got to find the inches in the fourth quarter. You can’t go out in second to last possession and have three incompletions. You can’t in the third quarter throw an interception that gives them a short field and they get a touchdown off of it. You can’t go two for five in the red zone. You know third and goal, we got to come away with those four point plays and get the touchdown, not the kick in the field goal. Those are all the plays throughout the game that you look back on and you say, it didn’t give us a chance to win.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on what it would take to close games out. title: Does Zach Sieler want to be traded away from Miami Dolphins?
summary: The Miami Dolphins remain winless on the season — sitting at 0-5 after a much needed bye week this past Sunday. As the team continues to try and get better, the vultures have already begun circling. According to various reports, teams have been ringing general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan to check on the availability of certain […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins defensive end Zach Sieler (92) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins remain winless on the season — sitting at 0-5 after a much needed bye week this past Sunday. As the team continues to try and get better, the vultures have already begun circling. According to various reports, teams have been ringing general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan to check on the availability of certain players in regards to potential trades. Dolphins veteran defensive tackle, Zach Sieler, is one such player. On Monday, Sieler met with the South Florida media, and the defensive lineman was asked about the possibility of being traded away from the Miami Dolphins as the trade deadline approaches. “I know people say rumors or talk, or whatever, this time of year, but you know, I’m here focused playing games here to win for the Dolphins, man. I think we’re doing a great thing and I’m excited for this next week coming up — coming off the bye ready to roll.” Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post then asked Sieler directly if he would be open to being dealt to a contender this season. “I love it here. I’ve been here for how long? I want to win here as a Dolphin. I think [head coach Jeff] Hafley and [general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan] Sully did an amazing job here. I’m excited to see this team is growing and [to see] where we’re going — let’s get some wins.” At 31-years of age, no one would blame Sullivan if he did decide to unload Sieler for some extra draft capital. However, according to Sieler, it seems he wants to remain a member of the Dolphins for the foreseeable future. The National Football League’s trade deadline is three weeks and a day from today — on Tuesday, November 10th. We will see if Miami’s longtime defensive stalwart continues to wear aqua and orange past that consequential day.

title: Miami Dolphins Trade Deadline Primer: The Top Candidates To Buy and Sell
summary: Miami Dolphins General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan has already shown a willingness to sacrifice short-term talent for long-term assets. Last offseason, the Dolphins dealt Jaylen Waddle to the Denver Broncos in a move that helped build one of the league’s largest collections of draft capital entering the 2026 NFL Draft. As the Nov. 10 trade deadline […]
full_text: Miami Dolphins General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan has already shown a willingness to sacrifice short-term talent for long-term assets. Last offseason, the Dolphins dealt Jaylen Waddle to the Denver Broncos in a move that helped build one of the league’s largest collections of draft capital entering the 2026 NFL Draft. As the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches, the question becomes whether Sullivan has another move or two up his sleeve. National analysts have identified several Dolphins as potential trade candidates, with three names appearing more often than the rest: Austin Jackson, Joshua Uche and Zach Sieler. The Dolphins as Sellers T Austin Jackson Alain Poupart, Sports Illustrated : “Jackson is scheduled to become a free agent after the season and he’s got a low base salary that would make him attractive financially to other teams.” Carter Bahns, CBS Sports : “Tackles are always in demand. He would be an affordable half-season rental.” Anthony DiMoro, Heavy : “With offensive lines such as the Philadelphia Eagles decimated either by departures or injuries, Jackson immediately steps in as a starting right tackle for the majority of offensive line-starved teams in the NFL.” Kyle Crabbs, Yahoo Sports : “Given his durability concerns and lack of a low end contract, Jackson has the makings of a perfect insurance rental at offensive tackle for a contending team.” Potential buyer: Jaguars, which is currently without standout tackle Anton Harrison. It’s easy to see why Jackson has emerged as the consensus favorite to be moved. Starting-caliber offensive tackles rarely become available, and Miami has already spent much of the season evaluating younger offensive linemen. If Sullivan is looking for the cleanest path to adding draft capital, Jackson may be it. EDGE Joshua Uche Alex Kay, Bleacher Report : “Parting with a late-round pick to bolster the defensive front with a player who recorded 11.5 sacks as recently as the 2022 season is worth the risk.” Potential buyer: Ravens Dan Graziano, ESPN : “He’s a seven-year veteran who’s playing well for a team in the first year of a significant rebuild. If the Dolphins get the opportunity to turn this signing into a useful draft pick, it’s not at all hard to imagine them jumping on it.” Uche presents the opposite dilemma. Unlike Jackson, there appears to be a real argument for keeping him: He has played well, fits the age profile of a player who could still contribute when Miami is ready to compete again and likely wouldn’t command a massive contract extension. The question becomes whether the Dolphins value a future draft pick more than continuity in the pass rush. DT Zach Sieler Poupart: “Sieler is coming off his best performance of the season and he remains a solid, at times very good, interior defensive lineman, but he will be 32 at the start of the 2026 season. That could be a problem for Miami, though not for a contender looking for D-line help.” Antwan Staley, Athlon Sports : “With no guaranteed money remaining on his contract after the 2026 season, the Dolphins could release Sieler next offseason. Ideally, they’d like at least an early Day 3 pick, possibly from a contending team that needs interior defensive help.” Jason La Canfora, Casino.org : “While Sieler is now in his 30s, he continues to draw double teams at the line of scrimmage despite limited help around him. As Miami seeks to accumulate draft capital, Sieler becomes a prime trading chip.” Sieler is arguably Miami’s best trade chip, but he’s also the player who would be hardest to replace. While most rebuilding teams listen when contenders come calling about veterans in their 30s, moving one of the locker room’s most respected veterans would send a signal that Miami is prioritizing future assets over short-term competitiveness. While a handful of Dolphins have surfaced in trade speculation, those three names consistently appeared across multiple national outlets. It’s worth noting that trading Sieler would result in a $10 million dead cap for 2026 and a $24+ million dead cap for 2027. A Jackson trade would result in a $4.5 million dead cap for 2026 and $14 million in 2027. Trading Uche would result in a dead cap for 2026 of just $600,000. (These stats courtesy of Spotrac .) Other Names To Watch None of these players surfaced as frequently as Jackson, Uche, or Sieler, but each has factors that could make him expendable if Miami receives the right offer. LB Willie Gay Jr. Justin Carter, Fansided : “With Rodriguez and Brooks both playing 90 percent or more of snaps, Gay’s 50 percent snap share can be replaced by getting Jackson Woodard or Liam Anderson on the field more.” WR Jalen Tolbert James Brizuela, Yahoo Sports : “Tolbert may not be utilized in the correct way with the Dolphins, but he could be a strong rotational option for another team that needs a boost to their wide receiver department.” S Zayne Anderson Carter: “Anderson ranks 30th among safeties in PFF grade. He’s only allowed two receptions all season and ranks first among safeties in yards allowed per reception.” The Dolphins as Buyers? While most trade deadline discussion has focused on the Dolphins as sellers, Miami could just as easily explore opportunities to acquire young talent. The roster remains one of the league’s youngest, and rebuilding teams sometimes use the deadline to take chances on players whose value has dipped elsewhere. The Dolphins have only $6 million and change in cap room for 2026 , which limits who they might be able to bring in. Just the same, here are a few names to keep an eye out for: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. One of the most discussed trade targets this season, Thomas is two years removed from a 1,200-yard, 10-touchdown rookie season that earned him a Pro Bowl nod. He’s young (24) and still on his rookie contract, which as a former first-round pick includes a fifth-year option. His affordability and potential could cost a Day 2 pick in the 2027 draft, making him a more expensive target than others on this list. Vikings WR Jauan Jennings Back in the offseason, the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson reported the team was interested in then-free agent Jennings, who ended up signing an $8 million one-year deal with the Vikings. The 29-year-old has been a dud in Minnesota this season (2 receptions for 9 yards), but the previous two years Jennings caught 15 touchdowns and 1,600 yards for the 49ers. Adding him would cost the Dolphins maybe $2 million the rest of the season but give the team a reliable possession receiver already familiar with Bobby Slowik’s offense. Titans DL Solomon Thomas The Dolphins are already in need of defensive line help, a need that will become even more pressing if they trade Uche. Maybe they can rehab another veteran lineman in Solomon Thomas, who has 18.5 sacks and 145 tackles over a 10-year career. Now, it’s possible he’s washed up, but at low salary ($1-2 million) and acquisition costs, he might be worth a look. Browns WR Jerry Jeudy Two years off a 1,200-yard Pro Bowl season, Jeudy is languishing with the Browns (12 receptions for 150 yards) and ranks fifth on the team in receptions. The 27-year-old could probably be had for a Day 3 pick, and the Dolphins would only owe him about $1 million for the rest of the season. Jeudy has a non-guaranteed $22.9 million salary for 2027 that would need to be restructured. Whether the Dolphins ultimately buy, sell or do some combination of both, the deadline should offer another glimpse into Sullivan’s long-term vision. Last offseason he was willing to move a popular player like Jaylen Waddle in exchange for future assets. If a contender comes calling for Austin Jackson, Joshua Uche, Zach Sieler or some other veteran, we’ll see whether that philosophy still applies.
