title: Is there a trust issue between Jalen Hurts and the Eagles?
summary: Much has happened to the Eagles over the last 72 hours. They lost for the fourth-straight time for the first time in head coach Nick Sirianni’s tenure on Sunday. And then at 10:10 a.m. on Monday, it was revealed they will be without franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of what has been a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Much has happened to the Eagles over the last 72 hours. They lost for the fourth-straight time for the first time in head coach Nick Sirianni’s tenure on Sunday. And then at 10:10 a.m. on Monday, it was revealed they will be without franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of what has been a failing season , after what was originally diagnosed by the Eagles as a “superficial” blood clot in Hurts’ left calf spread to his lungs, a danger area that could cause a pulmonary embolism, which is a sudden, life-threatening medical condition that occurs when a blood clot travels through the bloodstream and blocks an artery in the lungs. It was interesting that Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn and the Eagles released a joint statement— not just from the Eagles —about the blood clot situation on Monday under the headline: “Statement on the health status of QB Jalen Hurts from the Philadelphia Eagles and Jalen Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn: “Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. “Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [I.E. “blood thinners”]. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football. “Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that we will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. “We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery.” On Saturday, ESPN first reported the Eagles would NOT place Hurts on injured reserve, then changed it to the Eagles putting Hurts on IR, which would have forced Hurts to automatically miss the next four games. That changed once again on Monday, when Hurts and his personal team, in conjunction with the Eagles, ruled him out for the season. There was an interesting line in the ESPN corrected report on Saturday, October 17, that stated Hurts would be on IR, saying: “Philadelphia believes the blood clot is treatable, and the ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, with the Eagles ready to follow his lead.” The glaring part of that was “when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team,” suggesting that Hurts went outside the Eagles medical staff to get another opinion— from his medical team . But in today’s NFL, many players often seek second and third medical opinions using their own people—and leaving the playing decision up to them. Where does this leave Hurts in the Eagles’ future? One thing is for certain, some close to Hurts were not happy with how the Eagles dealt with the blood clot situation. They also felt Hurts should have been treated far better by the team this offseason by offering another contract extension. The Eagles never budged. With the perception of how the Eagles dealt with Hurts’ situation, coupled with the looming contract extension, it may not help the relationship. “The Eagles run a first-class operation and we’re talking about an NFL player who I’m sure was not flying commercial,” said Dr. David Chao, the former Head Team Physician for the San Diego Chargers. “I’m sure Jalen Hurts, a starting NFL quarterback, was not squeezed in the middle seat between two people on a plane. I would assume the Eagles made the proper precautions like every other NFL medical staff would for team flights. It is completely normal for players to get second and third opinions. “But it is an unbelievably dangerous situation if left untreated. The fact that it got to his lungs is a big, red warning light. It’s the reason why he is not playing anymore this season. I can understand why his family and friends would be upset, but if they knew flying was not great, so, too, did the Eagles’ medical staff. They would never have [knowingly] put a player in danger like that.” The 28-year-old Hurts has a five-year, $255 million contract that runs through 2028. This is the caveat in the deal: His guaranteed salary falls from $51.5 million this season to $22 million next year, to zero in 2028. Hurts came under offseason scrutiny that some around him found unfair, though Eagles’ owner Jeffrey Lurie came out with glowing things to say about Hurts on March 31, at the NFL Annual League Meetings in Arizona, saying: “I mean, there’s no bigger fan of Jalen than me. Clutch gene, absolutely. The guy, MVP of the Super Bowl 13 months ago, should have been MVP of the Super Bowl right before that against, yeah, Kansas City the first time, exceptional and so dedicated. I mean, I think you probably know, I spent a lot of time with Jalen, and he’s, as I do with most quarterbacks, and incredibly dedicated to the game, to winning, and being a huge winner, and I love everything about him. So anyway, those things take time. We never would discuss it. He’s in the middle of a new contract now.” Now, Hurts is laid up with a serious issue that may push back or may push forward how long he remains a Philadelphia Eagle. In six years as a starter, Hurts has a 59-28 record, he’s led the Eagles to five-straight playoff berths, which will obviously end this season, three NFC East titles, two Super Bowls, one Super Bowl championship and has a 6-4 postseason record. No Eagles quarterback comes close to that winning resume. When he walked off the field in London with 8 seconds left after leading the Eagles to a 17-16 lead against Jacksonville, it might’ve been the last Philadelphia saw of the most winning quarterback in franchise history.
author: Joseph Santoliquito

title: Eagles-Panthers Film Review: Sean Mannion should probably be replaced
summary: I’m completely done with this offense. I’ve been mad in the past, but never completely out on the whole offense so early into a season. I always try to seek positives. Those of you who have read my work for a while will know that I rarely call for a player to be benched or […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I’m completely done with this offense. I’ve been mad in the past, but never completely out on the whole offense so early into a season. I always try to seek positives. Those of you who have read my work for a while will know that I rarely call for a player to be benched or a coach to be fired. I would much rather explain what is going wrong and look for ways to fix it. But after watching the Eagles’ offense against the Panthers, I think Sean Mannion (you can add more if you want) should probably go. This under-center, outside zone offense he brought in has been dreadful, and I don’t see a coach who looks ready to solve the problems his own system is creating. With so little coaching experience, he looks completely out of his depth. I know fans will rightly call for Nick Sirianni, too. I am not defending him at all. He is the head coach, and he is responsible for allowing this to continue. But replacing the offensive coordinator and handing the offense to Josh Grizzard, or even Sirianni himself, is a more straightforward immediate change than firing the head coach. If Sirianni has to take over, let him deal with it. He’s the head coach. What I absolutely cannot get behind is giving Mannion even more responsibility. Or fire them both, whatever. I just can’t keep watching the same thing every week! It’s driving me crazy. The injuries are real, but this was a Panthers defense with both of its top two cornerbacks on injured reserve and Jaelan Phillips playing only 28 snaps. There were matchups to exploit. There were opportunities to move the ball. Instead, the Eagles repeatedly put their players in positions where they had almost no chance. I didn’t think Tanner McKee played well, but I am tired of trying to evaluate quarterbacks, running backs, and offensive linemen within an operation this dysfunctional. It isn’t fair on the players. Offense The very first play tells you almost everything you need to know. The Eagles line up under center, run play action, and leave a defender unblocked. The Panthers have four potential blitzers to their left, and the protection ends up asking Dameon Pierce to account for two defenders. I assume Willie Lampkin is supposed to pull across and pick up the linebacker, but he looks confused and helps where he isn’t needed. Without knowing the protection call, I can’t tell you exactly where the communication breaks down. I can tell you that the result is hopeless. This is the opening play. The staff has had all week to prepare it, and the protection still looks like this. We aren’t talking about a defense unveiling something in the fourth quarter that the offense has never seen before. The Eagles start the game unable to sort out who is blocking whom. After weeks of the same issues, that is unacceptable. The opening possessions felt insulting to the fans who turned up to watch this team. Eagles Offense' All22 vs. Panthers. Get ready; it's bad. 1) The Eagles' pass protection plan (NOT individuals – but the scheme) was abysmal again in this game. This is the very first play of the game. Under-center play action, of course, and the Eagles leave a Panthers defender… pic.twitter.com/p6g9sjnefb — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 19, 2026 On the next drive, Elijah Moore runs straight past Akayleb Evans (29) at the top of the screen. I highlighted Evans as someone to attack in the preview, and the opportunity is right there. McKee doesn’t have a chance to take advantage because the protection collapses again. The Panthers show a five-man front, but the Eagles appear to want their offensive linemen to block across a gap while leaving the edge defender to two tight ends. That requires Jake Majors to get across to No. 95, which leaves No. 92 for Tyler Steen. Steen can’t get over in time. Why are we making this so difficult? I understand that protections involve more than simply pointing five linemen at five defenders, but the Eagles keep creating problems for themselves with these assignments. They have seven players in protection against five rushers and still can’t give the quarterback a chance to throw to an open receiver. Majors is struggling at center, but he is hanging in there, and I thought the individual offensive line play was better than the overall protection would suggest. The staff deserves serious scrutiny for the plan it is asking these players to execute. 2) Next drive, another missed opportunity. Look at the top of the screen: Elijah Moore roasts 29 (who isn't good, and I called this out in the preview), but McKee doesn't have a chance because of protection. Again. It's a 5-man front, but the Eagles seem to want their lineman… pic.twitter.com/2j2YPeuCx7 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 19, 2026 The problems extend beyond blocking. The Eagles keep running this under-center play-action concept, often called “throttle,” a staple of the Shanahan offense in which the receiver can settle rather than continue across the field. It can work as a changeup to crossing routes. But the Eagles barely have a functioning crossing-route game, so what exactly are they changing up? The Panthers’ linebackers don’t bite on the fake and get good depth. There is no short route in the middle to draw them forward, leaving very little space behind them for the throw. The defense isn’t being stretched horizontally or vertically. The Eagles are borrowing a concept without creating the conditions that make it effective. It looks like running the Shanahan offense on beginner mode without understanding why the actual offense works. Their under-center passing game was utterly hopeless here: three incompletions and two sacks on five under-center play-action snaps. That isn’t helping a backup quarterback settle into a game. 3) The Eagles have run this under center play action Shanahan style 'Throttle' play a lot this year, and I can barely remember it working. It's often used as a mix-up to the standard crossing route, but the Eagles barely have any success with crossing routes, so why would the… pic.twitter.com/c11AWxkNRW — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 19, 2026 I mean, seriously, come on, guys. This is laughable. This chart looks made up! Under Center Dropback Success Rate 1) 59.5%, NYJ 2) 59.1%, SEA 3) 57.7%, SF . . NFL avg : 49.5% . . 30) 35.0%, MIA 31) 30.3%, DEN 32) 15.2%, PHI 😨 #Eagles pic.twitter.com/DZXoQPL5Il — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 19, 2026 Believe it or not, the Eagles did have two successful under-center runs in a row. Both were outside zone to the right from 12 personnel, and Dallas Goedert did a good job blocking on that side. Derrick Brown wasn’t on the field for the first one. On the second, the Eagles ran away from him, and the Panthers’ slant took their defensive linemen away from the opening. There were huge gaps to exploit, which matched what I thought about the weaknesses in this run defense before the game. These were good outcomes, and they gave the offense something to build on. After showing the same run successfully twice, the staff had an opportunity to make the defense pay for anticipating it. Change the direction. Run play action. Give the defense something else to consider. What do you think happened next? 4) The Eagles had 2 (!) successful under-center runs to the right-hand side in a row in this game. Both worked well because the Panthers slanted their lineman to the right and left a huge gap for the Eagles to exploit. Both were from 12 personnel, and both times they ran behind… pic.twitter.com/ConMvQn8wn — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 19, 2026 They ran it again. Same personnel, same direction, essentially the same look. This time, the Panthers saw it coming and blew up the run in the…

title: Jalen Hurts update: Eagles quarterback out for the season
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. Multiple NFL insiders reported as much on Monday morning. Pretty crazy stuff. Wild that Hurts was even able to play in the Eagles’ Week 5 game. Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles also issued a joint […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up during the first quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. Multiple NFL insiders reported as much on Monday morning. #Eagles QB Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season after several blood clots were revealed in his lungs, has been undergoing tests for days. Before the London game, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 am and did not sleep because sleep was a risk. He played without having slept. pic.twitter.com/avMUeBBOua — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 19, 2026 Pretty crazy stuff. Wild that Hurts was even able to play in the Eagles’ Week 5 game. Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles also issued a joint statement with an update on Hurts’ status: Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (ie. “blood thinners”). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football. Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery. Wow, that’s scary. But it’s good to hear optimism about his outlook. We are all rooting for him to get well soon. It feels weird to pivot to the football ramifications of this news but it’s the reality the Eagles find themselves in as well. Tanner McKee is now the quarterback for the rest of the season. That is, unless they Eagles decide to eventually bench him for Cole Payton, Joe Milton III, or someone not currently on the roster. (We know it won’t be Andy Dalton, because he reportedly declined to re-sign with the Eagles and joined the Atlanta Falcons instead.) The Eagles are 2-4 after losing four straight games and it’s currently hard to see things getting much better for them. We’ll have more on this developing story. Check back often for updates.

title: Eagles News: “This offense is such a trainwreck”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Before we go blaming the offensive struggles on injuries alone, do recall that it wasn’t very good when they were healthier. And are this year’s injuries a good excuse for the offense looking bad last year as well? How about the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Before we go blaming the offensive struggles on injuries alone, do recall that it wasn’t very good when they were healthier. And are this year’s injuries a good excuse for the offense looking bad last year as well? How about the offense looking confused from the first snap in the Eagles’ loss to the Carolina Panthers? Coaching is clearly part of the problem. This is the worst an Eagles offense has performed through Week 6 this century. Among 27 teams since 2000, the 2026 Eagles rank last in both EPA per drive and success rate. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) October 18, 2026 Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations as Eagles extend losing skid to four with loss to Panthers – NBCSP This offense is such a trainwreck, and their issues go way behind missing Jalen Hurts. They scored two touchdowns Sunday against the Panthers and it seemed like a hell of a day. They’re averaging 14.6 points during the four-game losing streak. They’re averaging 219 yards per game during the losing streak. These numbers are just unfathomable. They haven’t had 300 yards in a game since Week 2. We could go on with first downs, passing yards, 3rd-down percentage, but you get the idea. They’re all just abysmal. Is it all Sean Mannion’s fault? Nah. But he certainly hasn’t distinguished himself in his first six games as Eagles offensive coordinator and play caller. Maybe things will get better when they get Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall back and maybe Saquon will be back next week, although who really knows. This is all just such a mess right now. They got off to a decent start the first two weeks and has just spiraled downhill ever since. There’s so much to fix and I don’t even know how you go about starting. It just may be unfixable. Let’s talk about which NFL coaches should be fired soon – SB Nation Nick Sirianni — Philadelphia Eagles. There’s no sugarcoating what’s happened in Philly. This team is a mess. Injuries have wracked the team, seemingly finding a way to keep getting worse by the day. More and more players are hitting the injury report, entering IR, or just missing key snaps. Against the Panthers on Sunday the team did its best, but it was clear they just didn’t have enough players to really make an impact. At the center of everything is Nick Sirianni, who looks miserable trying to coach this season. Things weren’t great before the injuries, and now he’s forced to watch Tanner McKee, and a chorus of mediocre running backs try to form some semblance of an offense. The team is still decent defensively, but they’re banged up on that side too. It’s reached the point where it’s difficult to envision the Eagles winning many more games this year. That’s where the rub comes in, and what makes this so tricky. Sirianni does not to be fired based on the injuries and adversity he’s faced, especially when we look at his past history of success. The main issue is that if the Eagles end up with a very high draft pick, potentially in a spot to upgrade at quarterback — at what point is it worth trying to turn over a new leaf in the process? We have a scenario that feels somewhat similar to Doug Pederson. We had a Super Bowl-winning head coach who failed to follow up on the success, and owner Jeffrey Lurie believed that the long-term success of the franchise was more important than preserving the status quo, even if he thought Pederson was a decent coach. The team decided to part ways with their coach, Carson Wentz, draft a new QB, and install Nick Sirianni — ending a five-year tenure for all of them. Jalen Hurts update: Eagles quarterback out for the season – BGN It feels weird to pivot to the football ramifications of this news but it’s the reality the Eagles find themselves in as well. Tanner McKee is now the quarterback for the rest of the season. That is, unless they Eagles decide to eventually bench him for Cole Payton, Joe Milton III, or someone not currently on the roster. (We know it won’t be Andy Dalton, because he reportedly declined to re-sign with the Eagles and joined the Atlanta Falcons instead.) Different QB, same problems: Is Sean Mannion’s system holding back the Eagles? – The Athletic It would be a rationalization to blame injuries and exits. It happened too often with Hurts. It looked worse with McKee. And the constant is Mannion’s offense. “We have to do different things to get them going and score more points, plain and simple,” head coach Nick Sirianni said. “Everything’s on the table. To do the same thing over and over again and not get the results, that’d be foolish. Everything’s on the table of what we need to do to be able to put points on the board.” “Everything” being on the table is wide-ranging and ambiguous. It doesn’t endorse the status quo. When Sirianni was asked specifically about Mannion’s responsibility for the offense’s problems, he said no coach or player is on an island. Yet when Sirianni dismissed an offensive coordinator who had been with him for five playoff-bound years, none of which included a four-game losing streak like the Eagles’ current quagmire, he said the plan was a dramatic offensive shift that could provide a better schematic advantage. There’s been no advantage. The scheme inspires little consistent confidence beyond occasional spurts, even though team captain Jordan Mailata said he’s still confident in it. Eagles’ persistent offensive struggles mean ‘everything’s on the table’ — and that could include Sean Mannion’s role – Inquirer Sirianni certainly bears culpability for the losing streak. The seeds of his core beliefs, however, don’t provide shade for areas in which his previous ingenuity is now lacking. And that goes to the very root of the Sirianni conundrum. If he can’t devise an offense and/or call plays, and thus has to rely on Mannion-types for innovation, what is his greater value? To save himself, he may need to take back full ownership. It’s been that ugly on offense. Mannion and new offensive line coach Chris Kuper have had almost no solutions for defenses that blitz Eagles quarterbacks when they’re under center and drop to throw. Maybe because they almost always try to run play action in those situations. Brandon Graham Thought Kellen Moore Could Replace Nick Sirianni After the Super Bowl Win – Crossing Broad Is it me, or does BG basically admit that the Eagles planned on replacing Nick with Kellen Moore in 2024? That’s how it feels, doesn’t it? Where else would BG get this idea? I feel like the Kellen-Nick switch must’ve been talked about a bunch inside the organization for him to have this theory. Or maybe not. (Kinkead: BG was probably listening to too much WIP) Maybe BG cooked this up on his own. That’s possible. Maybe he — and the rest of the players — saw that Nick didn’t contribute to play-calling at all, and figured that since Kellen Moore was so good at it, he’d be an easy replacement for Nick if things went sideways. Whatever the case may be, it seems like the Eagles winning the Super Bowl in 2024 derailed that plan. Firing Nick after a Super Bowl win would’ve been nearly impossible (but it would’ve been baller as hell… bold move… scared money don’t make money, etc…), and Kellen was bound to move on to a head coaching job after his stellar season calling plays. But still, it’s a fascinating sliding doors moment. Another Bad Day – Iggles Blitz Some fans are now screaming for Nick Sirianni’s head. That’s not going to happen this season, nor should it. Firing him would not make this team better. It would just give angry fans something to be happy about. His future will be…

full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn’t easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It’s the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy defends play-calling after Jamel Dean interception
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers mounted their biggest fourth-quarter comeback in over 30 years on Sunday by overcoming a 16-3 deficit to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. One of the biggest plays of the game came when former Buccaneer Jamel Dean picked off Jalon Daniels and returned the interception inside the five yard-line. Unfortunately for Pittsburgh, they […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers mounted their biggest fourth-quarter comeback in over 30 years on Sunday by overcoming a 16-3 deficit to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. One of the biggest plays of the game came when former Buccaneer Jamel Dean picked off Jalon Daniels and returned the interception inside the five yard-line. Unfortunately for Pittsburgh, they were unable to punch the ball in the end zone. The first play on the ensuing drive was a play action pass intended for Darnell Washington that was broken up. The second play was a run by Jaylen Warren that put the ball to the one yard-line. Then on 3rd-and-goal, Aaron Rodgers threw a jump ball to DK Metcalf that was broken up, which lead to the Steelers kicking a field goal. Many were critical of the play-calling from Mike McCarthy, but the Steelers’ head coach defended his choice of plays on Monday. “I get the post evaluation, but those are solid plays,” McCarthy said. The Steelers were able to overcome not getting into the end zone late in the fourth quarter. Despite the Bucs getting into field goal range and sending the game into overtime, the Steelers drove 12 plays and Rodgers connected with Germie Bernard for the game-winning score. title: Jalen Ramsey is the glue to the Steelers’ defense
summary: Last week, Dave Dameshek asked me who was the one piece on defense the Steelers couldn’t afford to lose. I said that we may find out it was Joey Porter, as the Browns were able to have their way with the Steelers’ secondary and the cornerback room was wearing very thin. It turns out the […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, Dave Dameshek asked me who was the one piece on defense the Steelers couldn’t afford to lose. I said that we may find out it was Joey Porter, as the Browns were able to have their way with the Steelers’ secondary and the cornerback room was wearing very thin. It turns out the glue to the defense wasn’t Porter, though – it’s Jalen Ramsey. The future Hall of Fame defensive back had one of the best games of his career on Sunday, totaling 10 tackles, four tackles for loss, and two sacks, including the game-sealing sack on 4th-and-8 in overtime to clinch a 26-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Lest we forget that Ramsey is doing all of this with a broken wrist that he suffered in Week 1. Yet despite that injury, he hasn’t missed a game, and his versatility has been exactly what the Steelers had hoped it would be when Patrick Graham said he would play the STAR role. Per Sumer Sports, Ramsey has eight run stops – that is tied for the league lead among all cornerbacks with Cooper DeJean of the Philadelphia Eagles. His two sacks are tied for second among corners, as Kyler Gordon made his return to the Chicago Bears’ lineup in Week 6 and had three in one game. His reliability in this role, combined with his tackling ability (only two missed tackles on the season) has made him irreplaceable. Players like Ramsey evolve as they get to the final holes of their career, and he has done just that. While he may no longer be the outside bump-and-run man-to-man lockdown cornerback he was in the late 2010s, his pure talent as a football player has seen him grow into being dominant as this Joker in the deck for the Steelers’ defense. Some guys lead with words, Ramsey leads by example – playing hurt, not making excuses, and showing that he is still more than capable of directly impacting the outcome of games. It’s the morning after game day, and the Steelers are tied for the lead in the AFC North. Jamel Dean’s record day The Steelers signed Jamel Dean away from Tampa in the offseason with the hopes of forming a tremendous one-two punch at corner with he and Joey Porter. Obviously, Porter is now gone and Dean has become the top dog at the position, and he answered the bell against his former team with a tremendous performance. Dean broke up six passes, which is a single-game record for the Steelers. Additionally, he allowed just three receptions on 11 targets, which is the second-lowest number of catches allowed when targeted 10 times this season. Who is first? His teammate, Asante Samuel Jr, who allowed two catches on 10 targets last week against the Indianapolis Colts. And not to pat myself on the back, but when I made the Steelers’ mock schedule and predictions in the offseason, I said Jamel Dean would have a game-sealing interception. Dean has been tremendous, and is a big reason why the Steelers currently rank top 10 in EPA against the pass and success rate. Special teams struggles The coach the Steelers miss the most was standing on the other sideline on Sunday. Danny Smith’s special teams unit was always a reliable one for the Steelers – the same cannot be said about this current group. Kaden Wetjen had a terrific 59-yard kickoff return negated by a Cole Holcomb penalty, which took the Steelers from starting at Tampa Bay’s 41 to starting at their own 20. There was another special team penalty on a punt, this one on Doneiko Slaughter. The Steelers were set to start at the Bucs’ 44 yard-line but instead had to start at their own 46. Throw in yet another Chris Boswell missed field goal, and you have a unit that has done a 180 over the course of just six games. Quick hitters Nick Herbig was awesome, recording his first two sacks of the season. Need to see more of that going forward. We talked about it across our other post-game pieces, but what a performance from both DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard. Both stepped up in massive ways, combining for 22 receptions. If the Steelers are going to be aggressive before the trade deadline, safety and linebacker are far bigger needs than receiver. Dare I say call the Chargers about Derwin James. Congrats to Yahya Black for his first career sack and Daylen Everette for his first career interception. Big plays from young building blocks. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers news: What to make of the Steelers’ win over the Bucs
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and kept pace with the Cleveland Browns in the AFC North. Technically, Pittsburgh sits in second place, but a win is a win. full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and kept pace with the Cleveland Browns in the AFC North. Technically, Pittsburgh sits in second place, but a win is a win. In the NFL, they don’t ask how; they ask how many, and the Steelers are 4-2. However, the Steelers started slowly out of the gate, and the offense, in particular, needs to get off to a better start. Todd Bowles’ defense was relentless early on, and the Steelers had no answers. Luckily, the offense got on track down the stretch and in overtime as Pittsburgh came away with the win. Defensively, allowing Jalon Daniels and the Bucs offense to operate as freely as they did early in the game is unacceptable. Jalen Ramsey had himself a big game, but this defense was off balance for much of the game, but put it together to help the offense close out the Bucs. Simply put, this team can’t afford to start games slowly on offense and defense and expect to win. Still, that’s four wins, and Pittsburgh is in the thick of the AFC North race. title: Mike Macdonald: Zach Charbonnet could make Seahawks return ‘in some capacity’ vs. Chiefs
summary: The Seattle Seahawks need any sort of running back help they can get, as they fittingly face the Kansas City Chiefs and former Seahawks star, Super Bowl 60 MVP, and current NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III on Sunday night. While Jadarian Price is not an option until Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, Zach […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks need any sort of running back help they can get, as they fittingly face the Kansas City Chiefs and former Seahawks star, Super Bowl 60 MVP, and current NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III on Sunday night. While Jadarian Price is not an option until Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, Zach Charbonnet seems on course to make his season debut this weekend. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday that Charbonnet could play, pending how this week’s practice goes. “Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting,” Macdonald said. “There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity.” Charbonnet has to be activated off injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster this week, otherwise he reverts to IR for the rest of the season. Even when he’s activated, that doesn’t necessarily mean he’ll play Week 7, but Macdonald’s quotes sound encouraging. In the meantime, he’s practiced in a limited capacity throughout his 21-day window, but it sounds like “full week’s worth of reps” could mean a full participant designation in the Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices. The fourth-year man out of UCLA was Seattle’s leader in total touchdowns last season with 12, to go along with his career-best 730 yards on the ground. With Emanuel Wilson and George Holani having ball security and efficiency struggles, Charbonnet’s impending return from a January ACL tear is about as welcome and desperately need outcome as the Super Bowl champions can get. “I know he’s had a certain date in mind, which is a really ambitious date,” Macdonald said. “For those who have tried to come back from significant knee surgery understand the undertaking that takes. Zach’s a beast. He looks great. It’s not easy to say, ‘Alright, let’s go.’ For him to have that courage to say that and work through the things that he’s worked through, you can’t do anything but tip your cap to him.” Charbonnet’s practice status on Wednesday should give us a solid indicator as far as whether or not he’ll be able to help out an otherwise struggling Seahawks offense on Sunday.

title: Why the Seattle Seahawks don’t need to bench Sam Darnold
summary: We’ve all sat with this one for a bit. Is Sam Darnold not the answer? Did he get rushed back from injury? Would the Seahawks be better off with Andrew Lock as the trigger man? One thing is clear: Seven interceptions in four games is… not good. Pulling the struggling quarterback can feel like the […]
full_text: We’ve all sat with this one for a bit. Is Sam Darnold not the answer? Did he get rushed back from injury? Would the Seahawks be better off with Andrew Lock as the trigger man? One thing is clear: Seven interceptions in four games is… not good. Pulling the struggling quarterback can feel like the quickest and easiest lever to pull. The Seattle Seahawks, of course, will have a long wait until they can wash the sour taste of recent putrid performances on offense out of their collective mouths. The run of losses to the San Francisco 49ers and the Denver Broncos in the last two games featured plenty of frustrating mistakes to pave the road to an unspectacular 3-3 record. How do the 2026 Seahawks continue to run it forward? Brock Purdy hadn’t been sacked before facing the ‘Hawks, then got taken down three times by the “Dark Side.” That stop unit held SF to 4/12 on 3rd downs and tainted his pristine trajectory to hand him his 2nd INT of the season (first since the opening week). Bo Nix was held under 110 passing yards. It’s the offense that failed in their mission to be complimentary. Does Seattle need to bench their championship quarterback? Let’s start by not turning the ball over. The Seahawks offense has lost more EPA on turnovers than any other team in the NFL. 12 turnovers through six weeks is the most for any Seahawks offense in the last 25 years. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) October 16, 2026 I want to preface all of this and say that backup halfback, George Holani was questionable to play in Santa Clara. With that in mind, he deserves some appropriate credit, as a warrior for this team. He also deserves credit for being a strong pass protector… at times. Having said that, the man put the ball on the ground twice against the Niners, contributing to a sloppy performance by the Hawks. If you did not know, NFL coaches are serious about fumbles . That hyperlink is the Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady talking about reducing the load of player who led the league in rushing TD’s in 2024 and rushing yards in 2025. The thing is, Holani averages over seven touches per game. Before TNF, Shaheed was averaging a little over two touches per. I know you don’t want to have tells when a specific back is in the game… but perhaps time for less? That’s what I thought before the Broncos game. Rashid Shaheed got $34M guaranteed on his contract extension this past offseason. I wanted to see the Hawks use short passes as an extension of the run game, if need be, just to get his involvement in line with his contract priority. Then that man fumbled twice. Who’s next to get added to the mix? Here are Tory Horton’s last 8 catches: first down, touchdown, 6 yards, touchdown, first down, first down, first down, touchdown. He was not targeted in Week 6 against the Niners. Tory, come on down!! View this post on Instagram Interceptions are a little more convoluted of a blame game than fumbles. Cooper Kupp addressed the throw to Horton : “certainly within the grounds of what that play was. Got to make a play.” The same Cooper who is no longer a dynamic threat on the field. Is it possible that the 2026 Seattle Seahawks are simply in need of another high-level playmaker to join JSN in the priority list for defenses to worry about? Kenneth Walker III was that last season, but I’m not sure he’s the only. Is the pantry now raided? Does Seattle need to draft a wideout in the first round in the upcoming offseason? Let’s hit pause on that for now. Is it the offensive line? I mean, Abe Lucas’ performance was groan-worthy at times. When discussing the five sacks that Darnold took and how it reflects on the offensive line, Mike Macdonald explained, saying , “I mean, you can say it’s on the offensive line–it’s on our offense. You know, it’s both. It’s how efficient we can run the ball; how efficient we can move the ball other ways. The quarterback is getting hit way too much, so everybody sees that.” There are multiple angles here. Role players may be touching the ball a little more than originally planned, but also there is the question of scheme. As Field Gulls’ own Mookie Alexander mentions , “At the moment, the Seahawks do not have the type of offense that can control a game through the run. They are a much better passing team on early downs yet adopt a run-first mentality.” Mike Macdoanld on why the ball is being put in jeopardy so often : “In short, it’s really a function of ‘who’s applying pressure to who?’ So, if we’re playing the way we want to play, we should be applying pressure to defenses. Then, all of a sudden –it’s funny how that works–ball isn’t as in jeopardy as much.” It’s unfortunate that the running back that the ‘Hawks took in Round 1 of the NFL draft joins another early round back on the injury ledger, in Zach Charbonnet. Those two, along with up-and-comers like Jacardia Wright and (the no longer on the roster) Kenny McIntosh all being unavailable is sad. Does that mean that we should hit the panic button? Darnold does need to get into flow state. And yes: Sam should be expected to be able to get it done… even in the absence of a run game. Even if conditions are not perfect, we should expect him to be able to figure it out. He’s a Super Bowl-winning signal caller, but if he keeps throwing two INT’s per game, Seattle brass may have to pull him at some point . That point is not now. Coach Mike addressed the controversy around Sam Darnold, saying that, “I know we’re harping on the turnovers… but he’s been able to escape some really nasty pressure situations and find ways to move the ball down the field, that not a lot of people can do. That’s definitely in his skillset and we encourage him to continue to do that, within your progressions and things like that.” Seattle prides itself on cultivating environments for passers to succeed in. That environment seems crippled at the moment. View this post on Instagram Macdonald plainly stated that, “we got to be able to execute our run game and hold on to the football… straight up.” All of the coaches on staff will be tasked with exploring ways to improve this slumping offense. Those of you who think Brian Fleury and, to some extent, Sam Darnold are under some level of pressure are kidding yourselves. There is a standard. It will be interesting to see what Fleury chooses to change, if anything, headed into a possible humiliation ritual against Ken Walker. Now, acknowledging that things need to change, we can also understand that making a QB change is a very big deal. It’s one that has ripple effects on the direction of the franchise for years to come. "To bench a quarterback is a huge sea change kind of shift that will affect not just this season, but the entire future of the organization." 👀 @TheMikeSalk on the #Seahawks sticking with QB Sam Darnold amid turnover struggles. pic.twitter.com/sVJYoW6oZ8 — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) October 17, 2026 We can blame the run game, we can blame injuries, we can blame Shaheed, we can blame Tory Horton, we can blame the offensive line, and yes… we can blame Sam Darnold. Hell, you can blame Hard Knocks if you want to. This is not the end of the season as we know it. The Seahawks have totaled 10 turnovers in their 3 losses… and still only lost those by a collective sum of 8 points overall. Maybe the sky isn’t truly falling quite yet. Let’s just wait and see what things look like when Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet and Anthony Bradford make their returns to the lineup. Yes, THAT Anthony Bradford. View Link

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks almost had an ideal weekend of results to make up for their own disappointing Thursday night result against the Denver Broncos. It was a disastrous home loss for the Los Angeles Rams to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but the Rams are 2-4 and dealing with enough injuries to put their heavily hyped Super Bowl dreams in the toilet . What would’ve been great for the Seahawks is the Washington Commanders upsetting the San Francisco 49ers in Santa Clara, home of the Seahawks’ most recent Super Bowl win. Well, the Commanders looked like they were toast at 23-3 down and with Terry McLaurin carted off with a serious knee injury, but Mike Evans’ own injury seemingly stymied the 49ers offense in the second half, and Washington pulled within 23-17 in the fourth quarter. A would-be go-ahead touchdown by Jeremy McNichols was wiped out by a face mask penalty on Commanders guard Chris Paul, who had a fist full of face mask and was rightfully penalized. That the 49ers were allowed unlimited helmet-to-helmet shots without any penalties? Different story. Here's a look at the shot that Diggs took straight to the helmet on this pass. He also had to have his hand looked at. No flags thrown on this play pic.twitter.com/NPkLQo8zwC — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) October 20, 2026 Anyway, Malik Mustapha (who’s not going to be popular around these parts any time soon) made a clutch 4th down stop on Treylon Burks to deny the Commanders on a must-have 4th down after the two-minute warning. Washington got the ball back and was gifted 15 yards on a personal foul penalty for hitting Luke McCaffrey on a fair caught punt. Jayden Daniels got the Commanders within striking distance of an all-time comeback, but he took an intentional grounding penalty that also required a 10-second runoff. Another confusing route tree by David Blough at the end of the game. This play never had a chance. All #Commanders receivers running downfield and not working the middle of the field. There would have been plenty of time to clock it after. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/gJPTqtLNx0 — Carolina Commander (@SC_Commanderr) October 20, 2026 The Hail Mary attempt… well there was no attempt, because the Commanders o-line vomited all over the grass. Jayden Daniels gets sacked as time expires. 49ers win 23-17 pic.twitter.com/7NMR0apwfI — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) October 20, 2026 Ah well. title: NFC West update: LA Rams in injury crisis mode with several long-term absences
summary: Entering the regular season, the Los Angeles Rams were widely considered to be a Super Bowl contender but through six weeks, they sit last in the NFC West and now they’ll be without three key players for an extensive period of time—one for the remainder of the year. Head coach Sean McVay announced wide receiver […]
full_text: Entering the regular season, the Los Angeles Rams were widely considered to be a Super Bowl contender but through six weeks, they sit last in the NFC West and now they’ll be without three key players for an extensive period of time—one for the remainder of the year. Head coach Sean McVay announced wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring in Sunday’s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals and is expected to miss 6-10 weeks, with the hope of returning shortly after they team’s bye (Week 11). In addition, the Rams placed defensive tackles Kobie Turner (groin) and former Seahawk Poona Ford (ruptured triceps) on injured reserve. Turner is expected to miss 4-6 weeks, while Ford will not return this season. As for special teams, recently signed kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL in his team debut on Sunday and is set to miss the remainder of the season, leaving Los Angeles in search of their third kicker of the season following the release of Harrison Mevis. It’s a crucial blow for the Rams, who are still without reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett (knee) and given they sit at 2-4 with two losses having come against divisional opponents, it’ll be an uphill battle if they want to re-emerge as a legitimate threat in the NFC. As one of the league’s most dangerous red zone threats, Adams’ absence is especially troubling, especially when taking into consideration his replacements (Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Xavier Smith) have combined for just eight career touchdowns, compared to the the star wideout’s 18 across the last two seasons. Although Adams’ injury timeline is quite lenient, there remains the possibility he could still be sidelined for the team’s Week 16 matchup against the Seahawks. On the defensive side, the absence of Turner and Ford will likely impact the Rams ability to stop the run, an area where they’ve already struggled so far this season. Former fifth-round picks Ty Hamilton and Larrell Murchison appear poised to see increased playing time, although neither have ever slotted in as solidified starters. With a cloud of uncertainty looming over their future, both the wild card and divisional standings are likely to impacted. The Rams currently sit three games behind the San Francisco 49ers for first in the NFC West and 1.5 behind the Detroit Lions for the final wild card spot. It bodes well for Seattle, who—like Los Angeles have dropped back-to-back games and have looked like a shell of themselves as of late. However, it certainly helps one of the most dangerous forces in the NFC has as well. Despite the injury news, the Rams are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and the Cardinals over their next four games—a favourable upcoming stretch of games by all means. Given the star power on their roster, it’s difficult to count Los Angeles out of the playoff picture, even nearing the halfway mark of the season, but there’s certainly work to be done if they want to keep up in the NFC race.

title: Seahawks ‘likely’ placing Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve
summary: Seattle Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will not be on the field any time soon. The second-year player out of Miami suffered a shoulder injury while trying to recover Rashid Shaheed’s fumble in last Thursday’s loss to the Denver Broncos. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the injury is evidently severe enough to place him on […]
full_text: Seattle Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will not be on the field any time soon. The second-year player out of Miami suffered a shoulder injury while trying to recover Rashid Shaheed’s fumble in last Thursday’s loss to the Denver Broncos. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , the injury is evidently severe enough to place him on injured reserve, which means missing at least four games. Seattle’s bye week is after the fourth game of that IR stint, so the earliest Arroyo could return is Week 12 at the San Francisco 49ers on Thanksgiving weekend. Arroyo had just two targets and one catch for 17 yards this season, all while generally splitting snaps with fellow backup tight end, Eric Saubert. It was notable that against the Broncos, the Seahawks not only made Nick Kallerup a game day active for the first time since Week 3, but Kallerup had already out-snapped Arroyo before the injury occurred. The Seahawks selected Arroyo in the second round at No. 50 overall. Arroyo was lauded for his receiving skills, albeit with essentially one season of productivity. One of the cautions with Arroyo (outside of his blocking) was his health. In 2022, Arroyo tore his ACL severely enough that he only played four games in 2023. After missing no games in 2024, Arroyo hurt his knee at Senior Bowl and didn’t participate at the NFL Scouting Combine. So far, injuries have impacted Arroyo in his NFL career. Toward the end of last regular season, Arroyo went to injured reserve after hurting his knee against the Atlanta Falcons, although he was activated in time for the NFC Championship Game. At least this injury isn’t another knee, but it’s nevertheless an unfortunate health setback for Arroyo. The Seahawks practice on Monday, so we should get confirmation sooner rather than later that Arroyo will be out in the long term. Seattle signing Josiah Deguara to the practice squad figures to be insurance while Arroyo is sidelined.

While Arroyo’s status for Sunday is not yet clear, Deguara’s signing at least suggests it’s up in the air — if not trending downward. Deguara, 29, was a third-round pick of the Green Bay Packers in 2020, and played four seasons with them catching 47 passes for 436 yards and two touchdowns. He spent 2024 with the Jaguars and 2025 with the Cardinals, catching three balls in both stops. He was released by Philadelphia last week, after going back and forth between the team’s 53-man roster and practice squad. Should Arroyo miss time with the shoulder injury suffered against the Broncos, Deguara could be elevated for Sunday Night Football against the Chiefs and make his Seahawks debut.

title: 3 things we learned about the 49ers in Week 6: Romello Height has arrived
summary: Boy, the San Francisco 49ers know how to make things interesting. A game that felt pretty much over at halftime turned into a thriller as the 49ers held off Jayden Daniels and the Commanders’ comeback attempt. In a game where Terry McLaurin was seriously injured, the Commanders’ passing attack came alive in the second half. […]
full_text: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Boy, the San Francisco 49ers know how to make things interesting. A game that felt pretty much over at halftime turned into a thriller as the 49ers held off Jayden Daniels and the Commanders’ comeback attempt. In a game where Terry McLaurin was seriously injured, the Commanders’ passing attack came alive in the second half. The 49ers lost Mike Evans before the half, but according to Kyle Shanahan, his Achilles is intact, and the injury is the same one he dealt with during the week. The 49ers are 6-0 with a chance to go 7-0 next week before their bye, which will be the turning point for the health of the roster as the team expects to have Nick Bosa, Demarcus Robinson, Christian Kirk, and other important players coming out of the bye. The team could get reinforcements back for Atlanta, but coming off the bye, it will be as close to healthy as possible. Here’s what we learned from Monday night’s win over the Commanders. The 49ers crowded safety room Before his injury, Marques Sigle was a revelation. Malik Mustapha was returning from injury, but during his time replacing Sigle, he has been fantastic and made the two biggest plays of the night in succession. A complete run stuff on third down from the safety position for no gain, followed by a hard-fought PBU on a target to the taller Treylon Burks, ended the Commanders’ drive. Washington would get the ball back one more time before the defensive line shut the door on the comeback attempt, but the question is: when Sigle returns, can you justify sending Mustapha to the bench? The thing is, Ji’Ayir Brown hasn’t played poorly in 2026. Mustapha has been a tone-setter with his physicality and is flashing every week. It’s a good problem to have, and perhaps it allows some more flexibility for Raheem Morris with all three safeties, but Mustapha has played like a man possessed. Mike Evans is the engine of the 49ers offense Brock Purdy has played his best football ever in 2026. It’s no coincidence that it comes in a season when Mike Evans was added to the fold. The first half was a laser show, with Evans nearly topping 100 yards before the half. The problem is that when Evans departed, the 49ers leaned on Christian McCaffrey, but the Commanders knew the 49ers were out of separators and blitzed constantly in the second half, knowing they wouldn’t be beat downfield. Herein lies the problem. The 49ers need to target another receiver by the trade deadline, one who can separate independently from Kyle Shanahan and his scheme. If that means knocking down Robinson in the pecking order when he returns, then so be it. The 49ers shouldn’t shy away from adding impact players because they have players returning. If adding a separator pushes Jordan Watkins or Jacob Cowing off the roster, you have to do it. The second half was a glimpse of the 49ers being down to their seventh and eighth receivers. Add more firepower. Do not get complacent and bank on returning players. Hello, Romello Height What a game for Height. Six total pressures, two sacks (one wiped away by a penalty), two QB hits, and two hurries. The rookie was a star on Monday night. The entire defensive line deserves credit, but Height’s breakout game in tandem with a returning Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams’ continued progress is such a plus for this 49ers defense. The 49ers are closer than ever to a championship defense. A deeper look into Height’s game on Monday night is even more impressive. In true pass sets (no play action or screens), Height generated five pressures, recorded a sack with two QB hits and two hurries. On 19 true pass sets, Height finished with a 26.7% win rate. Impressive game. The 49ers’ defensive line is getting better each game.
author: Jason Aponte

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers continue to distance themselves; Rams and Seahawks lose
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers walks the field after winning the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, a team both the Rams and Seahawks lost to. Should tiebreakers come into play, those two victories could be a deciding factor. So that puts the 49ers at 6-0 and 3-0 in the division. With the losses, they now have a three-game lead (and change if you could tiebreakers) over the second-place Seahawks. Yes, the Commanders win wasn’t pretty, but the 49ers are 6-0, and if we have to endure a game like that Commanders game to be 6-0, I don’t think there’s a fan in the world who wouldn’t take that. It’s not without some wrinkles. Wide receiver Mike Evans may miss some time . While Christian Kirk has resumed practice, it might take some time to get in sync with Brock Purdy. At least the 49ers get Dre Greenlaw back next week and maybe Nick Bosa. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) The biggest thing about the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos isn’t that they lost a game they probably should have won; it’s that Bo Nix may be getting more criticism for his play than Sam Darnold. Ryan Fitzpatrick absolutely destroyed Bo Nix on live TV 💀 pic.twitter.com/HGu3T5fi4A — PredictArena (@PredictArena) October 16, 2026 And he should. Nix has had a tendency to come back in the second half in 2026, but he didn’t do any of that here. You can also add in some very bad decision-making. Nix went 17 for 27 and 107 yards passing. Yes, 107 yards passing and the Broncos won. It’s fair to note the Broncos also had 74 yards rushing. So how did the Broncos win? Defense, all defense. How did the Seahawks lose? Well, not being able to run the ball might be the biggest reason. 113 yards total. Rashid Shaheed losing one of his two fumbles doesn’t help. Then there’s the other quarterback. Sam Darnold had two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and five sacks. 17-14, Broncos. The Broncos are 4-2 after that stat line from Bo Nix. He didn’t throw a touchdown or an interception and got sacked twice compared to Darnold’s five. Do the Broncos look like a 4-2 team? That’s up to you. The Seahawks are now games (yes, plural) behind the 49ers, and it’s not going to get any easier. Arizona Cardinals (2-4)/Los Angeles Rams (2-4) Oh, you know what time it is. Let’s Ram It! Let’s Ram it all the way to last place in the NFC West. The Arizona Cardinals not only beat the Los Angeles Rams, but did so by field-goal-ing the Rams to death. Six field goals were all the Cardinals needed to get the 18-16 victory. This was a Los Angeles Rams team that some thought would go undefeated before the season began. Now they are last place in their own division. My, what a tangled web we weave. And the Rams had a chance to win this thing. They marched down the field, got the touchdown, and the Cardinals only had 45 seconds left with no timeouts. Turns out 45 seconds is too much time for Jacoby Brissett, because next thing you know he’s pushing the ball down the field and getting into field goal range in 10 of those 45 seconds. Many are saying the Rams get an easier schedule so they can right the ship, but again: They lost to a team via six field goals. The only other team the Cardinals have beaten is from Los Angeles, and that team, the Chargers, is 0-6 right now. And yes, the Rams lost their kicker early in the game and didn’t have a kicker to make field goals. Then again, should the Rams need a kicker for the Cardinals? That’s a huge win for the Cardinals and an equally miserable loss for the Rams. Are they out? No. But they are now in last place with several divisional losses on them as well. They are almost at “run the table to get in the playoffs” territory. Almost. And it gets worse. First, wide receiver Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks due to a hamstring injury. That’s devastating for the wide receiver group (something 49ers fans know all too well). Second, their shiny new kicker, Blake Grupe, was injured on Sunday, which was enough to add him to injured reserve. So the Rams need to overcome a four-game deficit without a kicker or their veteran wide receiver. Onto Week 7 The 49ers will travel to face the Atlanta Falcons, a game with the dreaded 10:00 AM start time. Not exactly ideal when the Falcons have been humming for a couple of games until Sunday—when the Chicago Bears crushed them. That score says 31-23, but 16 of the Falcons’ 23 points came in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, Chicago was scoring touchdowns until the fourth quarter. Regardless of Atlanta’s performance, they have the best running back in the game in Bijan Robinson. With Robinson, the Falcons can run the ball, and if you’ve watched them lately, he’s not exactly the easiest thing to stop. It’s a great test for the 49ers, who have limited explosive runs. The Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs as the Sunday Night Football game. It feels strange to want the Seahawks to win just to hand the Chiefs a loss, but the Chiefs could do the 49ers a favor by putting the Seahawks to 3-4. As much as some of us may dislike both teams, that will be a fun game to watch. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will probably be the star of the show; the Seahawks running game hasn’t been the same since he left in free agency, and the Chiefs have had a running game since acquiring him. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos. The same Denver Broncos who managed to beat the Seahawks. Given what we’ve seen of this Cardinals team, a win isn’t out of the ordinary. The Rams will have their second straight week of not playing on primetime. They might play a bit more on Sunday afternoon if the league flexes them out of anything in the future. They host the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders lost to the Buffalo Bills, but were in it until the end. The Rams could be their get-right game. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next at Atlanta Falcons 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday Night Football ) 3rd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Denver Broncos 4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Las Vegas Raiders
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 3 quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Commanders: The fast start paid off
summary: It wasn’t the prettiest game and, at times, was quite a scary one, but the San Francisco 49ers found a way to edge past the Washington Commanders on Monday night to improve to 6-0 on the season. Heading into the game with injury questions once again, the 49ers lost Mike Evans just before halftime. But […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers scrambles against the Washington Commanders during the first half of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t the prettiest game and, at times, was quite a scary one, but the San Francisco 49ers found a way to edge past the Washington Commanders on Monday night to improve to 6-0 on the season. Heading into the game with injury questions once again, the 49ers lost Mike Evans just before halftime. But their 17-point lead was too much to overcome, despite a furious comeback by Jayden Daniels and Co., allowing the 49ers to improve to 6-0 with the Atlanta Falcons up next before the bye week. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Commanders on Monday night. Fast start pays off One of my keys to the game for the 49ers was getting off to a fast start. Obviously, that’s important in any game, but it felt extra vital in this one. We’ve seen the 49ers operate well in the clutch over the past two weeks against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks, thanks to quality play from Brock Purdy, but I pointed to Evans’s injury status as a big reason why an early lead would be key. Getting off to a fast start could ease some of the pressure off a clearly-banged up Evans, while also allowing the 49ers to remain balanced and the Commanders to get even more one-dimensional. That all turned out to be true, as the 49ers offense couldn’t get going without Evans in the second half. One gripe from Kyle Shanahan in this game was also the 49ers’ lack of balance in the second half from a play-calling perspective over the final quarter. The 49ers went pass-pass-pass on two consecutive drives to start the fourth quarter, with both resulting in three-and-outs. The 1st started with a Brock Purdy sack, derailing the drive, while Purdy was sacked on second down on the second drive. Washington also excelled in the pass game, with Jayden Daniels going for 300 passing yards, despite their run game producing just 53 yards on 3.1 yards per carry. That’s all to say: it was extremely important the 49ers got off to a lead, as the hole proved too far for the Commanders to dig out of in the second half. Third and fourth down execution The 49ers didn’t win the time of possession battle, mainly because the Commanders had the ball for nearly 80 percent of the fourth quarter. But they did win the late-down battle, which was also a key of mine heading into the game. Coming in, the 49ers were the second-most efficient offense in the NFL, which meant they weren’t getting to third downs often, ranking 32nd in the NFL in third downs per game. But when they did get there, they still converted at a high rate, ranking first in the NFL coming into the game. Meanwhile, while the Commanders were a solid defense on early downs, they’ve really struggled on third downs, ranking 28th in the NFL in EPA allowed per play on third downs and 24th in the NFL in conversion rate. Through three quarters on Monday, the 49ers were 7 of 11 on third downs and 2 of 2 on fourth downs. So, in essence, they converted 9 of their 11 late-down opportunities, and that resulted in four scoring drives on six opportunities through three quarters, with the other two being Christian McCaffrey’s fumble and a punt. With the pass game options looking as they did, and the Commanders’ defense coming in as a solid run defense, it felt like this one could be a game with longer drives, and that proved to be the case for the 49ers. They had drives of 9, 8, 7, 14, and 11 plays through the first three quarters, but executed well on later downs to keep them going. Now, of course, the 49ers ended the game with three three-and-outs. But they also did a really good job defensively on later downs. The Commanders were just 3 of 12 on third downs and 1 of 3 on fourth downs, and it made a huge difference. To start the game, the 49ers forced a field goal on a successful Washington drive, got a sack on third down for a three-and-out, and forced a turnover on downs as the Commanders got to 4th & 2 on the 49ers 13-yard line. That’s three key late-down stops resulting in only three points. San Francisco also got a sack near midfield on third down on Washington’s opening drive of the second half. Then, after allowing two touchdown drives, the 49ers had multiple late-down stops. On Washington’s second-to-last drive, the 49ers forced an incompletion on third down and got a fourth-down sack, which was wiped out by an illegal contact. On the next set of downs, though, they got another third-down stop before Malik Mustapha’s big pass breakup forced a turnover on downs. Of course, on the final drive, the 49ers got a sack on Daniels on third down to end the game on the final play. Overall, the 49ers offense executed quite well on third and fourth downs through three quarters, setting themselves up in a good position, while the defense consistently came together with clutch plays on late downs to stop a very quality Commanders passing offense. Some step up, while others struggle to As in any close game, the 49ers don’t win this one without consistent play from some and clutch play from others. We have to continue to praise Brock Purdy for his performances. The 49ers quarterback kept the ball out of harm’s way and completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown. He continued to hit explosives to his pass-catcher group, despite the injuries, and had a couple of savvy third-down scrambles to extend drives. He’s seeing the field at a high level and isn’t making mistakes, while conducting a very efficient offense. Purdy averaged 9.1 yards per play, and it could’ve been more if some other plays were made in the second half. Mustapha deserves praise, not only for his huge fourth-quarter play, but for his overall start to the season. As I’ve said the last few weeks, he’s been vital for Raheem Morris’s defense as a glue piece in the secondary. On the defensive line, Romello Height continues to stack some really good games. He’s been a shoutout the last two weeks, and he played very well on Monday night, recording six pressures with his 0.5 sacks. Keion White, Mykel Williams, Gracen Halton, and Osa Odighizuwa all made key plays as well, as the 49ers pass rush got 21 pressures as a whole. I have to also point out the quality play of Jaden Dugger, who has really broken out the last two weeks in Dre Greenlaw’s absence. Dugger had a team-high 11 tackles, and his versatility, which was a big talking point in the offseason, is showing out. He had multiple pressures again on Monday. Then, even completely battered with injuries, Mike Evans had some big early plays that set up the 49ers scoring drives. That was key because the 49ers receivers were not targeted at all in the second half, with that group struggling to make plays. George Kittle had a strong first half as well, with five catches for 69 yards and a touchdown, but couldn’t come down with a key play on a third down in the second half that led to a quick punt. The 49ers offensive line also had another very solid game, creating some key holes in the run game against a defense that ranked top 10 against the run coming into the week. Brock Purdy was also pressured on just 7 of his 34 dropbacks, despite being blitzed nearly 45 percent of the time. One note to make: the 49ers benched Upton Stout again for a portion of the game, this time late in the fourth quarter. Raheem Morris initially had Ashtyn Davis in as a big nickel, then subbed him out as well after giving up a big play and committing a penalty. The 49ers then went with Deommodore Lenoir in the slot and Jack Jones outside to end the game. Stout played just 28 of the 67 defensive snaps. He was credited with giving up three catches on four targets for 22 yards and a touchdown, per PFF. I also do want to touch on Kyle Shanahan’s playcalling to end the game here as well.…
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images 49ers hold off furious Commanders’ second-half rally to go 6-0 “Though the Niners escaped with a win, the question now centers on Evans’ health. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Evans’ Achilles injury is the same thing (soreness) he dealt with all week. Shanahan said he didn’t think Evans would need further testing or imaging.” 49ers’ Mike Evans exits Commanders game with Achilles issue, but avoids major injury (paywall) “Head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated Evans avoided a serious injury. Shanahan said Evans couldn’t continue due to what Shanahan had previously termed “Achilles soreness,” an issue that prevented Evans from practicing during the week and made him to questionable to play in Monday’s game.“ Kyle Shanahan on Mike Evans’ injury: ‘We don’t think it’s a long-term thing’ “Christian Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7 against the Falcons. “He had two good practices in. It’s just his first two practices of the year. We were down on wideouts, so it’s still something we discussed. But we decided to give it another week.” Per Shanahan, Demarcus Robinson will not be ready this week.“ How 49ers QB Brock Purdy mastered the art of layering passes over defenders “Renardo Green wants to go fishing. As one who enjoys his time alone, one who appreciates peace, he’s looking forward to picking it up as a pastime. But he’s not thinking of sitting on a boat with his feet up, letting idleness bring him tranquility. That’s not quite the adventure the 49ers cornerback has in mind. He wants to get into the water. Deep water. “In the shallows, I’ll do it (with my hands),” said Green, the San Francisco 49ers’ third-year cornerback. “But I want to go deep-sea fishing and go hop in that water and get to it. I want a spear.” How 49ers QB Brock Purdy mastered the art of layering passes over defenders “Equipped with an iPad and 3D glasses, he watches two squares move in, out and around. His job is to identify how and when those squares converge and diverge with his eyes moving in and out rapidly. Purdy also does daily work with saccades, a rapid eye movement exercise in which he must follow arrows that pop up all over a screen and touch the correct one when prompted. According to Purdy, the goal of the two-to-four-minute sessions is to force him to process movement and information as fast as possible while improving his depth perception. “All those things help me just work on my eyesight, my eyes moving, being quick with my eyes, making quick decisions,” Purdy said. “And then it records my decision-making, how fast, the percentage of getting right and wrong. I do think it helps.”
