title: Bobby Okereke continues to play key role in Panthers' revival
summary: Bobby Okereke had a mixed stint with the New York Giants, but the linebacker's game has progressed in leaps and bounds in the opening five games of his stint at the Carolina Panthers.
full_text:
Bobby Okereke had a mixed stint with the New York Giants, but the linebacker's game has progressed in leaps and bounds in the opening five games of his stint at the Carolina Panthers.

 Okereke - who has deep family ties to Nigeria - takes the Africa Player of the Week for Week 6 for his performance against the Philadelphia Eagles, but he was not the only Nigerian-American NFL star who made a key impact in a win this week.

 Chimere Dike, Oluwafemi Oladejo (both Tennessee Titans) and Osa Odighizuwa (San Francisco 49ers) also put in memorable shifts.

 African Player of the Week: Bobby Okereke (Carolina Panthers) 

 

 Okereke - whose parents are Nigerian and has played a major role in the NFL's development work in Africa and particularly his home country - starred in week 8 with eight tackles, two passes defended and a sack in a 25-14 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

 Seven of Okereke's tackles were solo as he was among the leaders of a stellar defensive performance which saw the Panthers go to 3-2 for the season.

 His sack on Tanner McKee on the first play of the game for an 11-yard loss was one of the most memorable moments of the week.

 With a sack, a forced fumble, an interception, and a total of four passes defended across his first five Panthers games, Okereke is at or near many of his tallies in key areas for the whole of his final season with the Giants.

 The Panthers, too, continue their upward trajectory - having improved year on year since a disastrous 2023 campaign which saw them win only two games. Last season's record of 8-9 was significantly better, and this time, they top the NFC South as it stands.

 

 African Moment of the Week: Chimere Dike (Tennessee Titans) 

 Dike's 58-yard punt return at the beginning of the fourth quarter was an instrumental play for the Tennessee Titans in their 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

 The return came right at the beginning of the quarter, with the Colts leading 13-6. Dike came close to going all the way for the touchdown himself, slicing through at least seven potential tacklers before he was eventually brought down.

 That run nevertheless set up a drive on which the Titans scored and levelled the game, and they never looked back from there - snatching control of the game and clinching their first win of the season.

 Dike - who has Nigerian ties through his father - played a key role. In addition to the 58-yard punt returns, he also tallied 118 yards across five kick returns.

 Honorable mentions 
 Dike's teammate and Nigerian-American compatriot, Oluwafemi Oladejo, scored a surprise touchdown in the Titans' win off a blocked punt.

 Osa Odighizuwa - also of Nigerian descent - picked up a sack in the Monday night game as the San Francisco 49ers beat the Washington Commanders 23-17.

 Another player of Nigerian descent, Emeka Egbuka, scored a touchdown for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Seattle Seahawks' Nick Emmanwori was another player with Nigerian roots to have big plays in a defeat, as he picked up seven tackles and a sack in the 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos.

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone and comes from a family with deep West African ties despite being born in Nacogdoches, Texas himself - tallied 134 yards across 12 receptions in the Week 6 loss.

 Mo Alie-Cox - another NFL player with Sierra Leonean ties - scored a touchdown for the Colts in defeat to the Titans.

 Alvin Kamara (roots in Liberia) crossed over for a crucial touchdown in the New Orleans Saints' 34-27 win over the New York Giants.

 Africa-born Player Watch 

 It was not the best day at the office for Zimbabwe's Nate Landman as his LA Rams went down 18-16 to the Arizona Cardinals, but the linebacker still managed 10 tackles.

 Guinea-born Liberian defensive end Kwity Paye picked up a sack for the Las Vegas Raiders, but also ultimately in defeat as they went down 33-30 to the Buffalo Bills.

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 7: From Eagles to Matthew Stafford
summary: Get ready for Week 7 with takes on the Colts' decision-makers, Caleb Williams' MVP case, Matthew Stafford's play, the Browns' trajectory and the Eagles' next moves.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 7 ? 'Thursday Night Football' between Bears QB Caleb Williams and Patriots QB Drake Maye is a great "future of the league" contest. Bengals at Ravens will always be a banger ... if QB  Lamar Jackson is active. Chiefs at Seahawks on Sunday night will either right the Seattle ship or make the alarm bells scream.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with some reactions to the biggest Monday news -- Jalen Hurts being placed on season-ending injured reserve  and the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard -- before peeking at what's going wrong in Los Angeles and what's going right in Cleveland, of all places.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Colts are right to keep Steichen 
 Eagles should make three trades 
 Williams should be MVP candidate but ... 
 Simmons for Defensive Player of Year 
 Cleveland is a QB away from contending 
 Stafford's age is starting to show 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... Carlie Irsay-Gordon was right to give Shane Steichen more time 
 The Colts (2-4) fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday following their Week 6 loss to the Titans  (1-5). That's the thing about home losses to winless divisional rivals: They spur swift corrective action.

 Interestingly, head coach Shane Steichen was not fired midseason alongside Ballard. As owner  Irsay-Gordon said in her statement released by the Colts : "This does not change our goals for this season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect to compete, improve and win football games." There's a clear message to Steichen in this final line -- that she is leaving the door open for him to coach his way into another year on the job.

 Just how many wins that might take is unclear. ESPN's Football Power Index gives the Colts an 8.8% chance to make the postseason -- something they have not done since 2020. Is Steichen's percent chance to save his job -- 1 in 12 -- about the same?

 

 No matter the size of the crack in the door, I think this is a sharp call by Irsay-Gordon. While midseason coach firings shake up the game-day result more than midseason general manager firings, the primary brunt of the blame in Indianapolis rests with Ballard. Since Andrew Luck's' surprising retirement in 2019, the Colts have ridden a carousel of veteran stopgaps at QB -- Philip Rivers, Jacoby Brissett , Carson Wentz , Matt Ryan,  Gardner Minshew II  and Daniel Jones -- with one huge swing-and-miss at the draft plate in Anthony Richardson Sr .

 No matter the shocking context of Luck's early retirement, Ballard failed to solve the most important position in sports despite several more bites at the apple than the average general manager gets. To be fair, he got unlucky. Richardson's early-career injuries interrupted what was meant to be a long developmental arc. Jones was a wonderful hit in 2025 before injuries derailed his play as well.

 Ballard extended his tenure with strong drafting, but even the success of that approach was overstated. The Colts constantly prioritized size and athleticism early at edge rusher and got burned for it ( Dayo Odeyingbo , Kwity Paye , Laiatu Latu ). Recent picks ( CJ Allen , Justin Walley , Jaylahn Tuimoloau ) needed to fill urgent holes have all become targets for opposing offenses.

 Even if Ballard is a relatively solid drafter, any guy calling the shots for a decade will accumulate a lot of misses -- and the Colts under Ballard have not been aggressive free agency spenders or traders to account for those gaps. At least not until last year, when Ballard's seat really started to get hot. Then he signed safety Cam Bynum and cornerback Charvarius Ward and traded for cornerback Sauce Gardner . They were big and understandable swings given how dire his job security was. But it was too little, too late.

 It was impossible to imagine putting Ballard in charge of another quarterback search. But it is not impossible to imagine handing whatever new quarterback the Colts find in 2027 or 2028 to Steichen. The work Steichen did in 2025 to precipitate not just great, but historically elite numbers from Jones and the offense is a bigger feather in his respective cap than anything Ballard achieved over a decade at the helm of the roster. Steichen remains one of the league's best coaches for optimal fourth-down decision making and clock management. He has been far from perfect -- he failed to develop Richardson. But so did 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan with Trey Lance . Steichen's overall body of work with Jalen Hurts in Philadelphia and Jones in Indianapolis outweighs the Richardson snafu.

 

 So Steichen is good. But can he elevate this group to an acceptable level for ownership? See Irsay-Gordon's statement again: "Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision. Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now." Is she alluding to the hard work of finding a new general manager or the work of moving contracts before the trade deadline  on Nov. 10? Will Steichen be able to save his job coaching an offense without  Quenton Nelson , who has only one year left on his deal and could be a trade target? Or without DeForest Buckner , the frustrated star defensive tackle who deserves a deep playoff run?

 The best historical comparison for Steichen's current position is that of Jim Caldwell, who coached the Lions in 2015. General manager Martin Mayhew was fired after a 1-7 start and the expectation was that Caldwell would meet the same fate. Instead, Caldwell went 6-2 and kept the job for another two seasons. I'm not sure Steichen has the roster necessary to win 75% of his remaining games -- Matthew Stafford is not quarterbacking this team, folks -- even before the Colts start gutting the roster. Then again, I'm still not sure Steichen could possibly go 7-1 with Jones at quarterback, and that literally happened last year.

 

 It's not worth predicting anything with Irsay-Gordon. She is a new owner and is clearly committed to doing things her way. We don't have a scouting report on her yet. But I'm glad she is giving Steichen the season to coach for his job, and I'm excited to see what desperation cooks up in Indianapolis over the next few months.

 
 

 I think ... the following Eagles will be traded to the following teams 
 I expect the Eagles to trade away multiple players at the deadline. It's Howie Roseman! How could they not?

 At 2-4 and with quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve for the rest of the year , the season is lost. Sure, they have enough talent to finish 8-9 or 7-10 -- Tanner McKee is not a terrible backup, receiver  DeVonta Smith  is back in the starting lineup, running back Saquon Barkley  (hamstring) and guard Landon Dickerson  (knee) are soon to join him, and that defense remains ravenous. But Howie Roseman is not the sort of general manager to limp to 8-9 when there are big offseason decisions to be made.

 Is Hurts still the franchise quarterback in Philadelphia? On "This is Football with Kevin Clark" last week, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport openly wondered about the Eagles' plan for Hurts this offseason -- that was before blood clots in Hurts' leg and lungs ended his 2026 season . Is Nick Sirianni still the head coach in Philadelphia? He won a Super Bowl, but his inability to develop coaches and key game-management failures this season invite questions as to his job security.

 

 Roseman has already dipped his toe into the reload waters by dealing center…

title: Bears' Kyler Gordon returns with vengeance, answers critics
summary: In his season debut, Gordon was a huge factor in Chicago's win Sunday after battling through various injuries.
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The ink was barely dry on the  Chicago Bears ' initial 53-man roster when general manager Ryan Poles cast doubt on whether nickel corner Kyler Gordon would ever play another down of football in Chicago.

 " I don't know ," Poles said when asked about Gordon's future with the Bears on Sept. 1, before adding he still had hope.

 Those three words spoke loudest about a frustrating situation inside Halas Hall. The Bears had planned for Gordon, 26, to become a cornerstone in Dennis Allen's defense. But he didn't participate in any team drills during the 2026 offseason because of a right calf injury. He spent all of training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list before being moved to reserve/PUP , which meant he would have to miss at least the first four games. He wasn't even in the building to start the season while rehabbing independently.

 The best way to quell concerns -- at least in the short term -- about dependability was to return to the lineup and dominate, which he wasted little time doing Sunday in Atlanta. Gordon, who was activated Saturday, became the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983 as Chicago held off the Falcons, 31-23 . Gordon became the third Bears player since sacks became official in 1982 to record three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game.

 

 Gordon had a lot to think about as he stood by himself during the anthem inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The highest-paid slot cornerback in the NFL -- $13.3 million per year after signing an extension on April 15, 2025 -- Gordon had played in just five of Chicago's previous 25 games (21%). And while his teammates kept the faith, the injuries created some doubt about his dependability.

 "I mean, it is what it is," Gordon said. "I can't control what someone else says.

 "But at the end of the day, I'm going out there and do my job and do [it to] my best ability and be the best player and the leader at my spot."

 Gordon's talent was never doubted. He was Poles' first draft pick, No. 39 overall in 2022 out of Washington, and Poles rewarded him with the three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed. His skills were on display Sunday, but Gordon has a bigger hurdle to clear: staying healthy.

 

 No stranger to soft tissue injuries, Gordon has dealt with multiple hamstring, calf and groin ailments. He has also had a concussion and a fracture in his right hand.

 "He was ready to play," Bears coach Ben Johnson said. "I talked with Kyler yesterday morning, and [said], 'Hey, I think we want to activate you. Are you ready to go?' And he said, 'Absolutely,' and he sure enough was. So, huge spark there for us on the defense.

 "We've got to make sure that we keep him on that right track. We've tried to limit his role a little bit, just making sure he was in good football shape. But those snaps that he had were huge ones for us today."

 Trying to find the cause of Gordon's injuries 

 Two stints on injured reserve in 2025 prompted the Bears and Gordon to investigate the root of his health problems. Was it overtraining or undertraining? Was it the type of training he was doing on his own? Was an underlying injury issue to blame for what Poles classified in July as "a delay" in his recovery?

 In the offseason, the team organized a virtual meeting, according to a source with direct knowledge of the call, with its decision-makers, trainers, strength and conditioning and other support staff, as well as with people Gordon had hired to work with away from Halas Hall. The purpose was to get all parties on the same page with a plan for Gordon's rehabilitation and offseason training.

 But frustrations continued as Gordon showed up to offseason workouts in late May with a calf injury.

 

 To fully understand the recurring soft-tissue ailments, the Bears then sent him to specialist, according to a source familiar with the request.

 Gordon learned during the rehab process that the issue was not just his calf, but "something wrong with the way the glute was firing that created a posterior chain issue," according to a source. That caused the calf to strain as well as the hamstring.

 Unlike during the previous offseason, Gordon stayed in the Chicagoland area to rehab and train. He worked with Montel Fleming, known as "Dr. Moe," on body alignment and injury prevention. Fleming also works with other Bears players, from Jaylon Johnson to defensive back Cam Lewis and running back D'Andre Swift .

 The Bears told Gordon's camp during the offseason that he could work with "your guy, come back when you're ready," a source with knowledge of the situation recalled. But those on both sides admit that building consensus on how to attack a delicate injury was, at times, frustrating. One issue for Chicago, per a team source, was that multiple players with severe injuries -- offensive tackle  Ozzy Trapilo (torn patellar tendon), pass rusher Dayo Odeyingbo (torn Achilles) and linebacker Noah Sewell  (torn Achilles) -- returned to the team and the field before Gordon.

 Poles said on Sept. 1 : "Any time you have an injury and you're coming back from something there's discomfort that you have to push through and that's what it comes down to. So we haven't been able to get over that hump and we're not progressing as fast as we'd like."

 But Gordon's injury was much more complicated than a calf strain, a source added.

 That Gordon was away from the team -- front offices and coaching staffs typically prefer their players rehab injuries at the team facility -- was an additional layer to consider.

 And the Bears' messaging about Gordon's injury was hard to ignore. In June, while citing Gordon's on-field impact as undeniable, Ben Johnson pointed out that "you can only develop trust [as a player] by being available." That seemingly applied public pressure on Gordon, as did Poles' "I don't know" comment. A source involved believes the team was attempting to "light a fire" under Gordon with those comments.

 Asked Sunday if his team and the Bears' medical staff are on the same page as far as working with Fleming, Gordon said: "Think that'd be a question for Coach."

 Gordon tried to find the positives in what he went through last season, when he played in just three regular-season games and both postseason contests.

 "I've just never been through that before," he said. "So obviously just learning to have that delusional optimism and just use that.

 "So it's been great. Learned a lot and now we're here. So God's great."

 Gordon didn't say he was vindicated, or needed to be 

 If there was doubt outside the locker room, it wasn't shared by Gordon's teammates.

 "My dog came back after all the talk, all the chatter, worked his ass off, came back and balled," Jaylon Johnson said.

 When asked what it meant to have Gordon back, defensive end Daniel Hardy said: "Everything, man. That guy came out here and put his heart and soul on tape. Phenomenal athlete.

 "He was working his butt off trying to get back to us and y'all could see it out there. He wasn't just chilling at home. He was out there grinding and working and getting his body healthy so he could come back and be the star that he is."

 

 Receiver Rome Odunze played with Gordon at Washington and still gets caught by surprise by his teammate.

 "You think you've seen it all from that guy and then he goes out there and does some stuff like that," Odunze said. "He's one of those players that gets you up out of your seat for sure. The way he moves, his ability to impact the game is incredible.

 "So, super glad to have him back."

 A Bears defense that had allowed 6.2 yards per play (30th in NFL) and ranked 28th in explosive play rate allowed (7.6%) prior to his return Sunday believes Gordon could fix some of the unit's biggest vulnerabilities.

 The Falcons entered the game averaging 361.8 yards per game and were held to 257. Gordon's impact off the nickel blitz was a major factor.

 "Because…

title: How Browns' past two draft classes are catching the NFL's attention
summary: From offensive playmakers to unknowns at QB, here is a look at the bedrock of Cleveland's young core.
full_text:
It's late October, and the Cleveland Browns (4-2) are in first place in a wide-open AFC North, positioning them as potentially one of the best stories in football through six weeks.

 The young Browns have assumed the defiantly passionate and infectious personality of their coach, Todd Monken. And thanks to back-to-back impactful draft classes, this upstart team is on a path to competing for a division title.

 "The Browns are the Browns? F--- that," as Monken exclaimed after a Week 2 win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Browns players have rallied behind a mentality of not letting teams bully them and redefining how people speak about Cleveland football. Buzz around the league, per sources, is that this build has the early feel of a new, different Browns era.

 "Everybody obsesses about QB, but it absolutely matters what environment you place a quarterback in. Look at the Browns, young team, looks like two straight strong drafts," one AFC assistant general manager told ESPN. "If they keep developing that talent next year, we're going to say that's a real good environment for a young QB."

 

 Over the past two draft classes, eight of the Browns' 10 picks in the first three rounds are starters on the 2026 roster. A ninth, safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren , plays a key third safety role and stepped in for starter reps after Grant Delpit  suffered a concussion Sunday. And rival league executives are raving about the Browns' draft classes.

 One AFC personnel director chimed in: "EMW [McNeil-Warren] was my guy."

 It turns out a lot of the Browns "guys" were in demand, but Cleveland's front office, led by general manager Andrew Berry, plus assistant GMs Glenn Cook and Catherine Hickman, did the work and those picks are performing on the field.

 The Browns' Day 1 and Day 2 selections have already shown signs of immediate success.

 "When you talk to Andrew Berry, it's almost like talking to a computer," one longtime NFL executive who knows Berry well told ESPN. "He's structured. He's detailed and programmed. He does a great job articulating that with ownership. He's responded with strong drafts.

 "The challenging part is it takes a stomach to stick with it. Sometimes, the head coach, general manager or both don't last through that pain. But you must give credit to that whole organization for standing strong through Berry's plan, and you see it paying off."

 The Browns have had 2,802 total snaps from their 2025 and 2026 draft picks this season, which ranks behind only the Miami Dolphins (3,348).

 Two massive trades -- dealing defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams and facilitating the Jacksonville Jaguars ' draft-day trade up for two-way star Travis Hunter -- helped Cleveland replenish several high picks it lost trading for Deshaun Watson in March 2022. And the team has even more draft capital in 2027, with two first-round picks and 11 total selections.

 

 Berry made clear to ESPN in August that the Garrett trade did not change Cleveland's timeline toward winning, but the offer was "too good to pass up."

 "You think about it like we get three or four good players and $20-30 million saved from trading Myles. Now, you're giving up a great player in Myles. We think that's worth it," Berry said. "You never go into a season expecting to have as big of an impact of rookies that we did last year. That's unusual. We'd never expect to duplicate that immediate production with this group. But we're happy and optimistic about the guys we have."

 Fast-forward to October and there are indicators that Berry and his team have talented young players on offense. Denzel Boston (pick No. 39) leads all NFL rookies in receiving yards (345) while wide receiver KC Concepcion (pick No. 24), left tackle Spencer Fano (pick No. 9) and right guard Austin Barber (pick No. 86) all play key starting roles.

 Here's a look at what is starting to become foundational classes from the Browns' past two drafts:

 

 Offensive playmakers: RB Quinshon Judkins , TE Harold Fannin Jr ., RB Dylan Sampson , WR KC Concepcion, WR Denzel Boston 
 The Browns' offense has struggled with slow starts, but their offensive skill position players have flashed in their young careers. Boston has quickly established himself as the team's most reliable pass catcher. His 6-foot-4 and 215-pound frame has made him a prototypical "X" receiver in Monken's scheme.

 "Boston was a great pick. We loved Boston; he was our No.1 WR in the draft," one NFC general manager told ESPN. "The size, physicality. People were just scared of the speed. That was a great pick. They've done well using him to his strengths."

 Boston, Concepcion (186 yards) and Fannin (166) rank 1-2-3 in receiving yards on the team. Last season, Judkins (pick No. 36) led all NFL rookie running backs in rushing before sustaining a season-ending right ankle injury and fractured fibula in Week 16. Neither he nor Sampson (pick No. 126 in 2025) played in Cleveland's Week 6 win against the Baltimore Ravens because of injuries, but both are expected to return to the lineup soon to lead the Browns' backfield.

 

 

 Defensive pillars: DT Mason Graham , LB Carson Schwesinger , S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren 
 Cleveland's defense hasn't skipped a beat without Garrett or former defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz, and their recent draft picks have played a big role.

 Schwesinger, the 2025 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year and the Browns' No. 33 pick, made the play of the game against the Ravens, forcing a fourth-quarter fumble by running back Derrick Henry that led to a Browns touchdown. Already regarded as one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL, Schwesinger looks like a star.

 Graham, whom the Browns drafted with the No. 5 pick after trading back from the No. 2 slot with the Jaguars, recorded four sacks before a sprained MCL and ankle sidelined him the past two games.

 McNeil-Warren's snaps were increasingly weekly before Delpit's injury, and he is a de facto starter.

 

 Starting offensive linemen: LT Spencer Fano, RG Austin Barber 
 Two rookies make up a new-look offensive line for the Browns. One was expected, while another came as a surprise. Fano quickly earned his role in training camp as the franchise's left tackle. Barber was drafted after spending his college career (Florida) at tackle, but in the middle of camp, the team experimented with Barber at guard. He excelled in the summer, and an injury to Teven Jenkins opened the pathway for Barber to start, which he hasn't relinquished.

 Fano has recorded run block win rates and pass block win rates in the eighth and sixth percentiles, respectively, for tackles, according to ESPN Analytics and NFL Next Gen Stats. Barber has fared better, recording run block win rates and pass block win rates in the 50th and 68th percentiles, respectively. Both rookies have contributed to an overall improved offensive line in 2026.

 

 TBD roles: C Parker Brailsford , LB Justin Jefferson , TE Joe Royer , TE Carsen Ryan 

 

 Brailsford, a 2026 fifth-round pick, entered camp as a potential option to start at center, but a wrist injury derailed him. He has been inactive for all but one game. Jefferson, another 2026 fifth-round pick, has appeared in two games, contributing solely on special teams.

 Ryan, a seventh-round pick this year, has played on special teams and been used sparingly as a No. 3 tight end.

 Royer, a 2026 fifth-round pick, missed all of camp and has been on the non-football injury/illness list because of undisclosed personal reasons.

 

 QB questions: QB Dillon Gabriel , QB Shedeur Sanders , QB Taylen Green 
 Though Watson has engineered four game-winning drives this season, his contract expires after the season. His prior struggles and injuries led Cleveland to select three quarterbacks in the past two drafts.

 Gabriel and Sanders, both 2025 picks, started a combined 13 games as rookies, but neither did enough to merit consideration as the long-term answer at the position.…

title: NFL announces U2 will play in first Thanksgiving Eve halftime show
summary: The former Super Bowl halftime performers will join names like Beyonce who have headlined Netflix's holiday halftime shows.
full_text:
The first Thanksgiving Eve NFL game will include a legendary musical guest.

 On Tuesday, the NFL announced that U2 will play the halftime show during the Nov. 25 matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams , airing on Netflix. The band will take the stage at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, which will also be the site of Super Bowl LXI -- which is still waiting on a musical guest confirmation for its halftime show.

 

 U2 played the Super Bowl XXXVI halftime show in 2002, several months after the 9/11 terrorist attacks. Lead singer Bono wore a jacket with an American flag lining, and the band played three songs: "Beautiful Day," "MLK" and "Where the Streets Have No Name."

 Thanksgiving Day has often been a prime spot for stunning halftime show performances. Dolly Parton dressed up in a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader outfit for her performance in 2023, Mariah Carey was carried onto the field by musclemen in 2005's game in Detroit, and Shaboozey wore a Detroit Lions jacket in his show in 2024. Netflix has also made its halftime shows a priority, bringing Beyoncé to its Christmas Day game in 2024 and Snoop Dogg in 2025.

 The band's sixteenth studio album, "Carnaval de Luz," will be released on Nov. 13. U2 has released three singles from it already: "Street of Dreams," "Silencio" and "The Greatest Show on Earth." U2 is planning a world tour in support of the album in 2027.

title: What does firing GM Ballard mean for Colts coach Steichen?
summary: Carlie Irsay-Gordon made a big change Monday, but is it the first of many as the trade deadline nears?
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- When the Indianapolis Colts introduced Chris Ballard as their general manager on Jan. 30, 2017, they were elated to land one of the hottest executive candidates in the league.

 Late owner Jim Irsay made brief remarks before ceding the microphone to Ballard in the initial news conference. But Irsay expressed plenty in his short statement, saying of Ballard, "I really feel Chris is the best candidate for general manager that has come about so far in the 21st century."

 Flash forward nearly 10 years and fans on Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium were heartily chanting "Fire Ballard!" as the clock ticked down on the Colts' stunning loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans .

 Irsay's bold statement was quite a claim to live up to, but Ballard's vision for the Colts never came close to producing the results Indianapolis expected.

 No division titles. Two playoff appearances and one playoff victory. A sub-.500 record at 72-82-1.

 It all culminated in Ballard's firing on Monday.

 Now the Colts are at a crossroads. Many questions are left to be addressed. Here are a few:

 Will coach Shane Steichen survive? 

 Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, Jim Irsay's eldest daughter, seemed to tie the fates of Ballard and coach Shane Steichen together. She met with them privately late last season, amid a seven-game, season-ending losing streak marked by injuries. In that meeting, she granted them another year at the helm.

 

 It was, she said, a final chance to demonstrate that they could deliver.

 "We have been very clear with [Ballard] and [Steichen], but giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher," Irsay-Gordon said in January.

 But after firing Ballard but not Steichen, it at least raises the possibility that Steichen will be judged on his own merits. Unlikely as a return for the coach might seem, Steichen does have a solid reputation in NFL circles. Had he been fired after last season, sources told ESPN he was likely to be in the mix for other head coaching opportunities.

 But, for the time being, Steichen's seat remains quite hot.

 Could other major changes be looming? 

 There was a notable line in Irsay-Gordon's statement on Monday:

 "Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision," she said. "Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now."

 Did she mean this generally? Or could it also be a hint at what is to come in the near term?

 

 In either case, the Colts are heading for changes in the future. Big roster moves are certain to be among those changes once a new GM takes over and begins acting on personal preferences.

 In light of the looming Nov. 10 trade deadline, the Colts have to at least consider moving some of their valuable players. At the top of that list are guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner .

 Both are in the final seasons of their contracts and continue to show moments of dominance. Thirty-year-old Nelson, an eight-time All-Pro, was engaged in contract talks before the season but did not reach a deal. It is unclear where things stood before Ballard's firing. Buckner was coming off neck surgery earlier this year and had considered retirement, but he has surpassed expectations since his return. Even at 32, he is drawing double-teams on 74.5% of his pass-rush snaps, the highest rate of his career.

 Buckner on Sunday was outspoken about his frustration.

 "I'm pissed off," he said. "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year."

 Offloading players at the trade deadline would be a reversal of philosophy for the Colts, who recently were making calls to the Arizona Cardinals about potentially pursuing receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . before he was traded to Houston.

 But the situation changed pretty dramatically after Sunday's loss and Ballard's dismissal. The Colts now sit at 2-4 and face Minnesota and Jacksonville in their next two games -- teams with a combined record of 9-2.

 What's next at QB? 
 The Colts' next GM is unlikely to have any ties to current starting quarterback Daniel Jones , increasing the odds Jones could be elsewhere in 2027.

 Jones is struggling mightily in his return from the ruptured Achilles he suffered last season. He ranks near the bottom of the league among starting quarterbacks in several key statistical categories, including QBR (30th), completion percentage (29th) and yards per attempt (29th). Jones had a career-best 68% completion rate in 2025, but in 2026 is completing a career-low 59.6% of his attempts.

 There are mitigating factors, like the lack of dependable receiving targets, but it is difficult to envision Jones having a future in Indianapolis under a new executive unless something changes. Jones signed a lucrative extension in March, agreeing to a two-year, $88 million deal. The Colts can void Jones' deal after this season, but it will come at the cost of $35 million in dead money that must be accounted for on their 2027 salary cap.

 Not to be ignored is 2023 fourth-overall draft pick Anthony Richardson Sr ., who remains on the Colts' roster, but hasn't started a game since 2024. Richardson is in the final year of his rookie contract.

 

 How will new ownership handle decisions? 

 This is a pivotal moment for Irsay-Gordon and her sisters. They are charged for the first time since their father's death last year with overseeing key decisions that will shape the franchise. They've long been involved in the decision-making process, but the final call historically rested with their dad.

 Now, the three sisters will have final say.

 Among the key things to watch is whom they will rely upon for counsel. Jim Irsay routinely sought the advice of people like Bill Polian, his former GM and team president, and Tony Dungy, the Colts' Hall of Fame former coach. Will Irsay's daughters use a similar approach? Do they have trusted advisers around the game to assist with the challenge of hiring a new GM?

 Colts COO Pete Ward remains with the franchise, as he has been for more than four decades. He remains one of the sisters' closest advisers and can help them navigate a GM search.

 But the Irsay sisters have always felt prepared.

 "We were exposed to every area you could possibly think of," Kalen Jackson, the youngest Irsay sister, said last year. Their father, she said, "never cut us out of any areas of any kind. And I think that will help us in this transition [to ownership]."

title: Three things that are working for the Jaguars and three things they need to fix
summary: We're examining three things that are working (and three that are not working) for 4-2 Jaguars as they enter their Week 7 bye.
full_text:
LONDON --  Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen watched his team give up 34 points, have a touchdown taken off the board because of a penalty, throw an interception in the end zone, get hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone and give up three plays of 30 or more yards.

 So, naturally, he was upset at the 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium on a last-second field goal. But he wasn't shaken.

 "I've got a lot of confidence in this team," Coen said. "We didn't get the result we wanted [against Houston]. We're not going to change a thing about our process. Do we have to evaluate and clean up areas in which we need to, specifically in some areas that we just talked about? Absolutely.

 

 "But I have a lot of confidence in this team."

 The Jaguars enter their bye week with a  4-2 record and are atop the AFC South with a two-game lead over the Indianapolis Colts and Texans. Their next four opponents have a combined record of 10-13 -- and one of those games is in Jacksonville against the Colts, who haven't beaten the Jaguars on the road since 2014.

 Quarterback  Trevor Lawrence  agrees with his coach's confidence heading into an off week.

 "We'll have some time to reflect and just see what we need to get better at," Lawrence said after throwing for 300 yards in back-to-back games for just the second time in his career. "I think our team, we've got a lot of confidence. We know who we are. We're not going to go soul-searching or anything like that; it's just how can we continue to do the little things better and better because they cost you in these tight games."

 Let's take a look at three things that have gone right and three that have gone wrong with the Jaguars through the first six games.

 

 Three things that are working for the Jaguars 
 Lawrence is playing at a high level 
 Lawrence leads the NFL with 14 passing touchdowns and leads the NFL in off-target percentage (9.0%) -- which is by far the lowest of his career (15% in 2025 was his previous low). That stat focuses solely on ball placement, and it shows Lawrence has been accurate.

 It also an indication of how good Lawrence's decision-making has been, save for the end zone interception he threw Sunday. And he's doing all that while averaging a career-high 8.0 yards per attempt, too.

 

 Lawrence has yet to play at a high level for a complete season. He had good stretches in the second half of the 2022 and 2025 seasons but struggled in the first parts of those seasons. Not this year ... he's off to a hot start in 2026. If he's able to maintain the pace and the Jaguars again reach the playoffs, he should be in the MVP conversation.

 
 The run defense 
 The Jaguars led the NFL in rush defense last season and have continued to do so this season under coordinator Anthony Campanile. Opponents are averaging only 72.2 yards per game against them, and a player hasn't rushed for 75 or more yards in a game against them in the Jaguars' past 24 matchups.

 Nose tackle DaVon Hamilton has anchored the middle of the defensive line, but Coen said ends Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker , linebackers  Foyesade Oluokun and Ventrell Miller , and safety Antonio Johnson are big parts, as well.

 Every week the first thing the defensive staff and players emphasize is stopping the run, regardless of which team and quarterback they're facing.

 "It's the standard," Coen said. "It's one of our core pillars of success. And I think those guys have bought into it."

 
 Travis Hunter is emerging 
 Hunter is coming off the best game of his career -- four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown, plus an end zone interception on defense -- and Coen said the Jaguars have to "keep building off of it."

 

 With cornerback Montaric Brown out the past two weeks because of a hamstring injury, the Jaguars didn't use the rotation they had been using through the first month, and Hunter has played every defensive snap. He hadn't been used much offensively (just two catches) until Sunday, when he played a season-high eight offensive snaps.

 Hunter has six pass breakups, and his 57.3 passer rating on throws in which targeted is the 12th best in the league, per NFL Next Gen Stats. It's easy to forget Hunter has played only 13 games after missing 10 last season because of a knee injury, but it looks like he's starting to settle in and get more comfortable as the season progresses.

 

 Three things that the Jaguars need to fix 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr .'s lack of production 
 At this point, the biggest question with Thomas is whether he'll be on the roster after the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Thomas dropped one pass while wide open in the first quarter and failed to come up with a catchable ball late in the first half of the Jaguars' loss to Houston. Those cost the Jaguars at least six points -- the second one would have allowed the Jaguars to try a long field goal at the buzzer and the first would have put them well into Little's field goal range.

 Thomas was benched at halftime and we might not see him as a significant part of the offense again. Rookie sixth-round pick  Josh Cameron played more in the second half and so did Hunter, who had three catches for 40 yards and a touchdown after halftime. After the game, Coen said Hunter's offensive role needs to expand.

 Coen also didn't exactly throw his support behind Thomas the way he has in the past when asked about Thomas' struggles with drops and contact. His response on whether it's tough to have confidence in Thomas going forward: "Week to week. Guys have to step up and make plays."

 

 Thomas has nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, which puts him on pace for 26 catches for 298 yards and three touchdowns. His lack of production is surprising considering he had a good offseason -- outside of Parker Washington , Thomas was the most impressive offensive player in OTAs and training camp. But he had two drops in Week 2 against the Broncos and hasn't recovered.

 Cameron and Hunter have both earned bigger roles, which would leave Thomas as, at best, the sixth option as a pass catcher behind Washington, Jakobi Meyers , Brenton Strange , Cameron and Hunter. He's maybe even behind Bhayshul Tuten , too. The Jaguars might decide it's time to move on and see what they can get in a trade.

 
 The pass rush 
 The Jaguars are tied for 10th in the NFL in QB pressures (81) but are tied for 20th in sacks with 11. The top two pass rushers -- Hines-Allen and Walker -- have a combined 3.5 sacks. Three of those sacks came in the season opener (each had 1.5). Hines-Allen hasn't had one since, and Walker managed a half sack against the Eagles in Week 5. That has not been good enough.

 Nobody has emerged as a reliable No. 3 pass rusher, either. B.J. Green II had a great camp but was injured in the opener and is on IR. Linebacker Dennis Gardeck and DT Hamilton are tied for third with four QB hits.

 The Jaguars were counting on improved coverage in the secondary forcing quarterbacks to hold onto the ball longer to give the rush time to get home. That hasn't happened. Opposing quarterbacks are getting rid of the ball in 2.76 seconds -- the sixth-quickest in the league.

 

 The Jaguars didn't add a pass rusher in the offseason but that's something they should consider at the trade deadline. It might require multiple draft picks because they have only $5 million in cap space -- third-lowest in the league -- and might have to pay a higher price to entice a team to retain some salary, depending on whom they pursue. Arizona's Josh Sweat and Miami's Josh Uche are mentioned as possibly being on the trading block. An intriguing option could be Khalil Mack . He's on a one-year deal with the Los Angeles Chargers , who have $30 million in cap space per Roster Management and could still retain some of his salary.

 
 Kickoff coverage 
 The Jaguars are allowing 28.9 yards per kickoff return (ranked fourth-worst). The problem earlier in the season was the coverage…

title: Fantasy football buzz: McLaurin, Evans injuries; Should you cut your Chargers?
summary: Mike Evans, Terry McLaurin leave Monday night action early. Plus, what do you do with your Chargers?
full_text:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

 Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

 
 Oct. 20: McLaurin, Evans leave MNF with injuries 
 By Michael F. Florio 

 Injuries were, unfortunately, the main story on Monday night.  Terry McLaurin left early in the game as a result of a knee injury. He had to be carted off the field wearing an air cast . He seems likely to miss significant time. Mike Evans exited late in the first half -- after recording three catches for 94 yards -- due to an Achilles injury. Evans had been playing through this injury for the last couple of weeks. It seems likely he'll miss some time to allow this injury to heal.

 
 The Evans injury led to more volume for the 49ers' stars. Both Christian McCaffrey (10) and George Kittle (8) had a season-high in targets. Both were already weekly must-starts but this added volume means even more production in fantasy. 
 Even without McLaurin, Jayden Daniels  remains a weekly must-start. One week after running for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, he threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns. He has now scored at least 19 fantasy points in 17 out of his 22 career full games (77%). One thing to watch, however? He's been sacked nine times over the last two weeks. 
 Stefon Diggs  saw seven targets on Monday night, going for 44 yards and a touchdown. He should see a boost in both targets and fantasy value as the top option for Daniels. 
 Chig Okonkwo  is worth adding off the waiver wire for those streaming tight end. He saw seven targets, catching all of them for 69 yards. He led the Commanders in both catches and yards. His targets have increased each game this season and he may just be the No. 2 target for Daniels moving forward. 
 Treylon Burks left the game late. The Commanders are banged up at WR, meaning more volume could also go the way of Antonio Williams . Williams is worth a flier in 12-team leagues or deeper. 
 Rachaad White played on 71% of snaps, with seven carries and five targets. He turned that into 57 yards, a touchdown and 15.7 fantasy points. He is in play as an RB2 or flex option weekly with Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR. 
 After averaging 27.0 fantasy PPG over the season's first three weeks, Brock Purdy has cooled off averaging just 17.7 FPPG over the last three weeks. He still has been an extremely safe option and gets a bounceback opportunity next week against the  Atlanta Falcons , who have allowed the third-most passing yards. 
 
 Time to cut your Chargers? 
 

 So, you drafted a Charger and are not sure what to do with them heading into the team's bye week?

 Many of them are droppable, starting with Justin Herbert . He has not reached 14 fantasy points in any game this season and is currently the overall QB25. Numerous QBs who have missed multiple games ( Lamar Jackson , Daniels, Michael Penix Jr ) have scored more fantasy points that Herbert. The only place I wouldn't let him go is in a superflex league, where all starting QBs are rostered.

 The toughest decision is with Omarion Hampton . He's a talented back with double-digit touches in every game. It's hard to give up on this kind of player. The issue is that the Chargers are splitting their snaps in thirds between their three RBs. The Chargers' interior offensive line is struggling to create running lanes and the offense, as a whole, is struggling to create consistent scoring opportunities.

 I have a lot of shares of Hampton but, as tempting as it has been, I have not yet dropped him. In 12-team leagues or deeper, you have no choice but to hold on. In 10-team leagues, it comes down to your RB depth. I played Rachaad White over Hampton in one league this week, which is making me question why I haven't dropped him. Still, after looking over the waiver wire, there's simply more upside in holding onto Hampton.

 Ladd McConkey is the other question. McConkey has been extremely banged up and has left early in all but one game this season. I still believe in the talent -- and the bye week should (hopefully) allow him to get healthy. Please? I'm not ready to give up on McConkey and would keep him. However, the rest of the Chargers can be dropped if you're in need of finding a bye week replacement.

 Of course, in most leagues, waivers don't run until early Wednesday morning. Spend today trying to trade any of these guys in exchange for a player you may like more than what's available on the waiver wire. Who knows? There may just be a manager in your league who still believes in a big name like Herbert.

 
 Oct. 19: How Davante Adams injury affects Rams offense 
 

 By Tristan H. Cockcroft 

 The news on Davante Adams ' injury suffered Sunday is devastating, as Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that the veteran wide receiver has a ruptured hamstring and will miss 6 to 10 weeks . Adams is the No. 7 wide receiver in fantasy points (102.0, or 17.0 per game), and he had been a top-10 weekly scorer in three of his first five games.

 

 A 6-to-10 week timetable effectively ends Adams' fantasy regular season, as the midpoint of that range would take us through Week 14, directly before standard league playoffs begin. Though most leagues offer IR spots in which he could be stashed, steering through the bye weeks while keeping him there -- even if you're granted two or more of them -- isn't easy to do. If you need roster flexibility for bye weeks or injury fill-ins, it's reasonable to drop Adams in order to seek replacements. For now, try to keep him stashed there once he's officially moved to injured reserve, considering his past production and fantasy playoffs utility. The Rams have an extremely favorable Week 15 matchup for the position (DAL), as one example.

 In Adams' absence, the Rams' offense takes a noticeable hit, as Adams and fellow Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had accounted for 42% of the team's total targets for the season, and that's despite Nacua having missed two games due to a groin injury. Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington will all likely see expanded roles while Adams is out, with Mumpfied the closest to fantasy relevant and more so in 12-team leagues with deep benches or 14-plus-team formats. Be aware, however, that those three totaled 12 targets and 24.4 fantasy points during Nacua's Weeks 2-3 absences, reflecting their low priority in the receiving pecking order.

 

 It's the Rams' tight ends who should benefit most while Adams heals, as was the case in those same Weeks 2-3 games. Terrance Ferguson scored 17.4 fantasy points on nine targets in Week 2, before injuring his MCL in Week 3 and landing on IR. Tyler Higbee emerged with 20.2 fantasy points on 11 targets in Week 3, and he has now averaged 12.4 points and 6.8 targets in the past four weeks. Higbee is a definite add in any league larger than ESPN's standard, and Ferguson, who is eligible to return in Week 8, could warrant similar appeal if he's ready to play a week from now.

 Stafford, meanwhile, will probably be more matchup dependent while Adams is sidelined. The veteran quarterback has been hit-or-miss for much of the season to date, but he'd offer his best fantasy utility for what align as favorable matchups in Weeks 9 (WSH), 10 (@ARI) and 15 (DAL).

 Oct. 19: Who got the ball on Sunday? 
 

 By Eric Moody 

 The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Most of Week 6 is in the books, so we're already looking ahead to Week 7. Which games grabbed our analysts' attention?

 The Minnesota Vikings will look to keep their perfect start going when they host the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. The Vikings are early 5.5-point favorites, tied for the second-largest spread of the week.

 

 The New York Jets visit the winless  Miami Dolphins in a game that has the second-lowest points total of the week (38.5).

 The Pittsburgh Steelers , fresh off an overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , will face the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in Paris.

 Who do we like? Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado and Eric Moody break down the games and share the bets they're backing before potential odds shifts later in the week.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings    and subject to change. 

 
 Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . 

 

   Minnesota Vikings -5.5 vs. Indianapolis Colts 
 Bowen: I'll take Minnesota and give the points because of Brian Flores' defense. This unit is allowing a league-low 12.8 PPG and leads the NFL with a blitz rate of 67.6%. The Vikings will heat up the pocket versus Daniel Jones and a Colts offense that is limited without a true vertical element in the game plan. I like Minnesota to cover at home.

 Last week: Buccaneers +3 (Result: Steelers 26, Buccaneers 19 in OT )

   Pittsburgh Steelers -2.5 at New Orleans Saints 
 Moody: The Steelers have won two straight, including an overtime victory last Sunday in Tampa Bay. The Saints have allowed 31.7 points per game over their last three contests and rank 29th in total yards allowed. New Orleans has also struggled against the run, allowing 138 rushing yards per game through six weeks. That should give Steelers running back Jaylen Warren opportunities to make an impact. title: PSG unveil jersey for Steelers vs. Saints NFL game in Paris
summary: If you've ever wondered what reigning Champions League holders PSG might look like should they suddenly relaunch as an NFL franchise, this is it.
full_text:
The NFL International Series has seen games take place in the U.K., Australia, Brazil, Germany, the Republic of Ireland and Spain in the past. But Sunday's matchup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris will be the first to take place on French soil ( watch live on NFL Network at 9:30 a.m. ET ).

 As such, Paris Saint-Germain are gearing up for the big occasion in a very literal sense by releasing a special-edition football jersey designed by Fanatics in collaboration with the NFL and Nike.

 - Ranking the Premier League's best long-distance goals 
- Champions League Power Rankings before MD3: Who's No. 1? 
- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Who has the stronger claim to win the Ballon d'Or? 

 If you've ever wondered what the two-time reigning UEFA Champions League holders and perennial Ligue 1 champions might look like should they suddenly relaunch as a new NFL franchise, this is it.

 

 The jersey is available in two colorways, the first being PSG's traditional colors of blue, red and white and the second being a lustrous mix of maroon and gold.

 

 Styled to look like NFL jerseys with a loose fit and a deep V-neck, the designs feature PSG's club crest and an array of Parisian details including stylish monograms, the local two-digit French department code (No. 75) and the fleur-de-lis, which appears on the French club's crest as well as that of the Saints.

 The crossover shirts have gone on sale this week, giving both PSG and NFL fans the chance to get their attire in order ahead of the game this coming weekend.

 However, they are not the first hybrid soccer/NFL jerseys to have been made available. Here are some of the best that have been released over the past decade.

 

 Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur (2018) 
 

 Released in 2018 ahead of London's first NFL International Series game, Chelsea were furnished with a limited-edition jersey that came in plain blue and white with Eden Hazard's name and number splashed across the back.

 Tottenham were also bestowed with an NFL-style jersey in 2018 alongside their London rivals. With Harry Kane known to be a huge NFL fan who holds ambitions of becoming a kicker in the league one day, the simple white design presumably went down very well with Spurs' then-star striker.

 PSG and Barcelona  (2018) 
 

 PSG and Barcelona formed a mini-capsule of European heavyweights to receive the NFL crossover treatment. Both jerseys comprised simplified versions of the traditional club colours, with Brazilian pair Neymar and Philippe Countinho occupying the respective name tapes.

 Inter Milan  (2025) 
 

 Released as part of a range to coincide with the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup in the United States, Inter's NFL jersey was a fairly straightforward design. At least the Nerazzurri colors of black, blue and bright yellow helped lend a little extra contrast and "pop" to proceedings.

 Australia  (2026) 
 

 Created as part of a limited range of "football x football" NFL-style hybrid jerseys for the 2026 FIFA World Cup (hence the number stitched on the front and rear), Australia's design certainly looked the part in vibrant gold and green.

 England  (2026) 
 

 Also part of Nike's bespoke range of 2026 World Cup offerings, England's rose-red design came with smart tonal detailing and the Three Lions badge affixed to both sleeves.

 France  (2026) 
 

 The crème de la crème of the 2026 World Cup range was definitely the France design which looked like a legit NFL jersey with its deep blue base and bold tricolore detailing. There might be a few sporting this jersey when France gets its first taste of live NFL action this weekend.

title: Can the Saints carry their winning momentum into Paris?
summary: After New Orleans snapped its three-game losing streak, the team's focus quickly turns to Week 7 in France.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Some of the New Orleans Saints didn't quite know what to make of their 34-27 win against the New York Giants on Sunday.

 A video of Saints coach Kellen Moore's postgame speech showed the contrast. While players clapped and cheered as Moore handed out game balls, the overall atmosphere was subdued despite the win snapping a three-game losing streak.

 The Saints got the job done, but it had taken a monumental effort for a game that seemed well in hand in the fourth quarter. The Saints had even started to pull a few starters when up 34-10 with 11:30 left to play, but a fumble by CJ Donaldson got the Giants back in the game. The Saints (2-4) allowed three touchdowns in the last seven minutes and had to make a stop at their own 14-yard line to secure the win.

 

 "Most important thing in this league is that you got the win," Saints safety Justin Reid said. "I mean, this league is measured in wins and losses. It's not measured in scores. I thought that in a lot of ways, there's a lot of ways for us to continue to improve, but we showed up to the plate when we needed to and was able to close out a tough game. One of the big lessons that we can learn though is to continue to press the issue and not take our foot off the gas at any moment."

 Saints guard and team captain David Edwards made a brief statement in the postgame locker room, imploring everyone to use the game as a starting point as they head into a second road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris ( Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network ). The Saints flew to France immediately after the Giants game to get set up for the week ahead.

 "We won this game because of our week of preparation and our mindset, period. How do we carry that moving forward? Positive, all together, that's who we are," Edwards said. "We showed that today, how do we build on that? That's our f---ing objective this week coming up. You got me?"

 This week in France and Sunday's Week 7 game won't be without its own distractions. The NFL announced Sunday that the game is still scheduled as planned despite civil unrests and protests that have been happening over the past month in France.

 Saints players said they had a security briefing before they left for Paris and will take precautions when sightseeing in the early part of the week.

 Despite the outside disruptions, the Saints hope this week can be used as a "reset." Moore sees the trip as an opportunity for the players to spend more time together. "This is obviously a continuation of an extended trip going from New York to here," the coach said.

 

 New Orleans is also banking on time away from home as a means to figure out why nothing, not even their two wins, have come easily. In Week 2, the Saints had to come back from an 11-point deficit to beat the Baltimore Ravens   24-17 .

 The Saints' issues on offense have been abundant: An inconsistent kicking game, a struggling run game and shaky offensive line play that resulted in quarterback Tyler Shough breaking two bones in his left hand.

 Shough has had season lows in passing yards in the two complete games since the injury, but he also threw three touchdowns against the Giants. His up-and-down performances have mirrored the team's performances. They played their best football in spurts during the Giants game and looked lost at other times.

 Shough said he knows how good the team can be without self-inflicted mistakes. The QB hopes they take the good part of the Giants game and apply it to their practice week in Paris.

 "This is a good stepping stone for how we can continue to build and put this together," Shough said. "Still wasn't a complete game, but against a really good team in New York, man, it's a huge win for sure. So we've got to keep climbing and building off of it."

title: Jameis Winston vs. J.J. McCarthy: Pros and cons of Giants' QBs
summary: Coach John Harbaugh must weigh the options in his QB conundrum, with two players who could start at Houston.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants have a quarterback decision to make. 
 
 They can go with the veteran Jameis Winston , who just lost his first game as a starter this season, or the recently acquired and still somewhat unknown J.J. McCarthy on the road Sunday against the Houston Texans ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). 
 
 Coach John Harbaugh declined to make a decision on Monday, although it does appear to be coming soon with the Giants (3-2-1) scheduled to have a team meeting Tuesday and their first practice of the week Wednesday. 
 
 Just when it appeared Winston had closed his vice grip on the starting job, McCarthy went out Sunday and opened some eyes with his fourth-quarter performance. He had 243 yards passing and led three scoring drives in less than 12 minutes. 
 
 "I thought he came in there and did a heck of a job given the circumstances," Harbaugh said. 
 
 Just like that, a quarterback conundrum was born, leaving Harbaugh with two realistic options to be his starting quarterback this week.   
 
 Here's a closer look at the decision: 
 
 
 

 

 

 Jameis Winston 

 
 
 Pros 
 
 
 Winston has been the quarterback ever since Jaxson Dart sustained his season-ending knee injury in the second quarter of the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . It has been an up-and-down five games for Winston, but Sunday against the Saints was his first loss in four starts. The Giants are 2-1-1 since Winston took over as the starter and are in first place in the NFC East. They aren't in a position where they need to make any panic moves, such as switching QBs. 
 
 Winston has seven touchdown passes and four interceptions in his four starts. So it's not as if the Giants have struggled to get into the end zone with him at quarterback. Only seven quarterbacks have thrown more touchdown passes than Winston during that span this season. 
 
 
 
 Winston also has done it without a consistent running game. The Giants are 22nd in the NFL, averaging just 3.8 yards per carry over the past four games. 
 
 What Winston does have in his back pocket is time on task with his top receivers: wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely . They've spent the past month getting on the same page. Nabers has three straight 100-yard games. Likely (383 receiving yards) is less than 100 yards shy of setting a new career high. It's only Week 7.  
 
 Nabers, Likely and the locker room have full confidence in Winston. They've already seen they can win games with him as the quarterback and watched him play at a relatively high level throughout his career. They know that's in him. 
 
 "We all believe in Jameis," fullback Patrick Ricard said. "Jameis puts everything into this. He's a great leader. We know what he's capable of but I guess we'll see."    
 
 
 
 
 Cons 
 
 
 The Jameis Winston experience. With Winston comes inconsistent plays and mistakes. His four interceptions are tied for fifth most since becoming the starter. His 45.6 QBR is 22nd among 30 qualifying quarterbacks. 
 
 So it's not as if Winston has played great. But he has played well enough to win games. It also should be noted that Winston's four starts were against the Titans, Cardinals, Commanders and Saints -- teams with a combined 6-17-1 record. The schedule is going to be much less forgiving from here on out, with matchups against the unbeaten 49ers, the division-leading Jaguars and Browns, and a strong Seahawks squad coming up.    
 
 If the Giants are dreaming about the potential for better quarterback play ... 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 J.J. McCarthy 
 
 
 
 Pros 
 
 
 The element of the unknown is perhaps McCarthy's most attractive trait. He has talent as a top-10 pick of the Minnesota Vikings in 2024, and who knows, there might be high-end quarterback play buried somewhere in there. 
 
 At the very least, McCarthy flashed that potential in his short stint Sunday. It was impressive. 
 
 So was McCarthy's ability to throw the ball deep downfield. He went 3-of-4 for 119 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions on passes of 20 air yards or more. Winston did not attempt any such passes against the Saints. 
 
 Harbaugh said he would judge the quarterbacks based on "performance." And it's hard to argue what McCarthy did leading the Giants on three scoring drives and close to a fourth even though it was in a helter-skelter football circumstance trying to rally in the final minutes. 
 
 McCarthy could also provide a much-needed boost to the running game. The Giants designed an offense for Dart filled with zone-reads and quarterback rollouts. That's better suited to McCarthy's game than Winston's. Harbaugh conceded that.  
 
 "The elements that we're talking about with some of the read plays and some of the different things you do moving the quarterback around," Harbaugh said, "those are definitely things that are part of the equation." 
 
 The Giants are looking for a way to jump-start their run game, and McCarthy might be it. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Cons 
 
 
 A young and relatively inexperienced quarterback like McCarthy making his first start on the road against a defense like the Texans isn't ideal. Houston's defense hasn't been great this season, but it's still third in the NFL with 18 sacks and has perhaps the league's best pass rush duo with  Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter on the edges. 
 
 McCarthy has a 41.2% completion rate and minus-9.3 completion percentage over expectation (CPOE) under pressure since the start of last season. That ranks in the bottom half of the league among qualifiers. 
 
 Winston has a much more serviceable 50.0% completion rate and minus-0.4 CPOE. That would seem to give him a better chance against the Texans. 
 
 McCarthy also has had very few reps with Nabers and Likely, having arrived three weeks ago. 
 
 "You guys saw them," McCarthy said on Sunday, referring to the fourth quarter against the Saints. 
 
 They had almost no on-field working relationship prior to this past weekend. Only a few throws on the side at practice and pregame warmups.   
 
 It makes the bye week perhaps a better spot to make the switch (if necessary) to avoid the possibility of crushing McCarthy's confidence after an already rocky introduction to the NFL with the Vikings.

title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis explained
summary: ESPN spoke with a medical professional for a better understanding of causes, treatments and outlook for those with blood clots.
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

 Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline him for at least three months, sources informed of the diagnosis told Rapoport and Schefter.

 Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his leg to his lungs.

 

 Hurts was originally diagnosed with having a superficial blood clot, according to a team statement released on Oct. 15, which was discovered following an ultrasound in London before the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars . It was deemed that mobility was important and Hurts could safely play in the game, per the statement. A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot had moved, the team said. Hurts was subsequently ruled out of Sunday's Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers and has since been put on injured reserve.

 ESPN spoke with Dr. Jordan K. Schaefer, associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan specializing in disorders of hemostasis and thrombosis, for a better understanding of causes, treatments, and outlook for those with blood clots. Dr. Schaefer has not treated Hurts and is not involved with the Eagles.

 The conversation has been edited for brevity and clarity.

 

 

 Jalen Hurts is going to have to go on anticoagulants because he has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. What should we know about that? 

 Schaefer : About one out of four people presenting with a superficial vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot that is in the veins closer to the skin of the leg, will also have a deep vein thrombosis, which is in the deeper vein system.

 When we're initially evaluating a superficial vein thrombosis, we will often do an ultrasound to look at a few things. The things that we're really looking for are, is there a deep vein thrombosis at the time that you're diagnosing the superficial vein thrombosis? What is the size of the superficial vein thrombosis, and how close is that superficial vein clot to the deep vein system? And that kind of lets us know the risk of the superficial blood clot and how to approach the initial management. We'll also be talking to patients about symptoms that could suggest a pulmonary embolism, and a pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot travels through the bloodstream and into the pulmonary arteries of the of the lung. The reason we are cautious about superficial blood clots is they can extend into the deep vein system, where they're then at higher risk for traveling to the lungs and causing a potentially serious event of a pulmonary embolism.  Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism are the feared things that can kind of go along with a superficial vein thrombosis in a small percentage of patients.

 The risk of developing a deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism depends on that individual's characteristics of the superficial clot and the characteristics of that particular individual.

 Sometimes athletes may not be as symptomatic with a pulmonary embolism because they are so fit and healthy. They're kind of often a lower risk group because of their fitness.

 What is the timeline for anticoagulant treatment typically? 

 Schaefer : The standard for patients with a deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism is at least three months of anticoagulation, and then they are reassessed to determine the long-term plan.

 Contact sports are generally avoided [for patients on anticoagulants] due to the risk of bleeding.

 Based off the statement the team initially released, the doctors decided after the discovery of the superficial blood clot in London that activity was important and also that it was safe for him to play football. Do you usually recommend activity if superficial thrombosis is the diagnosis? 

 Schaefer : A small, low-risk clot that's far from the deep vein system is often treated with warm compresses, elevation, sometimes compression stockings, and in kind of symptomatic treatment, sometimes like things like ibuprofen or nonsteroidal -- what we call nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

 If there's a higher-risk situation where we're more worried about the clot going into the deep vein system or traveling to the lungs and causing pulmonary embolism, instead of doing that conservative treatment, we would do anticoagulation treatment, which is commonly referred to as a blood thinner.

 Is movement recommended? 

 Schaefer : It used to be that bed rest would be suggested for blood clots. However, immobility or not moving around is a known risk factor for blood clots, so there's been more of a movement toward what we call early ambulation or early activity after a blood clot to kind of promote blood flow.

 There are reports that after initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, Hurts was told not to sleep as a precaution . Is avoiding sleep a necessary precaution in these cases? 

 Schaefer : Not commenting on this specific case, but recommendations to avoid sleep are not typical in the management of a superficial vein thrombosis. I can't comment on the specific case or the details surrounding that recommendation. However, a recommendation to avoid sleep is not a common recommendation for patients with superficial vein thrombosis alone. When I'm seeing a patient with superficial vein thrombosis, I typically don't make any specific recommendations regarding their sleep, I guess would be more appropriate.

 How about in terms of flying? I have heard flying can either create the blood clot or make it worse. Is that accurate? 

 Schaefer : Yes, long-distance travel is a known risk factor for blood clots.

 According to the team statement, the blood clot was initially discovered while overseas. What's typically your recommendation in terms of how to proceed with getting home? 

 Schaefer : I think that's individualized to the individual patient. That depends on the characteristics of the blood clot, the patient, and then the treatment plan.

 Is there a rhyme or reason for why a superficial blood clot turns into deep vein thrombosis? 

 Schaefer : The risk of superficial blood clot progressing to a deep vein thrombosis and/or a pulmonary embolism can vary depending on the risk factors of the individual, and especially the risk factors of the clot. So, how long the clot is and where it is anatomically, how close it is to the deep vein system. All of these superficial blood clots have some degree of risk of progressing to a deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, and that's why the follow-up is so important to monitor people over time and assess for clots that start as superficial vein thrombosis and turn into a deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism.

 Understanding there are individualized cases, what is your recommendation generally in terms of playing a sport with a superficial blood clot? 

 Schaefer : I think it depends on the individual. I think there are always risks and benefits to different choices. It's a combination of the individual patient's clotting risk, the characteristics of the blood clot, the type of sport that's being considered, and what the treatment plan is. If somebody's on an anticoagulant drug, though, there are certain sports that can't be safely performed due the bleeding risk of the sport.
